title: Analysis of AI Technology Application Types and Strategies in K-Beauty Companies
abstract: This study analyzed artificial intelligence (AI) applications in major Korean K-beauty companies, classified their functional types and application characteristics, and proposed strategic directions for industrial use. A qualitative multiple-case study was conducted on six companies—Amorepacific, LG Household & Health Care, APR, COSMAX, Kolmar Korea, and LULULAB. Sources published from January 2020 to May 27, 2026 were reviewed, and supplementary verification was conducted on August 24, 2026. Academic literature, government and public-sector reports, corporate technical materials, and independent media/industry sources were triangulated. Cases were coded using five predefined functional criteria and then examined through within-case, cross-case, SWOT, and TOWS analyses. Five AI types were identified: diagnosis/analysis, recommendation/personalization, generation/simulation, prediction/discovery, and process optimization/automation. The cross-case analysis showed that brand companies focused on consumer experience and R&D, ODM companies on discovery and manufacturing efficiency, and beauty-tech/device companies on data-linked personalized services. The TOWS analysis suggested four strategic directions: expansion of hyper-personalized offerings in global markets, differentiation through evidence-based customer experience, shared AI/data infrastructure and workforce development, and stronger data governance, ethics, quality, and standardization. The findings indicate that AI in K-beauty is evolving from a consumer-facing tool into a strategic resource connecting R&D, manufacturing, and personalized services.

title: Efficient Exploration-Enabled Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Multi-UAV Cooperative Target Search
abstract: Multi-UAV Cooperative Target Search (MCTS) is a critical task in low-altitude sensing applications, requiring agents to efficiently explore unknown environments under complex constraints. However, traditional search methods are mostly unscalable and perform poorly in dynamic multi-UAV environments. As a promising alternative, Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged to overcome these limitations by enabling agents to learn adaptive policies directly from environmental interactions. A key limitation is that current RL methods lack efficient exploration, which is a critical bottleneck preventing UAVs from finding more targets. To address this limitation, we propose a novel method named AEQMIX, which integrates trajectory entropy maximization into QMIX, an advanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) method, to encourage efficient exploration. We formulate the MCTS problem as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) and design a multi-objective reward function. To mitigate the intractability of density estimation in high-dimensional spaces, we employ a nonparametric particle-based entropy estimator to quantify the spatial diversity of UAV trajectories. This entropy estimate is utilized as an intrinsic reward, incentivizing agents to maximize the distance between their trajectories and those of their neighbors. Extensive simulations demonstrate that AEQMIX significantly outperforms baseline reinforcement learning and traditional optimization methods in terms of search rate, coverage efficiency, and collision avoidance. Compared with DNQMIX, AEQMIX improves the search rate and coverage rate by 9.52% and 11.54%, respectively, while reducing the average collision count by 70.59% in the (40 × 40) environment.

title: Experimental realization of optical key distribution under strong wiretap eavesdropping
abstract: We report the experimental distribution of a cryptographic key based on binary intensity-modulation/direct-detection (IM/DD) transmission of an optical signal. The implemented secret key agreement protocol ensures security against passive wiretap eavesdropping, notably in the regime when the eavesdropper has an advantage in the intercepted signal strength over the legitimate recipient. Operating at a 1 GBaud symbol rate, the experimental fiber optic testbed yielded secret key rates between 43.5 Mbps at 61.1 km and 640 kbps at 81.6 km of the effective link length, with a 9% wiretap installed at the transmitter. The protocol performance was analyzed using a theoretical model incorporating transmitter noise and non-ideal key reconciliation efficiency. The presented results validate IM/DD optical key distribution as an efficient low-complexity solution for protecting optical communication systems against the predominant physical-layer threat of wiretap eavesdropping.

title: M2LG-DG: A Multi-modal Local-Global Domain Generalization Framework for Cross-site Major Depressive Disorder Classification
abstract: Classification models based on resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) often show lower performance at imaging sites not included during model development, which can limit their use in clinical settings. Domain generalization (DG) addresses this issue by learning representations from source sites that remain effective for unseen target sites. However, existing DG approaches for psychiatric disorder classification commonly rely on a single imaging modality and may not fully account for site-specific acquisition effects on the learned representation space. Subjects scanned at the same site share scanner hardware, acquisition settings, and preprocessing characteristics, which can cause representations to reflect acquisition conditions rather than diagnostic information. In this work, we present M2LG-DG, a source-only multimodal local-global framework for cross-site major depressive disorder (MDD) classification. The framework employs a dual-stream rs-fMRI encoder, where the global pathway models inter-regional dependencies through self-attention and the local pathway performs graph-constrained aggregation over functional connectivity-derived brain graphs. Imaging and non-imaging representations are decomposed into shared and private components and integrated through bidirectional cross-attention with a learned modality gate. A cross-site supervised contrastive objective forms positive pairs from same-class subjects acquired at different source sites, encouraging the fused representation to preserve diagnostic information across acquisition domains. On four held-out REST-meta-MDD sites, M2LG-DG achieves an AUC of 69.48% and exceeds the closest comparison method by 2.18 percentage points. Experiments on the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) dataset further support its applicability to other psychiatric neuroimaging classification tasks.

title: MR-JEPA: A General Purpose Video Foundation Model for Cardiac MRI
abstract: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) produces rich sequential data such as temporal cine videos and spatial LGE/mapping stacks, yet most deep learning approaches process individual 2D slices, discarding this context. We present MR-JEPA, a self-supervised video foundation model for CMR that extends LeJEPA to 3D spatiotemporal inputs through tubelet tokenization, spatiotemporal masking augmentation, and initialization from a 2D CMR foundation model. Unlike prior CMR video models limited to cine data, MR-JEPA is pretrained on multi-sequence data (cine, LGE, mapping) from 10,505 patients across two centers without annotations. We evaluate the frozen encoder on six downstream tasks using a unified multi-view gated attention architecture: LV ejection fraction, RV ejection fraction, three myocardial strains (GLS, GCS, GRS), and four-class disease detection. MR-JEPA outperforms other compared methods on all five regression tasks, including both a domain-specific CMR model pretrained on more data with text supervision and a natural-video foundation model, achieving an LV EF MAE of 4.79% (r =0.764) and a GLS MAE of 1.87 (r=0.805), with 21-27% MAE reductions over baselines on strain tasks. For disease detection, MR-JEPA achieved a macro AUG of 0.868, remaining competitive with the domain-specific baseline despite using a fully self-supervised pretraining objective. These results demonstrate the potential of a unified video encoder for robust, multi-view utilization of diverse CMR sequences in clinical cardiac quantification and diagnosis.

title: RailGen: Improving Railway Intrusion Detection via Agent-Guided Small-Scale Foreign Object Generation
abstract: Small-object detection under long-tailed data distributions is a fundamental yet challenging problem in multimedia. Railway Foreign Object Detection (RFOD) epitomizes this challenge with easily confused small intrusions and scarce samples. To address these issues, we propose a generative-augmented detection paradigm that leverages multimodal image generation to enrich the feature space of rare and small objects. We first construct RailGen, a multimodal image generation agent based on large models. Under semantic constraints, RailGen automatically invokes tools to generate railway scenes, calibrate intrusion positions, extract foreign objects, and fuse them into realistic intrusion effects. This process produces high-quality synthetic samples that effectively densify the feature representations of tail classes and complete the small-object feature space. Within this paradigm, we further propose FocalDEIM, a detection framework designed to enhance training with generated data. FocalDEIM improves dense matching with Focal Modulation for better small-object discrimination and adopts Focal Loss to emphasize hard samples, thereby alleviating blurred inter-class boundaries in complex railway scenes. Experimental results demonstrate that RailGen can generate high-quality small-scale foreign objects, reducing the object pixel area by up to 58x and 13.85x on average. Equipped with these challenging samples, our paradigm surpasses the baseline DEIM by 5.6% and 7.5% in mAP@50 and mAP@(50-95), respectively, and outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies verify RailGen's feature-space enrichment and FocalDEIM's boundary discrimination. The paradigm provides an effective multimodal generative solution for long-tailed small-object detection in safety-critical applications.

title: Adjacent-Sentence Semantic Similarity as a Measure of L2 Korean Reading Text Difficulty
abstract: 연구 목적: 본 연구의 목적은 Sentence-BERT(S-BERT)를 활용하여 L2 한국어 읽기 텍스트의 인접 문장 의미 유사도를 분석하고, 이를 텍스트 난이도 측정 지표로 활용할 수 있는지를 검토하는 데 있다.연구 방법: 『새연세한국어』에 수록된 초급 51편, 중급 40편, 고급 38편 등 총 129편의 읽기 텍스트를 대상으로 Kiwi를 이용하여 문장을 분리한 후 Sentence-BERT를 활용하여 문장 임베딩을 생성하고, 인접 문장 간 코사인 유사도를 산출하였다. 또한 Kruskal-Wallis 검정, Spearman 순위상관분석 및 평균 문장 길이를 고려한 다중회귀분석을 실시하였다.연구 내용: 첫째, 수준별 인접 문장 의미 유사도는 초급에서 고급으로 갈수록 증가하는 경향을 보였으나, 그 차이는 통계적으로 유의하지 않았다(H=2.709, p=.258). 둘째, 평균 문장 길이는 인접 문장 의미 유사도와 유의한 정적 상관을 보였으며(ρ=.362, p<.001), 평균 문장 길이를 함께 고려한 회귀분석에서는 초급과 중급(B=-0.0557, p=.023), 초급과 고급(B=-0.0587, p=.022) 간에 유의한 차이가 확인되었다. 또한 평균 문장 길이를 고려하기 전과 후에 수준별 인접 문장 의미 유사도의 양상이 반대로 나타났다.결론 및 제언: 인접 문장 의미 유사도는 기존의 형식적 이독성 자질을 보완하는 L2 한국어읽기 텍스트 난이도 측정 지표로 활용될 가능성이 있음을 확인하였다. 또한 텍스트 난이도를 분석할 때에는 개별 자질의 절대적 수치뿐 아니라 평균 문장 길이와 같은 관련 언어적 요인을 함께 고려할 필요가 있음을 확인하였다. 향후 연구에서는 다양한 한국어 교재와 실제 학습 자료를 대상으로 분석 범위를 확대하고, 문단 수준의 의미 응집성 등 다양한 의미기반 지표를 함께 활용하여 텍스트 난이도 측정 모형을 고도화할 필요가 있다.

title: Lee's Law: A Tripartite Model of AI Capability Doubling in the Post-Moore Era
abstract: This paper proposes Lee's Law, a tripartite framework asserting that artificial intelligence capability doubles approximately every six months across three concurrent axes: task scale, task duration, and operational sustainability. [Derived: Synthesis of empirical doubling intervals reported by METR (7 months for 2019–2025; 4.3 months for 2023–2025; 3 months for 2024–2025), Epoch AI (2.4 months for context windows), and METR/SWE-bench (70 days). Six months is selected as the median-weighted central tendency. Assumption: These heterogeneous metrics converge on a single underlying capability growth curve.] Unlike Moore's Law, which tracks a single physical variable (transistor count), Lee's Law tracks a composite variable: the complexity of human labor that AI systems can autonomously displace. [Derived: Analogical inference from Moore's Law definition to the "task horizon" metric introduced by METR.] I derive strategic implications for enterprise AI architecture, dynamic pricing, and workforce planning, while explicitly bounding the law's applicability against risks of benchmark saturation, cost divergence, and reliability gaps. [Derived: Logical extension of the tripartite framework into operational domains.]

Six months is selected as the median-weighted central tendency. Assumption: These heterogeneous metrics converge on a single underlying capability growth curve.] Unlike Moore's Law, which tracks a single physical variable (transistor count), Lee's Law tracks a composite variable: the complexity of human labor that AI systems can autonomously displace. [Derived: Analogical inference from Moore's Law definition to the "task horizon" metric introduced by METR.] I derive strategic implications for enterprise AI architecture, dynamic pricing, and workforce planning, while explicitly bounding the law's applicability against risks of benchmark saturation, cost divergence, and reliability gaps. [Derived: Logical extension of the tripartite framework into operational domains.]

title: 基于自适应拓扑的神经元网络架构
abstract: This paper presents a novel neural network architecture, termed "Adaptive Topology Neural Network" (ATN), that leverages the principles of self-adaptive topology to dynamically adjust neuron network internal structure. The core innovation lies in the automatic generation and optimization of the network's topology, leading to improved model generalization capabilities. We introduce a novel method for constructing and refining the topology, incorporating a feedback loop that continuously assesses and corrects the network's structure based on performance data. This adaptive process reduces the reliance on manual parameter tuning, offering a robust and scalable solution for training complex neural networks. The proposed architecture demonstrates significant improvements in performance across various benchmark datasets, showcasing the potential for automated network design and enhanced model robustness.

title: Probability Logic and the Intrinsic Time Dimension of Computation
abstract: This paper explores the integration of probability logic into computational modeling, proposing a novel "time logic" framework to enable probabilistic models to automatically recognize and leverage time series data, and facilitate dynamic forecasting. We detail the design of a probabilistic model centered on this time logic, emphasizing its ability to generate updated probability distributions and implement time-series analysis. The core mechanism involves introducing time dependencies within the model's probability distribution, which allows for automatic updates and effective time-series analysis. This work contributes to the advancement of probabilistic modeling by extending its capabilities to incorporate temporal dynamics.

title: High-Dimensional Non-Linear Matrix Quantum Computing Verification and Geometric Deformation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum computing to validate the quantum properties of matrix operations, leveraging geometric deformation techniques. We propose a novel framework for quantum computation verification that integrates quantum mechanics with geometric transformations, aiming to uncover subtle quantum behaviors not readily apparent through traditional methods. The core mechanism involves constructing quantum algorithms that exploit these geometric distortions to test the integrity of matrix operations. The paper introduces a preliminary quantum algorithm demonstrating the capability of this approach and discusses its potential impact on the field of quantum verification.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Non-Linear Machine Learning Model
abstract: This paper investigates the development of a dynamic adaptive non-linear machine learning model designed to enhance model generalization. Traditional machine learning models often remain static, failing to adequately adapt to evolving data patterns. We propose a novel architecture that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on incoming data, allowing for continuous learning and improved performance. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that iteratively refines the model's parameters to minimize prediction error and maximize accuracy. This paper details the model's architecture, training process, and experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in a range of machine learning tasks. The primary goal is to provide a robust and adaptable framework for machine learning, capable of handling complex datasets and evolving environments.

title: Graph Representation Learning for Multi-Modal Data Fusion
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Graph Representation Learning (GRL) to the problem of multi-modal data fusion. Traditional approaches to multi-modal fusion frequently operate on individual modalities in isolation, failing to leverage the potentially rich and complex relationships that exist between them. We propose a novel framework that utilizes GRL techniques, specifically Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), to represent multi-modal data as a graph structure. In this framework, data instances are represented as nodes, and edges are constructed to reflect relationships between modalities. By learning latent embeddings within this graph structure, we can effectively capture and exploit inter-modal dependencies, ultimately improving the accuracy and robustness of data fusion tasks. The core contribution of this work lies in its ability to uncover hidden correlations across modalities, a capability often missed by conventional methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and outline a practical implementation strategy. The key performance indicators (KPIs) for evaluating this approach will be measured through reduced dimensionality and improved prediction accuracy.

title: Quantum Memory Based on Quantum State Decoherence
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum state decoherence as a fundamental mechanism for constructing a high-density and high-fidelity quantum memory. The core concept relies on exploiting quantum bit (qubit) interactions to store and retrieve quantum states, coupled with the inherent properties of decoherence to maintain coherence for extended periods. We propose a framework leveraging controlled interactions between qubits to encode quantum information, followed by a carefully designed decoherence process to effectively 'lock' the state. The key challenge addressed is minimizing information loss during both storage and retrieval. The theoretical analysis focuses on the trade-offs between coherence time, storage capacity, and fidelity, providing a basis for future research and development in this critical area of quantum information processing. We present a simplified model to illustrate the principles involved and discuss potential avenues for improvement, highlighting the importance of precise control and mitigation strategies to combat decoherence effects. ---

title: Self-Adaptive Spin State Entanglement for Enhanced Quantum Computation
abstract: Quantum computation offers unprecedented computational power, but maintaining and manipulating entangled states remains a significant challenge. This paper investigates a novel approach to enhance quantum computation through the implementation of self-adaptive spin state entanglement. We propose a mechanism that dynamically adjusts the entanglement strength, optimizing the system for improved performance and efficiency. The core of this approach lies in the concept of self-calibration, enabling the system to maintain a desired entanglement level without requiring explicit control. This results in a more robust and adaptable entanglement, potentially unlocking new capabilities within quantum algorithms. The study involves a detailed analysis of the impact of this self-calibration on various quantum processing tasks, demonstrating significant efficiency gains. This work represents a fundamental shift in how we approach entanglement management, paving the way for more sophisticated and practical quantum systems.

title: Title: Algorithmic Semantic Coherence via Hierarchical Contextual Graph Embedding
abstract: This paper investigates the challenges of automatically generating coherent semantic representations – particularly knowledge graphs – and proposes a novel algorithmic approach, "Algorithmic Semantic Coherence via Hierarchical Contextual Graph Embedding," that addresses these challenges. Traditional methods often rely on shallow word embeddings, failing to capture the intricate relationships necessary for true semantic understanding. This research introduces a new framework centered around a hierarchical graph structure, leveraging a self-learning embedding technique to dynamically refine the graph, ultimately aiming for enhanced semantic coherence. The core claim is that this approach significantly improves the generation of rich, contextually-aware representations compared to existing methods. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, explains the self-learning embedding process, and provides a preliminary analysis of its performance. The research emphasizes the importance of hierarchical modeling in achieving robust semantic coherence.

title: Quantum Topology Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of mathematics, offers a unique approach to manipulating and controlling quantum systems. This paper introduces an Adaptive Algorithm based on Quantum Topology, designed to automatically optimize quantum system parameters through the exploitation of quantum topology's inherent structural constraints. The algorithm leverages the concept of "topology" – a mathematical structure that preserves distances and shapes – to iteratively refine quantum states, leading to more precise control and enhanced system performance. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, highlighting its potential to revolutionize quantum control methodologies.

title: Graph-Based Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph-based reinforcement learning (GRL) that incorporates intrinsic motivation to enhance exploration. Traditional GRL algorithms often rely solely on extrinsic rewards, leading to premature convergence to locally optimal solutions. To address this limitation, we propose a framework where agents are driven by internal rewards derived from information gain and uncertainty reduction within the graph environment. The core of our method lies in an "Intrinsic Reward Module" which dynamically adjusts the reward signal based on the agent's knowledge of the graph's structure and potential rewards. We demonstrate that this intrinsic motivation significantly improves the agent's ability to explore diverse regions of the graph, ultimately leading to better long-term performance. The key innovation lies in the strategic combination of extrinsic and intrinsic rewards, creating a more robust and adaptive learning process. We formally define the GRL framework, detail the Intrinsic Reward Module, and outline the theoretical underpinnings of the approach.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Programming for Complex Algorithms
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Programming (QECP) presents a paradigm shift in tackling complex algorithms by integrating quantum superposition and entanglement into the core constraint satisfaction process. This paper introduces a novel framework, the 'Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Solver', designed to significantly improve the efficiency and robustness of solving challenging problems. We explore how leveraging quantum mechanics allows the solver to efficiently explore solution spaces, reducing computational complexity and enhancing the solution's resilience to noise and ambiguity. We detail the design of the quantum enhancement strategy and its impact on key performance metrics, showcasing its potential to overcome limitations of traditional constraint programming methods.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Task Decomposition
abstract: This paper proposes a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework designed to address the limitations of existing approaches that primarily concentrate on individual agent training, often overlooking the vital role of coordination and collaboration within a multi-agent system. The core concept revolves around enabling agents to autonomously learn and execute a process of task decomposition, effectively breaking down complex objectives into manageable subtasks, and subsequently assigning these subtasks to other agents based on their respective capabilities. This approach introduces a mechanism for distributed problem-solving, promoting synergy and efficiency. The algorithm is formulated around a reward structure that incentivizes not only successful task completion but also effective task assignment and collaboration. We present a theoretical analysis of the proposed system, outlining the key components and their interactions. The system is evaluated through a series of simulations demonstrating its ability to outperform traditional MARL methods in complex collaborative scenarios. We highlight the advantages of this approach in scenarios where tasks are inherently complex and require diverse skills and coordinated efforts.

title: 基于动态几何结构的自适应量子态演化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for quantum state evolution based on dynamically structured geometry. Traditional approaches often require pre-defined quantum states, limiting their applicability to dynamic systems. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts the quantum state evolution based on local data characteristics, enabling precise calculation and modeling of quantum states. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through illustrative examples and analyze its potential for accelerating quantum computation and analysis. This work establishes a new paradigm for quantum state evolution, offering improved efficiency and flexibility compared to conventional methods.

title: Quantum Machine Learning Model Building
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for adaptive model construction leveraging quantum machine learning algorithms. Traditional model building processes rely heavily on human design, limiting efficiency and potentially hindering the discovery of optimal models. Our proposed framework automates the model construction process, incorporating data feature analysis to iteratively refine the model's parameters and ultimately achieve superior performance. We present a foundational algorithm demonstrating the potential for significant efficiency gains and improved model quality in various machine learning tasks. The core mechanism centers around a quantum optimization loop that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on observed data characteristics, fostering a more adaptive and robust approach. We explore the theoretical implications and preliminary experimental results showcasing the framework's capabilities.

title: Biak Spotted Cuscus Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Biak Spotted Cuscus Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BSIMA), motivated by the unique foraging behavior of the Biak Spotted Cuscus (Spilopithecus biak) – a unique marsupial endemic to Sulawesi, Indonesia. The algorithm draws inspiration from the animal's adaptive strategy of selecting food patches based on a combination of exploration and exploitation. BSIMA utilizes a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework incorporating a dynamic patch selection mechanism and a novel adaptation strategy based on the cuscus's visual acuity and spatial memory. The algorithm's core components include a patch evaluation function, a dynamic patch selection probability, and an adaptive inertia weight adjustment scheme. The algorithm is designed to effectively navigate complex, multi-dimensional optimization landscapes. The performance of BSIMA is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO and Differential Evolution. The results indicate that BSIMA exhibits robust performance and adaptability across a range of problem types. The algorithm's design and performance characteristics are thoroughly discussed, providing insights into its potential applications in various fields requiring efficient optimization solutions.

title: Quantum Probability Dynamics Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum probability dynamics algorithm designed for optimizing complex systems and enhancing system stability. Traditional probabilistic models often struggle with dynamically adapting to complex systems, and this algorithm addresses this limitation through the incorporation of dynamic adjustment mechanisms within the system's behavior. We introduce a quantum-enhanced approach to system state manipulation, aiming to achieve superior stability and performance compared to existing methods. The core mechanism relies on harnessing quantum superposition and entanglement to facilitate iterative state optimization. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this algorithm through simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing its potential for advanced optimization tasks.

abstract: Quantum Bayesian Network Optimization (QBNO) presents a novel approach to optimization problems, leveraging the power of Bayesian networks to dynamically adjust decision-making processes in the presence of uncertainty and feedback. This paper introduces a new architecture designed to enhance the robustness and adaptability of Bayesian networks, allowing them to continuously refine their parameters based on evolving system data. The core mechanism involves a dynamically updated Bayesian network that incorporates real-time uncertainty and feedback, leading to improved performance across a range of complex decision-making scenarios. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing its potential to surpass existing optimization techniques.

title: Title: Bio-Inspired Quantum Error Correction (BIEQC)
abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical component of quantum computing, enabling the reliable operation of complex quantum algorithms. Current error correction schemes, however, are often cumbersome and require substantial overhead. This paper explores a novel quantum error correction scheme inspired by the self-correcting mechanisms of biological proteins, specifically focusing on dynamic adaptation of error correction factors based on environmental noise. We propose a 'quantum feedback loop' that mimics protein folding/repair, dynamically adjusting the error correction matrix to mitigate noise and improve robustness. The core claim centers on creating a quantum error correction scheme that is more adaptable, robust, and potentially more efficient than existing methods, leveraging biological inspiration for a fundamentally new approach. This research contributes to the development of a biologically-inspired quantum error correction paradigm, with the potential to significantly advance the field of quantum computing.

title: Dynamic Topology-Dependent Quantum Computing Compilation
abstract: Quantum computing relies heavily on efficient compilation techniques to translate high-level quantum algorithms into low-level gate sequences suitable for specific quantum hardware. Traditional quantum compilation methods often rely on fixed, pre-defined topologies, which can be inefficient and inflexible when dealing with the inherent physical constraints and algorithmic variations present in real quantum devices. This work introduces a novel approach to quantum compilation that dynamically adapts the topology of quantum circuits based on reinforcement learning. We propose a "topology optimizer" that learns to optimize circuit topologies in real-time, considering factors such as quantum decoherence, quantum error correction, and resource limitations. The core mechanism involves iteratively adjusting the circuit's topology to minimize resource usage and error propagation. This dynamic approach promises to significantly improve the performance and practicality of quantum computing by aligning compilation strategies with the nuances of quantum hardware. title: 基于形式语义的程序合成
abstract: This paper explores the formal semantic-based program synthesis approach, aiming to automate the creation of programs that precisely meet specified requirements. The core idea revolves around leveraging formal semantic models to guide and refine the program synthesis process, resulting in higher accuracy and efficiency. Traditional program synthesis methods often struggle with ambiguity in requirements, leading to generated programs that do not fully satisfy the intended functionality. This research proposes a novel methodology where formal semantics provide a precise and unambiguous representation of the desired program behavior, acting as a bridge between the abstract requirement and the concrete code. We introduce a framework that utilizes these formal semantics to iteratively refine the synthesis process, reducing the likelihood of errors and improving the overall quality of the synthesized program. The key innovation lies in the integration of formal verification techniques within the synthesis loop, ensuring that the generated code adheres to the specified semantics. The presented approach offers a promising pathway toward more reliable and efficient program synthesis, particularly in domains where rigorous verification is crucial.

title: Quantum Computation Complexity Theory Based on Quantum Information Entropy
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum information entropy to the theory of computational complexity. We posit that quantum information entropy can serve as a novel metric for quantifying the complexity of quantum algorithms and their associated resource requirements. The core argument is that traditional measures of computational complexity, such as circuit depth or quantum gate count, often fail to fully capture the inherent challenges posed by quantum systems. By leveraging entropy, we aim to provide a more nuanced and potentially more accurate assessment of the difficulty of quantum computations. This work introduces a framework for analyzing quantum algorithms through the lens of information entropy, exploring relationships between algorithmic complexity, entropy generation, and the resources needed to execute these algorithms. Specifically, we examine how entropy can be used to characterize the 'quantumness' of an algorithm and its impact on the overall computational cost. The ultimate goal is to develop a more robust and predictive model for quantum computation, leading to improved algorithm design and resource allocation. ---

title: Title: Zero-Knowledge Cryptographic Verification via Entangled State Propagation
abstract: Zero-Knowledge Cryptographic Verification (ZK) represents a significant advancement in secure communication, allowing a prover to demonstrate knowledge without revealing the underlying information. This paper explores a novel approach to ZK verification leveraging the principles of entangled state propagation. We propose a protocol that utilizes entanglement to establish a shared, verifiable state, and employs a quantum-enhanced algorithm to guarantee the state's consistency. This eliminates the need for direct data exchange, offering enhanced security and efficiency compared to traditional cryptographic methods. The core mechanism centers around the creation and manipulation of entangled states, which are then used to build a verifiable proof. This paper provides a detailed theoretical analysis and preliminary implementation of this protocol, demonstrating its potential for secure and efficient verification.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Adaptive Learning Mechanisms
abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, including data analysis, pattern recognition, and optimization. However, training complex quantum models often necessitates extensive fine-tuning of parameters, a process that can be computationally expensive and time-consuming. This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning algorithm, termed "Adaptive Quantum Learning," designed to address this challenge by incorporating a dynamic self-tuning learning mechanism. The core of this approach lies in dynamically adjusting the learning parameters based on subtle variations within the input data, thereby enhancing the model's generalization capabilities. This work explores the potential of this adaptive learning strategy, demonstrating its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation on a simplified quantum simulation. We present a framework for implementing this mechanism and analyze its impact on model performance, highlighting its advantages over traditional approaches.

title: Dynamic Topology Neural Network
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to modeling and predicting complex nonlinear systems utilizing Dynamic Topology Neural Networks (DTNNs). The core concept revolves around creating a neural network where the synaptic connections and the underlying topology are not fixed but dynamically adjusted in real-time. This adaptation is driven by machine learning algorithms, specifically reinforcement learning and evolutionary algorithms, allowing the DTNN to learn and optimize its structure based on incoming data. The key innovation lies in the network's ability to self-adapt, eliminating the need for pre-defined network architectures. We demonstrate the potential of DTNNs through a theoretical framework, outlining the mathematical formulation and the adaptive mechanisms. The network learns to represent the system's dynamics by continuously modifying its topology and connection strengths, leading to improved accuracy and efficiency in pattern recognition and prediction tasks. The presented framework offers a promising direction for tackling complex systems where the underlying dynamics are unknown or highly variable.

title: ## The Andean Mountain Cat Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (AMCI-MOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Andean Mountain Cat Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (AMCI-MOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to mimic the adaptive foraging strategies observed in *Otocolobus pricei* (Andean Mountain Cat). The algorithm leverages the cat's ability to dynamically adjust its search area, prioritize promising locations, and utilize a hierarchical exploration-exploitation balance – characteristics vital for navigating complex, multi-dimensional search spaces. AMCI-MOA incorporates three core principles: a 'territory' concept representing potential solutions, a 'scent trail' mechanism for prioritizing promising areas, and a 'hunting pattern' based on adaptive step sizes and exploration angles, inspired by the cat's hunting behavior. The algorithm's parameters – territory size, scent trail strength, hunting pattern parameters (step size, angle deviation, and frequency) – are dynamically adjusted based on the convergence rate and the quality of the best solution found. This approach aims to provide a robust and efficient method for tackling optimization problems with high dimensionality and intricate landscapes.

title: Absolute-Address Partial Residency
abstract: Caches, memoization, and lookup tables reuse previously computed information when that informationremains valid and the corresponding object can be identified again. This principle itself is not new and is notclaimed as a contribution of this record.This record refers to the proposed structure as Absolute-Address Partial Residency (AAPR). AAPR askswhether the same principle can be applied to execution relations in a trained dense Transformer. Aftertraining, the model weights, architecture, and the learned function mapping an internal state to the next stateremain fixed during inference, while actual activations remain input-dependent. The invariance of the trainedmodel therefore does not by itself imply that execution paths can be reused. An additional condition must betested: can some input-dependent execution relations be observed once, recorded, and reused later?To test this, post-hoc identifiers were assigned to all target channels of a trained dense Transformer.Activation histories were recorded while passing multiple inputs through the unmodified model, and a statictransition mapping keyed by previous activation addresses was constructed. In an NF4 4-bit Gemma 3 4Benvironment, closed-task validation using 80 of 2,560 MLP down_proj output channels per layer reproducedthe same top-1 result as an oracle that referenced the actual residual at every hop, across two seeds andtwelve hops for several task categories. A fact_geo failure caused by insufficient calibration coveragerecovered after adding fact-type examples and rebuilding only the transition map.A path that physically computed only the selected rows matched a path that performed full computation andthen retained the same rows by masking. Validation answers were also preserved after portions of the originalL1-12 down_proj weights were physically released from VRAM.

title: ## Antarctic Minke Whale-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Antarctic Minke Whale Optimization Algorithm" (AMWOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Antarctic Minke whales (Balaenoptera bonaerensis). Minke whales utilize a sophisticated strategy for locating food patches, involving bubble-net feeding and exploratory movements. This paper details the algorithm's design, focusing on mimicking the key aspects of whale behavior – bubble-net formation, exploration, and exploitation – within a computational framework. The algorithm leverages a population-based approach, employing a virtual "whale" representation, and utilizes a novel fitness evaluation function based on the distance to food patches and the energy expenditure associated with movement. The performance of AMWOA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The algorithm's design incorporates parameters directly inspired by observed whale behavior, such as bubble diameter, bubble number, and the exploration probability. Finally, the paper discusses future research directions, including incorporating more complex whale behaviors and exploring the algorithm's applicability to diverse optimization challenges.

title: Title: Quantum-Driven Evolutionary Computation for Constraint Satisfaction
abstract: Quantum-driven evolutionary computation offers a promising approach to solving complex constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) by leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum annealing. This paper explores the integration of quantum annealing with evolutionary computation to achieve significantly faster and more efficient search for optimal solutions. We detail the design of a hybrid algorithm that combines the strengths of both paradigms, focusing on the generation of candidate solutions, refinement through evolutionary operators, and the efficient exploration of the solution space. The core mechanism centers around quantum annealing's ability to efficiently address high-dimensional search spaces, coupled with the evolutionary algorithm's capacity to explore diverse solutions and adapt to changing problem landscapes. This research investigates the effectiveness of this hybrid approach in tackling challenging CSPs, aiming to surpass the limitations of traditional classical methods.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Embeddings for Semantic Data
abstract: This paper introduces a new approach to semantic data embedding, leveraging geometric principles to construct representations that explicitly encode structural relationships. Traditional embedding methods often fail to capture the inherent geometric properties of data, leading to reduced interpretability. Our method focuses on representing semantic relationships as shapes and connections, creating embeddings that are inherently more robust to noise and allow for a deeper understanding of data structure. This is a significant advancement in machine learning, offering a pathway toward more reliable and insightful data interpretation. The core mechanism involves the explicit construction of geometric representations, designed to enhance the robustness of embedding models.

title: Quantum State Dynamic Topology Transformation
abstract: Quantum State Dynamic Topology Transformation is a novel algorithm that leverages the inherent dynamic properties of quantum states to perform complex computations. This approach employs a novel dynamic topology transformation strategy, dynamically adjusting the quantum state to achieve enhanced computational capabilities. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around exploiting the self-organizing nature of quantum states, enabling adaptation to diverse input data sets. This paper presents the development of a robust and efficient algorithm for this transformation, showcasing its potential for advanced computational modeling and simulation. We detail the algorithm's architecture, operational principles, and preliminary results demonstrating its efficacy. The core claim underscores the algorithm's capability to dynamically reshape quantum states, offering a significant advancement over traditional static topology methods.

title: ## The Aurora Falcon Metaheuristic Algorithm (AFMA) – Inspired by the Hunting Strategies of the Aurora Falcon
abstract: This paper introduces the Aurora Falcon Metaheuristic Algorithm (AFMA), a novel optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting behaviors of the Aurora Falcon (Falco ido). The Aurora Falcon, renowned for its highly efficient and adaptable hunting strategies, particularly its "sky-scanning" and "hovering-and-diving" techniques, provides a rich source of algorithmic inspiration. AFMA leverages these observed behaviors to construct a population-based search algorithm capable of navigating complex, multi-dimensional search spaces. The core mechanisms of AFMA include a dynamic territory assignment scheme mimicking the falcon's territorial defense, a novel "focusing" mechanism based on echo location, and a probabilistic decision-making process mirroring the falcon's opportunistic hunting approach. While the algorithm is presented theoretically, it demonstrates a strong potential for application in various optimization problems. The algorithm's primary focus is on achieving efficient convergence and adaptability within the search space.

title: The Green Jay-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GJMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Green Jay-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GJMOA), a novel optimization algorithm designed to mimic the foraging strategies and adaptive behaviors observed in Green Jays (Cyanocorax luxuosus). Green Jays are known for their complex problem-solving abilities, including caching food items with meticulous spatial organization and adapting to changing environmental conditions. GJMOA leverages these behavioral traits to generate a robust and efficient optimization process. The algorithm incorporates key principles such as distributed exploration, localized exploitation, and dynamic adaptation of search parameters – mirroring the Green Jay's approach to resource acquisition. The core of GJMOA resides in a 'nesting' mechanism, where potential solutions are organized into hierarchical 'nests' based on their fitness and proximity to the current best solution. This hierarchical structure facilitates efficient convergence and avoids premature convergence issues common in some traditional metaheuristics. This paper details the algorithm's design, outlining the key components and their operational principles, and presents a theoretical foundation for its effectiveness.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的量子隐形计算
abstract: Quantum cryptography offers a paradigm shift in secure communication, relying on the laws of quantum mechanics to guarantee confidentiality and integrity. However, traditional cryptographic methods are vulnerable to various attacks, particularly those exploiting the inherent complexities of quantum systems. This paper presents a novel approach to quantum cryptography, leveraging the power of adaptive topology to enhance the security of quantum computation. We propose a framework wherein quantum states are encoded into a dynamically evolving topology, thereby mitigating attacks based on known patterns and simplifying the detection of malicious manipulation. This research explores the potential of this adaptive topology to significantly bolster the robustness of quantum computations against known attacks. The core mechanism focuses on establishing and maintaining a stable and complex topological structure that is difficult to analyze, resulting in enhanced resistance to attack. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in enhancing the security of quantum algorithms.

title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Graph Databases
abstract: Learning effective representations from graph databases is a fundamental challenge in various domains, including social network analysis, knowledge graph reasoning, and recommendation systems. Traditional methods often rely on labeled data, which is expensive and time-consuming to obtain. This paper introduces a novel self-supervised learning approach specifically tailored for graph databases. Our core claim is that training graph database embeddings without labeled data is difficult. We propose a system that leverages the graph structure and node relationships to learn robust embeddings by predicting missing edges or node attributes. This process forces the model to deeply understand the underlying graph structure. The resulting embeddings can be used for downstream tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and graph clustering. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through theoretical analysis and present a detailed explanation of the mechanism.

title: The Elastic Game: A Narrative Review of Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment and Player Modeling from Malone's Challenge to Adaptive Platform Games
abstract: Dynamic difficulty adjustment---the game's attempt to measure the player and reshape the challenge---moved from Malone's theory of intrinsically motivating challenge through the AI-for-DDA workshop's proposals and the AI difficulty scaling to the data-driven player models, the behavioral modelling surveys, and the adaptive platform games whose effects the eye trackers measured. This article presents a narrative review of that arc's canonical line: Malone's 1981 intrinsic motivation, Hunicke and Chapman's 2004 AI for DDA, Spronck and colleagues' 2004 difficulty scaling, Yannakakis and Hallam's 2007 entertainment optimization, Missura and Gartner's 2009 player modelling, Pedersen, Togelius, and Yannakakis's 2010 experience modeling, Lopes and Bidarra's 2011 adaptivity survey, Shaker and colleagues' 2010 personalized content, Zook and Riedl's 2012 temporal player model, Bakkes and colleagues' 2012 behavioural modelling, Isaksen and colleagues' 2015 survival analysis, and Denisova and Cairns's 2015 adaptation effects. The review is organized around three themes: the challenge's theory, in which the intrinsic motivation's theory and the AI workshop's proposals defined the adjustment's problem; player modeling, in which the preference models, the physiological entertainment measures, and the behavioural and temporal data-driven profiles made the player measurable; and adaptive systems and evaluation, in which the personalized generation, the survival analysis's game spaces, and the adaptation's measured effects built the evidence. It is concluded that the elastic game is the challenge's feedback loop---the player's model as the difficulty's input---and that its arc is the measurement's rise from the designer's intuition to the player's data.

title: Fenocosm reproduction snapshot: the fenocosm analysis package
abstract: The fenocosm analysis package — the software snapshot that regenerates every number and figure in the Fenocosm arm of the Feno program. Contents: the fenocosm/ package (the protocol module pinning every constant and seed; the exact 2k-state Kronecker forward pass and MSM-Cox counting channel; the sparse-event competitor roster — homogeneous Poisson, a Bayesian-blocks piecewise-constant Poisson, a free-transition Poisson HMM, a periodic-windowed Poisson, a Weibull renewal; the wavelet-scattering moment vector; the IAAFT and mask-aware point-process surrogate generators; the loaders and fetch/reduction modules; and one driver module per sealed record), the x*.py top-level drivers, verify.sh and the x0_verify.py apparatus gate, the tests/ suite (data-free by construction), tools/ (including the pandoc-free paper-PDF builder), and vendor/ with its CHECKSUMS.sha256 pinning the four vendored CC BY 4.0 modules byte-for-byte. LICENSE, CITATION.cff, PROVENANCE.md, README.md, CONSTITUTION.md and FINDINGS.md travel with it. Not included: data/ (all real light curves, flare event lists and burst tables are public archival products fetched at run time and never committed — the fetch and reduction code is included) and out/ (the sealed records are deposited separately, each with its own DOI). The apparatus gate runs from this snapshot with no network and no data files. Deposit note. All seven Feno-program repositories are private and remain private, so this deposit is standalone: it carries its own reproduction materials, its metadata contains no repository link, and sibling work is referenced by DOI rather than by repository path. Related Zenodo DOIs cited below are reserved with publication pending. Part of the Feno program. The source repository is private; the reproduction materials for this record are contained in the record itself.

title: ADAPTIVE TURKISH FEDERATED RAG ARCHITECTURE FOR LOW-RESOURCE SYSTEMS
abstract: Today, Large Language Models (LLMs) perform many tasks in the field of natural language processing with high success, from text generation to translation, semantic analysis to code writing. However, these models have some fundamental limitations that make their reliable use challenging. They can produce factual errors known in the literature as hallucinations and cannot directly access developments after their training period. They also sometimes reproduce biases present in the training data. The Re-trieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach aims to produce more up-to-date and verifiable outputs by dynamically feeding the model with external information sources, thereby reducing hallucination and temporal limitations. This study examines distributed learning approaches aimed at protecting data privacy and QLoRA-based fine-tuning strategies within a mathematical framework. It also addresses 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization techniques used to improve system efficiency. Furthermore, it de-tails morphology-aware hybrid access methods and adaptive routing mechanisms that can make deci-sions based on query complexity to achieve results more suitable for Turkish. The study demonstrates that combining RAG-based systems with federated learning and homomorphic encryption creates a secure, decentralized architecture, and that LLM can be efficiently run on low-resource systems using the NF4-QLoRA combination. However, limitations such as encryption latency, erroneous information from untrusted sources, and the inadequacy of standard evaluation methods for Turkish also exist.

title: Digitizing Renewable Energy Potential in Indonesia
abstract: Indonesia is committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2060 in response to the global climate crisis caused by dependence on fossil fuels. Achieving this goal depends on having reliable baseline data, especially field-validated and accessible maps showing renewable energy potential. Currently, these maps are only available in static formats, making them difficult to use. This study updates the static maps by creating an interactive geoportal to improve data transparency and accessibility. The process includes three main steps: development, integration, and validation. During development, the wind energy map is generated using the Weather Research and Forecasting Four-Dimensional Data Assimilation (WRF FDDA) model at a 5 km horizontal resolution and interpolated to a 1 km grid using ordinary kriging. The solar energy map uses a similar method, with added land suitability analysis. The hydropower map is based on the dependable flow Q90, in accordance with SNI 8396:2019. The bioenergy map includes urban waste biomass, using Net Caloric Value (NCV) data, and biomass from crops grown on degraded land. All these maps are combined into a single, publicly accessible interactive geoportal. What makes this study unique is the integration of diverse renewable energy data sources into a single national geoportal, and the first consolidated documentation and evaluation of an operational national system of this kind, something not offered by global platforms such as the Global Wind Atlas or the Global Solar Atlas, or Indonesian studies that mostly assessed a single resource type in isolation. This geoportal provides a centralized and accessible database of Indonesia’s renewable-energy resources, improves the analytical basis for national and regional energy planning, is intended to reduce resource-risk uncertainty for investors, and supports Indonesia’s transition from target-based renewable-energy policy toward data-driven implementation.

title: SFE-DCS: Differentiated Creative Search as a Portable Compactness Enhancer for Wrapper Feature Selection on High-Dimensional Medical Data
abstract: High-dimensional medical datasets carry thousands of redundant variables, so wrapper feature selection is attractive for its task-aligned accuracy yet costly because the binary search space grows exponentially. Strong wrappers reach a good but not minimal subset and then stall, leaving residual redundancy that inflates biomarker-panel size. This study recasts Differentiated Creative Search (DCS) from a stand-alone optimizer into a portable inner mechanism that confines a heavy-tailed search to the features the host wrapper has already selected, so the cost of escaping stagnation scales with the panel, not with the full dimension. Because the mechanism reads the host through its active set alone, it attaches to structurally different hosts: the add-and-remove search of the Simple, Fast, and Efficient feature selection algorithm (SFE) and the shrink moves of Uniform-solution-driven Binary Feature Selection (UniBFS), giving SFE-DCS and UniBFS-DCS. The evidence comes from 10 public medical benchmarks with up to 24,481 features, 8 competing methods, 4 downstream classifiers, and 30 runs per cell. Both hosts become more compact once the mechanism is attached. On SFE the panel shrinks by about one third, a reduction significant across datasets, while macro-F1 rises on the support vector machine and Naive Bayes classifiers; on UniBFS, which is already compact, the further reduction is smaller. SFE-DCS lies on the non-dominated front of the size and accuracy plane for all four classifiers, at the smallest mean panel of the methods tested and at the runtime of the single-agent hosts and roughly 20 times below full-space population metaheuristics. A component ablation, a hyper-parameter sensitivity study, and an unbiased nested cross-validation delimit where the mechanism helps.

title: Hybrid quantum interferometer bridging Hong-Ou-Mandel and N00N-state interference
abstract: Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference offers robustness in high-noise environments due to its phase-insensitive nature, while N00N-state interference provides enhanced phase sensitivity for precision measurements in low-noise settings. However, their realizations have typically required separate experimental platforms. Here, we report a single hybrid quantum interferometer that can dynamically transition between HOM and N00N-state interference by adjusting two time delays, $τ_1$ and $τ_2$. This tunability enables operation in phase-insensitive, phase-sensitive, or hybrid modes within a unified setup, as confirmed by theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration. Our system offers a versatile platform with potential for quantum sensing applications, paving the way for integrated quantum technologies capable of adapting to diverse noise conditions.

title: ViCo: Visual-oriented Coding with Self-Reflection for Chart Replication
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of generating high-quality academic charts that match the visual standards of human-authored papers. While existing AI agents can produce well-structured text and code, their generated visualizations often lack the stylistic and semantic fidelity of human designs. Advanced coding agents that employ self-reflection mechanisms exhibit poor visual reasoning and limited reflection following, resulting in sparse reward signals that severely undermine their reinforcement learning (RL). We propose ViCo, a training framework for visual-oriented coding that employs iterative reflections to align generated chart images progressively with the reference. We first introduce a self-supervised warm-up stage, which augments Monte Carlo Tree Search with consistency-based pruning to synthesize high-quality reflection trajectories, ensuring that each coding step strictly follows the outcomes of prior reflections. A multi-step RL algorithm is then developed, using counterfactual baselines to estimate advantage for reflection and action steps within each refinement cycle, thereby addressing the reward sparsity. To enable efficient reward in massive training, we propose an automatic, multifaceted evaluation framework that assesses charts' style, layout, and semantic consistency via a hierarchical heterogeneous layout graph structure. Experiments on three public benchmarks demonstrate that ViCo, trained on an 8B model, achieves performance close to proprietary LLMs with adequate reflection capabilities.

title: Agentic Quantitative Trading: A Survey of Workflows, Systems, and Evaluation
abstract: Quantitative trading is moving from isolated predictive models toward agentic workflows that combine reasoning, tool use, memory, and feedback. This survey reviews agentic quantitative trading across five stages: factor mining, signal discovery, portfolio construction, order execution, and risk management. We further examine agentic quant trading systems through architecture, coordination, and adaptation, while comparing benchmarks across strategy construction, offline trading, live market evaluation, and reliability assessment. Our review finds that current systems remain concentrated on signal discovery, while complete integration with portfolio construction, execution, and risk control is still uncommon. Multi-agent systems also rely heavily on aggregation despite increasingly diverse workflow structures. Benchmark evidence further shows that strong model or forecasting capability does not reliably translate into trading performance under live market conditions and reliability controls. We conclude with future directions for more complete trading workflows, stronger coordination, and evaluation matched to the capability being assessed.

title: CoJEPA: Combining Contrastive Learning and JEPA for Global-Local Music Representations
abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) has shown strong performance in learning rich representations through self-supervised prediction in latent space. However, it typically relies on teacher--student architecture with an EMA to stabilise training, and can tend to yield uninformative representations. Contrastive learning is stable to train and produces strong global representations, but remains limited on local tasks by the global nature of its objective. In this work, we combine both into CoJEPA: a single shared backbone jointly trained with a JEPA objective on masked sequence tokens and a contrastive objective on the class token. The contrastive gradient provides stability, removing the need for an EMA teacher entirely, while JEPA enriches the sequence tokens via local predictions that contrastive learning alone cannot provide. Crucially, no extra parameters are added to the backbone: the same model is guided towards richer representations purely through the design of its training signal. CoJEPA takes the best of both worlds, outperforming or matching both individual methods across global and local MIR tasks, with a particularly strong advantage on tonal and harmonic understanding, and without any task-specific architectural changes. CoJEPA shows that combining objectives with complementary inductive biases can substitute for scale, encouraging future work to invest in smarter training objectives over ever-larger models.

title: Scalable Statistical Inference in Stochastic Gradient Descent
abstract: Constructing confidence regions for stochastic gradient descent (SGD) ideally requires estimating the asymptotic covariance matrix, a severe computational bottleneck in high dimensions. Traditional cancellation-based batch means methods bypass this estimation but require inverting a sample batch covariance matrix. This introduces strict mathematical degeneracy when the parameter dimension exceeds the number of batches. To address this problem, we utilize equal batch size batch means method and propose a simultaneous, marginal-friendly framework. The proposed marginal statistics has a asymptotic Student's $t$-distribution, and eliminates the matrix inversion step, entirely circumventing high-dimensional degeneracy. To achieve valid simultaneous coverage, we present an algorithm utilizing wild bootstrap samples drawn from a statistic as a function of only the diagonals of the variance-covariance estimator, and to further incorporate the contribution of cross-dependencies, we introduce an efficient Quasi-Monte Carlo procedure utilizing a $t$-copula approximation. Additionally, we integrate a Lugsail variance estimator to aggressively correct finite-sample bias and under-coverage. The proposed methodology delivers interpretable, simultaneous hyper-rectangular confidence regions that are statistically robust, memory-efficient, and strictly scalable for high-dimensional inference. The theoretical results are supported by extensive numerical simulation analysis through various aspects of dimension, number of batches and error structure.

title: Improving Korean Medical LLM Reasoning via Multi-stage Filtering-based Knowledge Graph Triple Injection
abstract: 지식 그래프(KG)와 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)의 결합은 의료 질의응답 성능 향상에 효과적이나, 질문과 무관한 트리플이 노이즈로 작용하여 오히려 성능을 저하시키는 문제가 존재한다. 본 연구는 이를 해결하기 위해 생의학 지식 베이스인 UMLS를 기반으로 검색된 트리플에 Semantic Similarity Filtering, Confidence Filtering, LLM Relevance Filtering 3단계 필터링 파이프라인을 적용하여 고품질 트리플만을 선별한다. 특히 트리플의 출처에 따라 쿼리를 다르게 구성하는 이중 쿼리 방식을 도입하여 선택지 엔티티와 질문 엔티티 각각에 대한 정밀한 확신도 계산을 수행한다. 정제된 트리플을 Few-shot 및 Chain-of-Thought 기법과 결합하여 LLM에 주입함으로써, 의사․간호사․약사․치과의사 4개 도메인에서 기존 모델 대비 일관된 성능 향상을 달성하였다.

title: Aspect-Based Adversarial Attack Against Opinion Analysis Models with an Educational Perspective
abstract: Analyzing students’ opinions about classes, instructors, and the overall learning environment enables institutions to understand students’ needs and propose improvements to enhance the learning process. Furthermore, analyzing opinions at aspect-level allows a detailed analysis and helps to identify the relevant aspects that require attention to enrich the students’ experience. Currently, opinion analysis systems implement deep learning models to increase precision. However, these models can be misled by strategically modified inputs, known as adversarial examples, producing incorrect classifications. In this work, we analyze adversarial examples and their behavior in aspect-level sentiment analysis models to design aspect-aware modifications. Specifically, we define a model for generating aspect-level adversarial examples that modify inputs by targeting aspect–term relationships. The proposed model reduces accuracy by 20.90%, highlighting vulnerabilities in aspect-level models, where even small and targeted changes can degrade performance, providing a foundation for the development of defense mechanisms to ensure reliable predictions.

title: Title: Geometric Representation of Information Flow in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing geometric representations to enhance the understanding and optimization of neural network information flow. Traditional approaches often rely on complex, abstract models, while this work proposes a novel approach – the 'Flow Graph' algorithm – that visualizes network data flow based on shortest paths and topological changes. The core claim is to develop a new geometric representation that offers a more efficient and grounded method for analyzing and improving neural network performance. We outline the algorithm's design, demonstrate its efficacy through illustrative examples, and discuss its implications for future research in neural network design. The analysis will focus on minimizing computational complexity and enhancing the visibility of critical information propagation patterns.

title: Non-linear Self-Organizing Chaos Systems: An Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on the principles of non-linear self-organizing chaos systems. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, which struggle to effectively capture the inherent dynamic behavior of complex systems. This work proposes a new algorithmic framework that leverages the system's self-organization to dynamically adjust key variables, thereby optimizing energy, information, and state allocation. The core mechanism involves modeling the system's dynamics as a set of "chaos variables" and employing a feedback loop to iteratively refine these variables, leading to enhanced performance. The design incorporates a novel dynamic adjustment mechanism that dynamically alters system parameters based on observed behavior, demonstrating a significant improvement in optimization efficiency compared to traditional approaches. This research contributes to the development of robust optimization techniques suitable for challenging, non-linear systems.

title: Can an Advanced AI Certify Itself? Gödelian Incompleteness, Reflective Reasoning, and Recursive Self-Modification
abstract: This research note asks whether an advanced artificial intelligence capable of representing and modifying its own reasoning can obtain final internal certification of the correctness, consistency, and safety of its reasoning basis. The question emerged from a Japanese human-AI dialogue and is evaluated here against established results in mathematical logic and formal research on reflective artificial agents. Gödel's incompleteness theorems do not directly impose a simple global limit on AI; they apply to sufficiently expressive, consistent, effectively axiomatized formal systems. However, proof-based self-modifying agents face structurally related problems of self-reference and reflective trust. Work on Gödel machines, Vingean reflection, tiling agents, reflective oracles, and logical induction shows both the difficulty of self-certification and partial methods for reasoning under reflective and logical uncertainty. The paper proposes the Reflective Non-Closure Hypothesis (RNCH) as a conceptual synthesis, not a new mathematical theorem: an advanced AI that formalizes a sufficiently expressive portion of its own reasoning and uses internal reasoning to certify consequential self-modification should not be assumed to reach a final self-contained standpoint from which all relevant properties of its current and future reasoning are certified. Stronger meta-systems, probabilistic reflection, empirical validation, and external verification may solve particular problems while relocating rather than eliminating the trust boundary. The central safety implication is that increasing intelligence does not automatically remove trust assumptions; it can make their location more consequential.

title: Dynamic Topological Dependency Learning (TDTL)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Topological Dependency Learning (TDTL), a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning that leverages reinforcement learning to dynamically construct and adapt an internal knowledge graph based on observed data and inference results. Unlike traditional methods that rely on pre-defined topologies or manual annotation, TDTL autonomously learns data dependencies through a 'topological optimization' algorithm. The system begins with a simple, undirected graph and iteratively modifies it based on prediction errors, guided by a reward signal. A 'topological regularization' mechanism is incorporated to prevent over-complexity and maintain graph connectivity. The core claim is that a system can automatically build and adjust its internal knowledge representation's topology to reflect dynamic data dependencies without pre-defined topologies or manual labels. This represents a significant departure from existing knowledge graph construction and reasoning techniques. ---

title: Quantum Random Number Generation
abstract: Quantum random number generation (QRNG) offers a fundamentally different approach to randomness compared to classical methods. This paper explores the design and principles of a QRNG based on harnessing the inherent uncertainty in quantum measurements. The core claim is the development of a system capable of generating truly random quantum bit sequences. This is achieved by exploiting the probabilistic nature of quantum measurement, specifically the collapse of the wave function upon observation, which yields unpredictable outcomes. The generated sequences are expected to exhibit statistical independence, a crucial property for various quantum computing applications. This work lays the groundwork for a detailed exploration of QRNG techniques, highlighting their potential impact on secure quantum communication and simulation. We will detail the theoretical underpinnings, focusing on the mathematical formulation of the process and the statistical properties of the generated random numbers.

title: Non-Local Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of a novel quantum computation algorithm, termed "Non-Local Quantum Computation," to facilitate the transmission of quantum information across spatial distances. Traditional quantum computing relies on local quantum mechanics, limiting the capabilities of quantum information transfer. This research introduces a new algorithm predicated on the inherent properties of quantum entanglement, aiming to overcome these limitations and enable more efficient data exchange. The core mechanism centers on leveraging entanglement to establish a bridge across space, ultimately demonstrating a significant advancement in quantum information propagation. This work presents a conceptual framework and explores the potential impact of this approach on the broader landscape of quantum computing.

title: Quantum Topology and Algorithms: A New Paradigm for Computation
abstract: Quantum topology, a relatively new field of physics, holds the potential to revolutionize computation by leveraging the unique properties of space-time geometry. This paper explores the application of quantum topology to algorithm design, specifically focusing on quantum machine learning and optimization. We introduce a novel algorithm framework based on quantum topological concepts, aiming to enhance computational efficiency and performance compared to traditional approaches. The core mechanism involves the manipulation of topological states to facilitate novel algorithmic pathways. This work provides a conceptual foundation and preliminary results demonstrating the potential of quantum topology to significantly advance computational capabilities.

title: Quantum-Driven Constraint Relaxation
abstract: Quantum-Driven Constraint Relaxation (QDCR) is a novel quantum algorithm designed to systematically reduce constraints within dynamical systems. This paper introduces a quantum annealing approach, enhanced with a novel constraint-aware optimization strategy, to achieve efficient and targeted constraint alleviation. The core mechanism centers on utilizing quantum annealing to rapidly explore the solution space, effectively minimizing the impact of constraints while simultaneously enhancing the likelihood of discovering novel solutions. We explore the potential benefits of QDCR, particularly in scenarios where traditional optimization methods struggle with complex constraints, and detail the design of the algorithm's key components. The research highlights the theoretical advantages and potential practical applications of this approach, aiming to significantly advance the field of constrained optimization.

title: Active Learning for Robot Motion Control
abstract: This paper investigates the application of active learning techniques to robot motion control. Traditional robot motion control relies heavily on pre-programmed models and extensive trial-and-error experimentation. This approach can be inefficient, particularly in dynamic and uncertain environments. We propose a framework where a robot utilizes active learning to autonomously acquire new motion skills by interacting with its environment. The core concept involves the robot collecting data through interaction, and then employing an active learning algorithm to refine its control policy. This allows the robot to adapt to unforeseen circumstances and improve both the precision and efficiency of its movements. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of active learning and robot motion control, facilitating truly autonomous learning capabilities. The theoretical framework presented here outlines the methodology and provides a foundation for future research in adaptive robotic systems. ---
