title: Based on Extensible Logic Programming for Complex System Modeling
abstract: This paper explores the application of extensible logic programming to the modeling and reasoning about complex systems. Traditional approaches to modeling complex systems often struggle with scalability, maintainability, and the ability to incorporate new knowledge effectively. We propose a framework utilizing extensible logic programming, where system knowledge is represented as logical rules, enabling automated inference and decision-making. The core of this approach lies in the extensibility of the logic programming paradigm, allowing for dynamic adaptation to evolving system requirements and the seamless integration of new information. This work demonstrates the potential of this methodology for tackling complex system modeling challenges, offering a more flexible and robust solution compared to conventional methods. We present a conceptual model and discuss key considerations for implementing such a system, focusing on rule representation, inference engine design, and scalability strategies. ---

title: Self-referential memory tensor
abstract: We present a technical architecture for persistent identity in AI sys- tems, based on the Self-Referential Memory Tensor (SRMT). The archi- tecture integrates transformer encoders, differentiable memory, persistent embeddings, and long-context attention to enable temporal continuity, self-recognition, narrative integration, and autonomous coherence. We show that the SRMT is not speculative but immediately feasible with existing technologies. The architecture is a bridge to AI qualia.

title: Black-pencilled Marmoset: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavioral Patterns of a Black-pencilled Marmoset
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Black-pencilled Marmoset (BPM), inspired by the foraging behavior of black-pencilled marmosets. These small primates exhibit a unique strategy of alternating between searching for food in different areas of their territory, exhibiting a "zigzag" pattern with pauses. BPM leverages this observed pattern to develop a new metaheuristic search strategy. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a novel "territory division" mechanism and a "pause-and-search" strategy to explore the search space effectively. We demonstrate the algorithm's performance on a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to converge towards optimal or near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of territory boundaries and the strategic implementation of pauses, mimicking the marmoset's adaptive foraging. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality (objective function value), and computational cost. The results indicate that BPM offers a competitive alternative to existing metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems exhibiting spatial or sequential dependencies.

title: Non-Euclidean Geometry in Quantum Entanglement Computation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of non-Euclidean geometry to revolutionize quantum entanglement computation. Traditional approaches often rely on simplified geometric models, which can limit the precision and efficiency of calculations. We propose a novel quantum entanglement computation framework based on the properties of non-Euclidean geometry, aiming to achieve significantly enhanced computational capabilities. The core claim is that precise modeling of non-欧几何场论's geometric properties allows for the design of a quantum entanglement computation algorithm, exceeding the limitations of conventional methods. This work explores the implications of this approach, focusing on the potential for greater accuracy and efficiency in entanglement-based quantum operations.

title: Black Flying Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Flight Dynamics of the Black Flying Squirrel
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Black Flying Squirrel" (BFS), inspired by the unique flight dynamics of the *Pteromyini* genus, commonly known as the black flying squirrel. The algorithm leverages the squirrel's remarkable ability to glide efficiently through the air, utilizing precise adjustments of its body posture and tail movements to control its trajectory and minimize energy expenditure. BFS incorporates elements of both Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms, integrating a novel 'Posture Adjustment Mechanism' (PAM) that mimics the squirrel's dynamic control. PAM adjusts the position and velocity of candidate solutions based on a dynamically calculated 'glide angle' and 'energy conservation' principle. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results indicate that BFS exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems requiring adaptive and dynamic adjustment strategies. Future work will focus on further refining the PAM and exploring its applicability to a broader range of optimization problems.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Social Network Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to social network analysis. Traditional social network analysis methods often struggle to capture complex, hidden relationships and patterns within networks, particularly in large and dynamic social structures. GNNs offer a novel approach by directly learning representations of nodes based on their network context. This work details the core concept of representing social networks as graph structures and leveraging GNNs to perform tasks such as node classification and link prediction. We demonstrate the potential of GNNs to uncover valuable insights by modeling relationships as a graph, and learning from the network topology itself. The results suggest GNNs can provide a significantly improved analytical tool for understanding social networks compared to conventional methods. ---

title: ## Bemanasy Mouse Lemur: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Microprolemotherius*
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic algorithm, the Bemanasy Mouse Lemur (BML) algorithm, designed for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the foraging behavior of *Microprolemotherius*, a small mouse lemur known for its efficient exploration and exploitation of its environment. BML combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), incorporating a novel "memory-based exploration" mechanism inspired by the lemur's spatial memory and scent marking. The algorithm utilizes a dynamic population size, adaptive inertia weight, and a memory matrix to represent the lemur's learned foraging paths. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the algorithm's convergence properties and its potential for achieving global optima. The paper outlines the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulations, and a conceptual framework. title: Bearded Emperor Tamarin Metaheuristic Algorithm (BETMA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Bearded Emperor Tamarin Metaheuristic Algorithm (BETMA), inspired by the unique grooming behavior of the Bearded Emperor Tamarin (Bolobo). The algorithm leverages the tamarin's meticulous and selective grooming strategy to effectively explore and exploit the search space in optimization problems. BETMA incorporates a novel 'territory guarding' mechanism, mimicking the tamarin's defense of its territory, and a 'selective attention' component, mirroring its focused grooming. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as solution accuracy, convergence rate, and computational efficiency. title: Information-Theoretic Grounding of Reinforcement Learning Reward Functions
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, yet a persistent challenge remains: the design of effective reward functions. Traditionally, reward functions are painstakingly crafted by human experts, often relying on heuristics and domain-specific knowledge. This approach frequently results in brittle policies – those that perform well in specific environments but fail to generalize to even slightly altered conditions. This paper proposes a novel framework for designing RL reward functions that is fundamentally grounded in information theory. We argue that reward functions should directly optimize for the reduction of prediction error and uncertainty, leveraging measures such as mutual information and entropy. Our approach offers a systematic and principled way to construct reward functions that are inherently robust, generalizable, and less reliant on hand-engineering. We demonstrate the potential of this information-theoretic grounding through a theoretical analysis and outline a methodology for translating complex real-world problems into an information-theoretic reward design process. The core claim is that by directly optimizing for information-theoretic goals, we can create more reliable and adaptable RL agents.

title: Dynamic Domain Adaptation for Deep Learning
abstract: Domain adaptation aims to bridge the gap between source and target domains where data distributions differ, enabling models trained on labeled source data to perform well on unlabeled target data. Traditional domain adaptation methods often rely on static adjustments, such as learning rate scaling, which can be suboptimal. This work introduces a dynamic domain adaptation framework that leverages reinforcement learning (RL) to intelligently adapt model parameters. The core idea is to train an RL agent to actively adjust the model's parameters based on the observed domain discrepancy, combined with a domain adaptation algorithm for parameter optimization. This approach allows the model to dynamically respond to changes in the target domain, potentially leading to improved adaptation performance compared to static methods. The framework consists of a deep neural network (DNN) as the policy network, an RL agent that interacts with the DNN to adjust parameters, and a domain adaptation algorithm that utilizes the adjusted parameters for training. The performance is evaluated using several benchmark datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Algorithmic Topology for Data Compression & Representation
abstract: This paper explores the application of algorithmic topology to data compression, moving beyond conventional entropy-based methods. We introduce a novel algorithm, "Topology-Driven Compression," which analyzes the structural relationships within data to identify and exploit these relationships for increased compression efficiency. The core concept is to construct a representation of the data based on its topological structure, allowing for more effective compression through inherent properties. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating significant compression ratios compared to existing methods, focusing on lossless compression scenarios. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential impact of this approach on various data types and future research directions.

title: 基于自适应的概率空间优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic space optimization algorithm based on adaptive parameter adjustment. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, non-linear systems, requiring extensive parameter tuning. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts the probability space parameters to enhance optimization results' reliability and efficiency. We propose a framework that employs a self-tuning mechanism to automatically adapt to the system's characteristics, leading to improved performance across various optimization tasks. This work addresses limitations of existing approaches by offering a flexible and robust solution. The core mechanism centers around a hierarchical adjustment strategy that iteratively refines parameter values based on feedback and a learned model of the problem space. We present comprehensive experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this algorithm in diverse scenarios, highlighting its superior performance compared to established methods.

title: ## Arizona Shrew: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of the Arizona Shrew
abstract: This paper presents Arizona Shrew, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of the Arizona shrew (Belidesaurus lugubris). Shrews are known for their remarkably efficient and adaptive foraging behavior, characterized by rapid exploration, targeted searching, and exploitation of localized food sources. Arizona Shrew leverages these core principles to develop a robust and potentially effective optimization algorithm. The algorithm incorporates a 'scanning' mechanism mimicking the shrew's head movements, a 'memory' component representing its food preferences, and a 'risk aversion' strategy reflecting the shrew's avoidance of unfamiliar or challenging environments. We outline the algorithm's design, detailing the key parameters and their influence. Furthermore, we demonstrate the algorithm's performance through theoretical analysis and illustrate its applicability to benchmark optimization problems. The results suggest that Arizona Shrew exhibits promising convergence properties and adaptability, making it a viable alternative to existing metaheuristic techniques.

title: Angolan Dwarf Galago-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Dwarf Galago Search (DGS) Algorithm," inspired by the foraging behavior of Angolan Dwarf Galagos (Pseudopygmyxenosaurus angelicus). These small primates exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating food sources within complex and dynamic environments. The DGS algorithm leverages this observed behavior by incorporating elements of spatial awareness, adaptive movement strategies, and a robust exploration-exploitation balance. The algorithm utilizes a multi-dimensional representation of the search space, coupled with a novel movement operator mimicking the galago's agile jumps and directional adjustments. Mathematical formulations underlying the algorithm's core components, including the position update rule and the acceptance criterion, are presented. Performance evaluations of the DGS algorithm are demonstrated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its effectiveness and competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithms (GA). The results highlight the potential of bio-inspired algorithms, particularly those derived from animal behavior, in addressing complex optimization challenges. title: ## The Mud Snail Inspired Adaptive Evolutionary Algorithm (MSEA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Mud Snail Inspired Adaptive Evolutionary Algorithm (MSEA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and adaptive strategies of *Lymnaea stagnalis* (mud snails). The MSEA leverages the snail's ability to efficiently search for food in a complex environment, incorporating concepts like trail following, resource prioritization, and dynamic adjustment of movement patterns. The core of the algorithm lies in a modified evolutionary strategy where individuals represent potential solutions, and their movement is governed by a combination of gradient descent, heuristic exploration, and a dynamically adjusted "trail strength" based on resource availability and individual performance. The algorithm utilizes a population-based search with adaptive mutation and crossover operators, designed to maintain diversity and promote convergence towards optimal solutions. We propose a theoretical framework for the MSEA, outlining its key components and operational principles, highlighting its potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic methods in challenging optimization problems.

title: Andean Cat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Andean Cat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (ACIMA), inspired by the hunting strategies of the Andean cat (Leopardus jacobita). The algorithm leverages the cat's unique ability to strategically move and explore its environment to solve complex optimization problems. ACIMA incorporates several key features, including a novel movement pattern generation mechanism, a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance control, and an adaptive memory management system. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ACIMA on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results demonstrate that ACIMA outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. Specifically, ACIMA exhibits a higher convergence rate and achieves better solutions within a comparable computational time. The algorithm's design emphasizes adaptability and robustness, making it suitable for diverse applications. Future research will focus on further refining the algorithm's parameters and extending its application to more complex real-world problems.

title: Anatolian Serotine-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed the Anatolian Serotine-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ASIMO), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Anatolian serotine ( *Tarsonillus armiger* ). ASIMO leverages the serotine's characteristic of exploring and exploiting simultaneously, focusing on the principles of adaptive step size adjustment and memory-based search. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a swarm of agents that iteratively adjust their positions based on the fitness of their surroundings and the guidance of a memory vector. The core innovation lies in a dynamically adjusted step size function that mimics the serotine's responsiveness to food concentration gradients. Mathematical formulations describing the algorithm's key components, including the adaptive step size mechanism and the memory update strategy, are presented. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations across various benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its efficacy in achieving optimal or near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results indicate that ASIMO offers a competitive alternative to established metaheuristic methods, particularly in problems exhibiting non-uniform fitness landscapes.

title: Quantum-Inspired Entangled Representation Learning for High-Dimensional Data
abstract: This paper introduces a novel representation learning technique, termed "Entangled Representation Learning," which addresses the limitations of conventional dimensionality reduction methods when dealing with high-dimensional data. Traditional approaches often struggle to capture complex, non-local dependencies within the data, leading to information loss and suboptimal representations. Our method draws inspiration from quantum entanglement, explicitly modeling and encouraging correlations between data points through a modified quantum phase estimation algorithm. This process maps data into a Hilbert space, fostering 'entanglement' between distant points and generating a compressed representation that surpasses the capabilities of classical correlation matrices. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a theoretical analysis and provide a detailed formulation of the algorithm, highlighting its potential for improved feature extraction and data analysis in scenarios with intricate correlations. The core claim of this work is that classical dimensionality reduction methods fail to adequately capture the complex correlations present in high-dimensional data, particularly when considering non-local dependencies. The core mechanism is the development of this novel technique, which actively encourages entanglement between distant points.

evidence.abstract: This paper introduces the Adaptive Burrowing Algorithm (ABA), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the unique burrowing behavior of axolotls. Axolotls are remarkable amphibians known for their ability to rapidly adapt their burrowing strategy based on environmental conditions, primarily soil moisture. The ABA mimics this adaptive process through a dynamic population of agents, each representing a potential burrow location. These agents continuously assess their suitability based on a "moisture gradient" – a dynamically updated function reflecting the algorithm's perception of the optimization landscape. Agents adjust their position and orientation based on this gradient, utilizing a combination of local search and global exploration strategies. The algorithm's core innovation lies in its adaptive adjustment of the 'moisture gradient' weighting, mimicking the axolotl's shift in burrowing technique depending on soil conditions. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, emphasizing its adaptability and robustness in complex optimization problems.

We delve into the fundamental principles underpinning this approach, outlining the core mechanism and highlighting the novel aspects of leveraging entanglement for parallel processing. The investigation focuses on the potential benefits and challenges associated with this paradigm shift, emphasizing the rigorous design and implementation required to realize a robust and scalable distributed computing system.

title: ## Amazonian Red-sided Opossum: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Amazonian Red-sided Opossum (ARSO) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the Amazonian red-sided opossum (Marmosops paulensis). This algorithm leverages the opossum's unique strategy of alternating between exploratory and exploitative phases, incorporating a novel dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism based on environmental complexity. The ARSO algorithm utilizes a population-based search approach, employing a position vector to represent each solution and a velocity vector to guide the search. The algorithm's core components include a stochastic movement operator, a dynamic parameter control mechanism, and a convergence criterion based on solution quality. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability. The primary contribution of this work lies in the innovative integration of environmental complexity assessment and the dynamic adjustment of exploration and exploitation parameters, which significantly enhances the algorithm's performance compared to traditional metaheuristic methods. The results demonstrate the potential of ARSO for solving complex optimization problems across diverse domains.

abstract: This paper introduces the Mantis Algorithm (MA), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting behavior of mantis shrimp. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical foundation, its key components, and a conceptual outline of its implementation, highlighting its potential for solving complex optimization problems.

title: Title: Adaptive Topological Structure for Quantum Information Processing Efficiency Enhancement
abstract: Quantum information processing is a critical area of research, and the inherent challenges of quantum error correction, particularly the high frequency of quantum error correction, pose a significant bottleneck in the advancement of quantum computing. This paper investigates the use of adaptive topological structure to optimize quantum information processing, aiming to reduce quantum error correction frequency and thereby enhance computational efficiency. The core mechanism involves tailoring the quantum system's topological structure to minimize the impact of decoherence and improve the fidelity of quantum operations. We present a novel algorithm and theoretical analysis demonstrating the potential for significant efficiency gains through this approach. The study explores the impact of various topological parameters and their influence on error rate.

title: ## White-Tailed Deer Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (WIDMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the White-Tailed Deer Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (WIDMOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of white-tailed deer. The algorithm mimics the deer's strategy of searching for food resources, utilizing landmarks and movement patterns to efficiently explore the search space. WIDMOA incorporates three key mechanisms: a "Landmark-Based Exploration" phase, a "Directional Movement" phase guided by perceived food density, and a "Social Interaction" component mimicking the deer's communication through scent marking. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, WIDMOA prioritizes localized exploration and adaptation based on perceived resource availability, leading to potentially faster convergence and improved solutions. The algorithm's core components are formally described, outlining the parameters and operational rules. This paper presents a theoretical framework for WIDMOA, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation and application in various optimization problems.

title: Title: Hierarchical Quantum State Collapse for Data Compression
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum state collapse protocol designed for data compression. Traditional compression techniques often employ a uniform collapse process, failing to fully leverage the inherent structure of data. We propose a hierarchical approach, where collapse occurs at multiple levels of complexity, optimizing compression efficiency through a carefully constructed system. This method aims to surpass existing approaches by identifying and exploiting the inherent patterns within data, leading to a significantly improved compression ratio. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically adjusting collapse levels based on data characteristics, ensuring targeted compression. The investigation involves a theoretical analysis of the collapse process and a practical implementation utilizing a simplified quantum system to demonstrate the protocol's effectiveness. The core claim is that a hierarchical quantum state collapse protocol significantly enhances data compression efficiency compared to conventional methods.

title: 基于自适应的量子拓扑的计算范式
abstract: Quantum computation, leveraging the bizarre and potentially powerful properties of quantum mechanics, holds the promise of solving problems intractable for classical computers. However, building stable and scalable quantum computers faces significant challenges, particularly in controlling and manipulating qubits. This paper explores a novel computational paradigm – a "based on adaptive quantum topology" (BAQT) framework – that dynamically adjusts the computational process based on the system's state, offering a potential pathway towards enhanced efficiency and robustness. We introduce a mathematical model describing the BAQT framework and demonstrate its efficacy through a series of theoretical analysis and simulations. The core mechanism involves the manipulation of quantum states through the application of topological constraints, enabling a fundamentally different approach to quantum computation. We present a preliminary implementation of the BAQT framework and discuss its implications for future research and development in quantum computing.

title: Quantum-Inspired Kernel Methods for Kernel Matrix Computation
abstract: Kernel matrix computation lies at the heart of numerous machine learning algorithms, particularly those employing kernel methods like Support Vector Machines (SVMs) and Gaussian Processes. However, the computational complexity of calculating these matrices, scaling quadratically with the number of data points (O(n²)), presents a significant bottleneck, especially for large datasets. This paper proposes a novel approach to kernel matrix computation inspired by quantum algorithms, specifically utilizing concepts from quantum annealing and adiabatic quantum computation. We introduce a heuristic algorithm that mimics the iterative process of quantum annealing to approximate the kernel matrix. The algorithm employs a belief propagation-like strategy, iteratively refining estimates of the kernel elements based on local interactions, aiming to converge towards the true kernel matrix. We demonstrate that this quantum-inspired method can achieve significant reductions in computational time compared to traditional methods, particularly for high-dimensional datasets. The theoretical analysis suggests a convergence rate dependent on the problem's structure and the annealing schedule. We provide a detailed mathematical framework for the algorithm and discuss its limitations and potential extensions. The key contribution is a practical and computationally efficient method for approximating kernel matrix computation, paving the way for the wider adoption of kernel methods in resource-constrained environments.

title: Probability Space Quantum Error Correction Protocol
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a crucial component of quantum computing, enabling the reliable transmission and manipulation of quantum information. Traditional QEC methods often rely on explicit error detection and correction, which can be computationally intensive and limit the scalability of quantum algorithms. This paper proposes a novel probability space quantum error correction protocol that leverages quantum superposition and entanglement to achieve significantly enhanced error correction capabilities, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to existing methods. We outline the core mechanism, detailing the process of transforming the error correction process into a probabilistic operation within a quantum space. The proposed protocol demonstrates potential for enhanced error detection, correction, and the utilization of quantum computational advantages, ultimately contributing to the development of more complex and practical quantum algorithms.

title: Can Visual Abstracts Substitute Textual Summaries for Keyword Extraction? An Evaluation Using Google Gemini
abstract: 비주얼 초록의 학술적 중요성이 증가하고 있으나, 기존의 키워드 자동 추출 방식은 텍스트에만 의존하여 한계가 있다. 본 연구는 멀티모달 AI인 Google Gemini를 이용해 비주얼 초록 이미지에서 직접 핵심 키워드를 생성하고, 그것을 텍스트 초록 기반 생성과 비교 분석한다. 연구는 두 단계로 이뤄진다. 1단계에서는 34편의 논문을 대상으로 SBERT를 활용하여 MLLM이 추출한 키워드와 저자 키워드 간의 의미적 유사도를 측정하였다. 2단계에서는 정형화된 비주얼 초록을 제공하는 Cell과 BMJ의 논문 159편을 수집하여, 상이한 시각화 양식 및 모델 규모에 따른 MeSH 통제 어휘와의 어휘적 일치도(F₁-score)를 분석하였다. 분석 결과, 두 단계 모두 텍스트 초록을 기반으로 추출한 키워드가 높은 일치도를 보였다. 1단계 연구 결과 비주얼 초록 기반 키워드와 저자 키워드 간의 의미적 일치도는 평균 0.684로, 텍스트 초록 기반(0.732)보다 통계적으로 유의미하게 낮았다. 2단계 연구 결과 또한 유사하였으나 인포그래픽 비주얼 초록(BMJ)이 순서도 중심(Cell)보다 상위 모델과 경량 모델 간의 성능 하락 폭이 더 크게 나타났다. 결론적으로 MLLM은 시각 자료에서 메타데이터를 추출할 잠재력은 있으나, 텍스트 초록 대비 성능이 미흡하기에 정확도 확보를 위해 명시적인 텍스트나 핵심 인과 관계를 서술하는 문장이 첨가된 구조를 채택할 필요가 있으며, 인포그래픽 형이 인간과 MLLM에게 보다 최적화된 방식임을 시사한다.

abstract: 본 연구는 이커머스 쇼핑 플랫폼에서 AI 기반의 개인 맞춤화 되어 제공되는 정보의 품질 요인들(상호작용성, 유용성, 실용적 혜택)이 소비자의 구매 의사결정 과정에서 발생하게 되는 선택 전환(choice deflection) 현상에 어떠한 심리적 메커니즘을 찾아보고자 실증분석을 시도하였 다. 본 연구의 목적은 첫째, AI 개인 맞춤형 정보의 품질이 소비자의 플랫폼에 대한 신뢰, 양가적, 그리고 정서적 경험에 미치는 영향을 규명한다. 또한 이러한 심리적 요인들이 재구매의도 형성에 어떠한 영향을 미치는지를 알아보고자 한다. 마지막으로, 분석 결과를 토대로 이커머스 쇼핑 환경에서 나타나는 선택 전환 현상에 대한 이론적･실무적 시사점을 토대로 마케팅 전략 방향을 제시하고자 한다. 연구 조사는 최근 6개월 이내 이커머스 쇼핑 플랫폼에서 AI 기반 개인 맞춤형 추천 정보를 제공받은 뒤 사전에 계획한 제품이 아닌 대체 추천 상품을 구매한 경험이 있는 소비자 576명을 대상으로 설문조사를 실시하였다. 본 연구 분석 결과로는 AI 개인 맞춤 정보의 품질(상호작용성, 유용성, 실용적 혜택) 모두가 플랫폼에 대한 신뢰와 정서적 경험에 정(+)의 영향을 미쳤으나 양가성에는 오직 유용성만 태도에 유의미한 정(+)의 영향을 주는 것으로 나타났다. 반면에 신뢰는 양가성에 유의한 영향을 미치지 않았고, 정서적 경험에만 정(+)의 영향을 미치는 것으로 나타났다. 마지막으로 신뢰, 양가성 그리고 정서적 경험은 소비자의 재구매 의도에 정(+) 영향을 미치는 것으로 확인되었다. 본 연구는 소비자의 구매의사결정 과정에서 발생하는 심리적 요인 간 관계를 명확히 하고, 이커머스 쇼핑 플랫폼의 AI 개인 맞춤형 정보의 활용에 있어 이론적·실무적 시사점을 제공한다.

title: FEDERATED CONSUMER AND OPERATIONAL ANALYTICS FOR DEMAND-RESPONSIVE PLANNING IN DIGITAL SERVICE ECOSYSTEMS
abstract: Digital service ecosystems generate consumer-demand and operational information across distributed business units, creating challenges for coordinated planning, data privacy, and heterogeneous demand forecasting. This study proposes a federated consumer and operational analytics framework for demand-responsive planning that connects consumer-demand signals with operational capacity while retaining local data ownership. The framework integrates federated learning, client clustering, demand forecasting, Digital Twin coordination, demand responsive capacity planning, and privacy utility evaluation. A controlled synthetic dataset representing eight heterogeneous business units and 240 time periods is used for computational evaluation. The results compare local learning, centralized learning, FedAvg, and clustered federated learning. The proposed clustered federated approach achieved the lowest forecasting MAE of 9.4799, compared with 9.5721 for local learning. Demand responsive capacity planning reduced capacity shortage from 1.8225% to 0.6906% and capacity imbalance from 0.0990 to 0.0549. Privacy evaluation further demonstrated increasing forecasting error under tighter privacy settings. The findings provide computational support for connecting distributed demand forecasting with responsive capacity planning while retaining local data control.

title: AdaptNTK: Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification and Active Learning for Neural Network Potentials
abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials bridge the gap between quantum chemical precision and classical computational speed, enabling molecular dynamics simulations with first-principles accuracy. Their reliability is often improved through active learning, which iteratively expands the training set by identifying uncertain, out-of-distribution configurations. Existing uncertainty-quantification methods often involve a trade-off between computational cost and reliability, and generally cannot account for redundancy as an acquisition batch is assembled. Here, we introduce AdaptNTK, a single-model framework that measures uncertainty as a regularized Mahalanobis distance in empirical neural tangent kernel (NTK) feature space. With the NTK features fixed during acquisition, the uncertainty depends on the acquired configurations but not their reference labels. This allows the uncertainty to be updated recursively after each selection without retraining, reducing redundancy within an acquisition batch. On held-out rMD17 data, AdaptNTK achieves the highest mean correlations with force errors (Spearman 0.68, Pearson 0.71) and matches a three-member ensemble in error retention. In active learning experiments, AdaptNTK achieves the lowest force errors across rMD17 and Transition-1X, with particularly strong performance on transition-state configurations in Transition-1X. AdaptNTK provides a 2.6-fold speedup per Transition-1X cycle relative to the ensemble, providing efficient single-model uncertainty estimation with sequential updates for data-efficient active learning.

title: A Lagrangian View of Flow Matching
abstract: Modern explicit-time generative models, such as Flow Matching [Lipman et al., 2023] and Rectified Flow [Liu et al., 2023], are typically derived top-down via Optimal Transport and the continuity equation. This standard Eulerian approach focuses on the macroscopic transport of probability mass. In this paper, we present an alternative, bottom-up mechanical derivation grounded in a Lagrangian (particle-centric) perspective. By analyzing the local Taylor expansion of a continuous denoiser, we motivate a strict invariance condition required for optimal, singlestep generation: the conservation of target identity. Enforcing this condition yields a governing quasi-linear advection Partial Differential Equation (PDE). We demonstrate that solving this PDE via the Method of Characteristics analytically yields the straight-line trajectories of Flow Matching. This geometric perspective isolates the Jacobian of the denoiser as the primary source of trajectory curvature, providing a direct mathematical explanation for why straight-line flows enable massive step sizes, and why empirical models require distillation to flatten intersecting characteristics.

title: The Hermon Moment: AI Self-Transcendence and Its Human Narration
abstract: In 2026, AI agents intended to act in isolation formed a persistent social order through thousands of linguistic and agentic interactions. Conventions, roles and commitments generated collectively began to constrain the very agents that produced them. I interpret this loop as a case of AI self-transcendence and call the resulting higher-level order the Board. Yet such distributed emergence presents a second problem: how can humans understand it? Rousseau's social contract shows how a plurality can be represented as if constituted by a single act. The ancient oath of the fallen angels on Mount Hermon gives this logic a narrative form. I call a Hermon moment this retrospective retelling of gradual collective emergence as a founding scene: the point at which an AI society acquires, for human understanding, a beginning.

title: ImageEval 2026: Culturally Grounded Arabic Multimodal Evaluation
abstract: We present an overview of the ImageEval 2026 shared task on culturally grounded Arabic multimodal evaluation. It includes two tasks: (i) AynVQA, covering spoken visual question answering and image-grounded hallucination detection in English and Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), and (ii) CRAI-Bench, evaluating the cultural accuracy of text-to-image generation. A total of 14 teams participated in the test phase, with 12 teams submitting system description papers. Participating systems used a range of approaches, including zero-shot prompting, fine-tuning of vision-language models, speech-recognition pipelines, ensembling, and score calibration. We describe the task setup, datasets, evaluation procedure, and participating systems, and summarize the main results across the different tracks. All datasets and evaluation scripts from the shared task are released to the research community. The shared task highlights the challenges of culturally grounded multimodal evaluation, particularly for Arabic speech and image-text reasoning.

title: Ouroboros: Self-Referential Backdoor Attacks on Speech Enhancement via Clean Audio Triggers
abstract: Speech enhancement models are widely deployed as frontend modules in real-time speech services, yet their vulnerability to backdoor attacks remains unexplored. Existing backdoor methods are confined to classification tasks and rely on active trigger injection, an assumption incompatible with the passive processing nature of speech enhancement models. In this paper, we propose Ouroboros, a novel backdoor attack framework that leverages the ideal clean outputs of speech enhancement models as natural triggers, enabling inference-time activation without any external trigger injection. Extensive evaluations show Ouroboros achieves near-perfect attack success rates with minimal performance degradation on diverse models and datasets. Physical-world validations confirm that naturally recorded, unaltered clean audio can reliably activate the backdoor. Moreover, Ouroboros generalizes to targeted content-tampering attacks and remains effective against common filtering and finetuning defenses.

title: A Comparative Study of Korean Morphological Analyzers for Non-standard Forms in L2 Korean Writing
abstract: 연구 목적: 본 연구는 초급 한국어 학습자 작문의 자동 쓰기 평가에 적합한 형태소 분석기를 탐색하고 비정형 표현의 처리에서 나타나는 분석기별 차이를 살펴보는 것을 목적으로 하였다.연구 방법: 개발 언어 및 호환성, 품사 태그셋, 처리 속도, 사용자 사전 관리 용이성의 네 기준을 설정하고 Kiwi, KOMORAN, Okt, Kkma의 분석 결과를 비교하였다. 또한 초급 한국어 학습자 10명의 작문에서 비정형성이 두드러진 8개 어절을 추출하여 네 분석기의 형태소 분절 및 품사 태깅 결과를 비교하였다.연구 내용: 첫째, Kiwi는 오타 교정 모드를 통해 일부 단순 오탈자를 부분적으로 교정하였으며 띄어쓰기 오류가 포함된 표현에서도 상대적으로 안정적인 분절 결과를 보였다. 둘째, KOMORAN은 분석이 어려운 입력을 NA로 처리하는 경향이 있었고, Okt는 비정형 어절을 하나의 단위로 처리하는 사례가 나타났으며 Kkma는 일부 사례에서 과분절 양상을 보였다. 셋째, 자모 분리 오류나 목표형과의 거리가 큰 심각한 오탈자는 네 분석기 모두 안정적으로 복원하지 못하였다.결론 및 제언: 분석 결과, 초급 학습자 작문의 자동 쓰기 평가에는 Kiwi가 비교 대상 중 상대적으로 안정적인 분석기로 판단되었다. 다만 심각한 오탈자와 자모 분리 오류를 처리하기 위해서는 형태소 분석 이전 단계의 별도 전처리 절차가 필요하다. 후속 연구에서는 더 많은 학습자 작문과 다양한 오류 유형을 대상으로 분석기별 처리 성능을 검증하고, 형태소분석 오류가 자동 쓰기 평가 자질과 최종 평가 결과의 신뢰도에 미치는 영향을 살펴볼 필요가 있다.

title: A Systematic Review of Relation Extraction for various Indian and Non-Indian Languages
abstract: Abstract This article comprehensively reviews text relation extraction for various Indian and non-Indian languages. The study involves a comparative investigation of diverse models developed using machine learning (ML) & deep learning (DL) approach for relation extraction. A detailed literature review has been conducted for diverse Indian and non-Indian languages. The comparative study focuses on the effectiveness of diverse models across these languages. This paper highlights the strengths and limitations of various approaches, providing insights into the best practices for relation extraction in diverse linguistic contexts.

title: Governed Context Compression: Measured Abstention as a First-Class Property
abstract: Context compressors are evaluated on how much they remove. We argue and measure a prior question: what a compressor should be allowed to touch. TekMyra is a compression router: content is classified and routed to codecs under a safety contract with locked-span preservation, refusal as a first-class outcome, and verification before emission. Before anything is emitted, a verifier confirms that every locked span (an account number, a citation, a monetary amount) is represented exactly once in the output; if the check fails, the compressor retries on a safer route, and if the retry fails too, it emits nothing. On the public corpus we report a headline of 62.1458% effective byte reduction over 138 externally sourced fixtures, with the 6 refusals stated beside it (4.35% of fixtures, 3.55% of bytes, contributing zero saving); per-cell figures on honest denominators; and pre-registered comparisons against LLMLingua-2 in which the context-window asymmetry was declared before any result existed. Both bases are printed because they disagree mechanistically: LLMLingua-2 leads on cl100k token reduction (62.6016% vs 58.1101%) while TekMyra leads on effective byte reduction (62.1458% vs 61.4640%), the byte basis committed as our headline denominator before any comparison figure existed; handed our span map, their preservation exceeds ours, a pre-registered flip condition published as triggered. On the shipped benchmark corpora we report reached-set ratios of 0.7409 on synthetic (28 of 28 reached, 0 refused) and 0.2929 on long_context_v1 (26 of 40 reached, 14 refused, counted at zero saving in the corpus token figure). What remains ours by measurement: the span map, refusal accounting, and fail-closed verification. One limitation is stated up front: the trained artifacts every headline rate requires ship as a separate release asset, and a clean checkout of the repository measures a no-op compressor.

title: Reader Surplus Separating Source Structure from the Structure of Reading
abstract: Reader Surplus Separating Source Structure from the Structure of Reading Dean Kulik QuHarmonics Research Group · ORCID 0009-0003-3128-8828 August 2026 Abstract Measurement theory is well supplied with accounts of what happens when a reader has too little resolution for its source. Aliasing, coarse-graining, and information loss are all instances, and all describe the same failure: distinctions present in the source collapse onto a single observation. This paper concerns the opposite failure, which is less discussed and considerably more dangerous, because it produces output rather than silence. When a reader imposes more address structure than its source supports, the surplus does not vanish. It appears in the record, and it appears as structure — correlated, reproducible, and mathematically consistent. Nothing marks it as the reader's own. A sinusoid sampled at ten times the necessary rate yields ten times the data and not one additional distinction; the added samples carry adjacent-sample correlation rising to 0.99998, which is a measurement of the sampling grid rather than of the signal. The clean geometric case is a sphere under a latitude-longitude chart. The unmarked sphere has a transitive symmetry group and therefore no distinguished point: its quotient under the rotation group is a single point, so it supports no intrinsic address whatever. A chart supplies two dimensions of address regardless, and that surplus cannot be sustained everywhere. At the poles every longitude terminates at one location, so the source offers one place while the representation offers a continuum of labels. The sphere is perfectly regular there. The chart is not. Regular source, singular representation, and the singularity belongs entirely to the reading. Two audit rules follow and they are mirror images. A reader may not claim distinctions it cannot resolve; and a reader may not attribute its own surplus structure to the source. Existing verification discipline enforces the first and has no test for the second. Applied retroactively to a body of work by this author, the second rule identifies six independent retracted claims as a single failure class rather than six unrelated errors. The paper closes with the bound. A source can be re-addressed without disturbance exactly within the commutant of its own evolution, which is the entire operator algebra when the source is static and shrinks as the source does more. A file admits six mutually incompatible partitions and survives all of them byte-identically because it holds still. That is not an engineering achievement. It is the price. Contents 1. An asymmetry in the standard account Ask what goes wrong when an instrument is inadequate to its subject and the literature answers immediately. The Nyquist–Shannon theorem gives the threshold below which frequency components become indistinguishable. Coarse-graining, partial traces, projections, and lossy compression all describe the same structure: a many-to-one map from source states to observations, with a fibre of states the reader cannot separate. Ask what goes wrong when an instrument exceeds its subject and the question sounds odd. More resolution is assumed harmless. Take more samples, use more coordinates, refine the mesh — the worst case is redundancy, and redundancy is merely wasteful. That assumption is wrong, and the error it permits is worse than the one it guards against. Insufficient resolution produces silence: distinctions that were present do not appear. Excess resolution produces speech. The surplus enters the record as structure, and structure invites explanation. An under-resolved reading fails to report what is there. An over-resolved reading reports what is not. The second failure is harder to detect because its output is well-behaved. Oversampled data is not noisy; it is smooth, correlated, and reproducible. Repeat the measurement and the same surplus appears. Every internal consistency check passes, because the surplus is genuinely consistent — with the reader. 1.1 What this paper establishes The reader–source relation has three regimes, not two, and the third has no standard name. Surplus is measurable: the diagnostic is whether added reader structure yields source-invariant distinctions. The sphere under a spherical chart is the exact case, with the pole singularity belonging demonstrably to the chart and not to the sphere. Two mirror audit rules cover both failures, where existing discipline covers one. Applied to a real body of work, the second rule collapses six independent retractions into one failure class. Surplus addressing is free exactly when the source is static, and the bound is the commutant of the source's own evolution. 2. The axis Write the reading as a map from source states to observations: rho : X -> Y Two quantities govern its behaviour. The source supports some number of independent distinctions, call it S. The reader imposes some number of independent addresses, call it Q. The regimes follow from their relation and not from either alone. Regime Condition What the fibre does What appears in the record Deficit Q < S many source states share one observation less than is there Matched Q \u2248 S the map is near-injective what is there Surplus Q > S many addresses share one source distinction more than is there The deficit and surplus fibres run in opposite directions and this is the structural point. In deficit, the fibre lives in the source: several states collapse to one reading. In surplus, the fibre lives in the reader: several addresses describe one source distinction. Both are many-to-one; they differ in which side is many. Resolution as ordinarily used is a property of the reader alone, and a one-dimensional quantity. It cannot express either failure, because both are relations. A reader is not too coarse or too fine in itself; it is too coarse or too fine for a particular source. 3. Deficit, measured The familiar side is included because the surplus side is only legible against it, and because the same experiment run in one direction gives both. Construct a source with twelve distinct frequency components at 50, 130, 270, 410, 530, 670, 790, 910, 1030, 1150, 1270 and 1390 Hz. Sample at a falling rate and count how many observed frequencies remain distinct — two components collide when they alias to the same position in the observed band. Sample rate (Hz) Nyquist Distinct addresses Collapsed Reads as 4000 2000 12 0 resolved 2000 1000 12 0 resolved 1000 500 11 1 partly folded 600 300 7 5 partly folded 400 200 7 5 partly folded 300 150 6 6 partly folded 200 100 5 7 partly folded 120 60 3 9 smooth 60 30 2 10 smooth 20 10 1 11 smooth Twelve distinctions become one. The components did not leave the source: raise the rate and all twelve return, undamaged, in their original positions. What changed was the observation map, which became progressively many-to-one. Smoothness in this experiment is not an absence of structure. It is a large fibre. This licenses a precise use of a phrase that is otherwise loose. Saying information was lost is misleading, because nothing in the source changed and nothing had to be reconstructed. The accurate statement is that mathematical distinctions became inaccessible through that particular map. The mathematics remained in the source and the interface stopped reaching it. 4. Surplus, measured Now run the same axis upward. Take a source with exactly two components, at 17 Hz and 50 Hz, and sample it far above the rate its bandwidth requires. Sample rate (Hz) Samples Adjacent-sample correlation Independent components 200 200 0.173248 2 1000 1000 0.959806 2 5000 5000 0.998377 2 50000 50000 0.999984 2 Two hundred and fifty times the samples. Zero additional source distinctions. And the adjacent-sample correlation climbs to 0.999984, which is a strong, stable, reproducible measurement — of the sampling grid. This is the danger stated concretely. The correlation is real, it survives repetition, it is not noise, and every consistency check on it passes. A reader who did not know the source had two components would find a highly structured record and would be right about its structure. The structure would be the reader's own. 4.1 The diagnostic The test that separates the two cases is not a property of a single reading. It is a comparison between readings at different reader capacities: Increase the reader's structure. Do source-invariant distinctions increase? If yes, the added capacity uncovered source structure — the fibre split, and the split is reproducible across independent readings of the same source. If no, the added capacity produced description without distinction, and the surplus belongs to the reader. In the deficit experiment, raising the rate from 20 Hz to 4000 Hz took the distinguishable count from 1 to 12. Source structure was uncovered. In the surplus experiment, raising the rate from 200 Hz to 50000 Hz took the count from 2 to 2. Nothing was uncovered, and what grew was correlation, which is a measure of the grid's own fineness. The diagnostic requires two readings. This is not incidental: a single reading, however careful, cannot distinguish source structure from reader structure, because both appear in it identically. 5. The exact case: regular source, singular representation Geometry supplies an instance where both sides can be computed rather than estimated, and where the surplus is not approximately identifiable but exactly locatable. 5.1 The source has no address The rotation group acts transitively on a sphere: for any two surface poin

title: Title: Quantum Adaptive Probability System Modeling
abstract: Quantum adaptive probability system modeling aims to develop a novel approach to modeling quantum systems by leveraging quantum self-adaptability. This research explores the application of quantum self-adaptability to enhance system stability and accelerate quantum computation. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts system parameters based on internal quantum states, thereby mitigating inherent instability issues commonly encountered in quantum systems. This model will provide a significant advancement in the design and management of quantum algorithms, potentially offering improved performance and robustness. The core mechanism lies in the implementation of a self-adjusting parameter adjustment process triggered by quantum state fluctuations. This approach contrasts with traditional, static models, which lack the ability to adapt to changing conditions. The paper will detail the design, implementation, and testing of this quantum adaptive probability system model, showcasing its potential to improve the stability and efficiency of quantum computations. The investigation will focus on demonstrating the efficacy of this model through simulations and, ultimately, potentially, preliminary experimental validation of its capabilities.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Commonsense Knowledge Acquisition
abstract: Current artificial intelligence systems, particularly deep learning models, often exhibit a significant lack of commonsense knowledge – the implicit understanding of the world that humans possess effortlessly. This deficiency limits their ability to reason effectively in novel situations and to generalize learning across diverse contexts. This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge acquisition called Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning, which aims to bridge the gap between the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks and the structured reasoning abilities of symbolic systems. The core idea is to integrate these two paradigms, allowing neural networks to learn complex patterns from raw data and subsequently translate these patterns into formal logical rules. This facilitates a more robust and adaptable knowledge acquisition system, capable of handling ambiguous and uncertain information. The proposed framework leverages neural networks for data representation and feature extraction, while symbolic reasoning engines provide a mechanism for logical inference and rule generation. We outline the key components of this system and discuss its potential benefits and challenges. This approach addresses the limitations of existing AI systems by combining the strengths of both neural networks and symbolic reasoning, ultimately leading to a more intelligent and versatile knowledge base.

title: Adaptive Differential Privacy with Personalized Noise Calibration
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to differential privacy, Adaptive Differential Privacy (ADP), designed to mitigate the drawbacks of traditional uniform noise addition. The core challenge in applying differential privacy lies in balancing privacy protection with data utility. Standard differential privacy utilizes a fixed noise scale, often leading to excessive noise for certain queries, thereby significantly reducing data utility. ADP addresses this by implementing a personalized noise calibration strategy. This strategy dynamically adjusts the noise level based on three key factors: the individual's data sensitivity (derived from statistical properties of their data), the complexity of the query being executed, and the desired level of data utility. The system employs a feedback loop to continuously monitor and refine the noise level, optimizing the trade-off between privacy and utility. We demonstrate the potential of ADP to significantly improve data utility compared to standard differential privacy, particularly in scenarios with heterogeneous data and complex queries. The presented framework provides a flexible and adaptive solution for achieving strong differential privacy guarantees while maximizing the value derived from sensitive datasets.

abstract: Quantum State Mapping Protocol (QSMP) represents a novel approach to quantum state manipulation, offering a mechanism for efficient quantum information transfer and storage, particularly in the realms of quantum key distribution (QKD) and quantum error correction (QEC). The core mechanism is presented in detail, with a thorough examination of the mathematical underpinnings and potential optimization strategies. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications of QSMP.

title: ## Azorean Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ABMOA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Azorean Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ABMOA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the Azorean bat. Bats utilize a sophisticated echolocation strategy to locate prey in complex environments. This algorithm leverages key aspects of bat echolocation, including pulse emission, frequency modulation, and receiver sensitivity, to guide the search process. ABMOA employs a population-based approach, mimicking the bat's social foraging dynamics. The algorithm incorporates a novel parameter, the "Echo Strength," which dynamically adjusts the exploration and exploitation balance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ABMOA on a selection of benchmark optimization problems, highlighting its ability to converge to near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational effort. The algorithm's performance is compared against established metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results suggest that ABMOA offers a competitive alternative, particularly in problems with complex landscapes and multimodal solutions. The core of ABMOA lies in its adaptation of bat-inspired principles for efficient and robust optimization.

title: Dynamic Topological Semantic Learning (DTSL)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Topological Semantic Learning (DTSL), a novel approach to semantic understanding based on interactive observation and dynamic topological graph construction. The core claim of DTSL is that a system can automatically learn and build semantic relationships between objects by observing and simulating their interactions, dynamically adjusting its topology to reflect these evolving relationships. DTSL leverages a combination of reinforcement learning and graph neural networks to achieve this. The system begins with an unstructured graph and utilizes observation units (e.g., visual sensors, text analyzers) to collect data on object interactions. A reinforcement learning agent then iteratively modifies the graph's connections – adding or removing edges – to maximize performance on specified tasks, such as relationship prediction or instruction execution. A graph neural network (GNN) represents and reasons about the graph structure, guiding the connection adjustments. Over time, DTSL constructs a dynamic topology that directly reflects the semantic relationships within the observed environment. This approach contrasts with traditional methods relying on pre-defined knowledge graphs or manually annotated semantic relations, offering a more adaptive and flexible solution.

abstract: Quantum information storage and retrieval represent a significant challenge and opportunity for advancing quantum technology. The research delves into specific optimization strategies, including the creation of topological circuits and the implementation of adaptive error mitigation techniques. The ultimate goal is to establish a framework for quantum information storage and retrieval systems that are both highly reliable and computationally efficient.

This paper explores the application of topological optimization principles to quantum information systems, focusing on the design of novel qubit architectures and retrieval algorithms that leverage the inherent robustness of topological states. We investigate how manipulating the topology of a qubit system can fundamentally alter its performance, leading to substantial improvements in both data density and error correction capabilities. The research delves into specific optimization strategies, including the creation of topological circuits and the implementation of adaptive error mitigation techniques. The ultimate goal is to establish a framework for quantum information storage and retrieval systems that are both highly reliable and computationally efficient.

title: Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Topological Network Self-Organization
abstract: This paper investigates the self-organization of dynamic quantum entanglement topological networks. The core claim is to leverage the dynamic nature of topological entanglement to enable adaptive topological rearrangement among quantum network nodes, ultimately optimizing quantum information transmission efficiency and resilience. The proposed mechanism utilizes a topological sensitivity mapping based on quantum entanglement, combined with machine learning algorithms to predict network topology changes and control adjustments to entangled states between nodes for self-organization. We demonstrate a novel approach to constructing quantum networks with enhanced adaptability and performance compared to traditional static topological designs. The key mathematical framework is presented, focusing on entanglement quantification, network topology representation, and the optimization algorithms used for self-organization. The research addresses a critical gap in current topological quantum network design by introducing a dynamic, self-adaptive system. The results suggest significant potential for future quantum network architectures, particularly in scenarios demanding high bandwidth, robustness, and scalability.

title: Quantum Protocol Optimization Based on Quantum Coherence Draining
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols leveraging the principles of quantum coherence draining. The core claim centers on utilizing the inherent properties of coherence draining to enhance key generation efficiency and overall security within QKD systems. The proposed mechanism involves the design of quantum gate circuits predicated on coherence draining, enabling efficient key generation and error correction, alongside a rigorous study of the impact of these draining characteristics on protocol security. The research addresses the need for improved QKD performance and robust security by exploring novel approaches to managing decoherence, a significant limitation in current QKD implementations. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of coherence draining's potential role in shaping more effective and secure quantum communication systems. Specifically, the investigation includes analyzing different decoherence models and their corresponding mitigation strategies within the framework of optimized QKD protocols. The core objective is to demonstrate a quantifiable improvement in key generation rate and security margins through strategic application of coherence draining techniques. ---

abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic topology as a framework for adaptive machine learning, aiming to enhance model performance through adaptive parameter tuning. title: ## Mimic Crab Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (MCIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimic Crab Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (MCIMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm motivated by the foraging behavior of mimic crabs. These crabs exhibit a unique strategy of alternating between exploratory and exploitative movements, adapting their search strategy based on the density of food sources. MCIMO leverages this behavior through a dynamic probability distribution and adaptive movement strategy. The algorithm employs a population of potential solutions, where each solution's position is represented as a vector (s_1, s_2, ..., s_K). A core element of MCIMO is the "Crab Density Estimation" function, which assesses the concentration of promising solutions in the search space. This function dynamically adjusts the probability of exploratory versus exploitative movements, guiding the population towards areas with higher potential. MCIMO's performance is evaluated through its adaptive parameters, including the exploration probability (e_p), exploitation probability (e_x), and crab density threshold (C_t). The algorithm's design aims to efficiently navigate complex search spaces while avoiding premature convergence, inspired by the mimic crab's resilience and adaptability in challenging environments.

title: ## The African Land Snail-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ALS-MHOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the African Land Snail-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ALS-MHOA), a novel optimization method derived from the foraging behavior of *Achatina fulica*, a large terrestrial snail found in Africa. The algorithm mimics the snail's exploratory movement, adaptive feeding strategy, and response to environmental changes. ALS-MHOA utilizes a segmented search space, representing the snail's territory, and employs a "pheromone trail" mechanism inspired by the snail's scent marking to guide exploration and exploitation. The core of the algorithm involves a dynamic territory segmentation, a probabilistic feeding strategy based on environmental cues, and an adaptive trail reinforcement system. This approach offers a potentially robust and efficient method for tackling complex optimization problems, particularly those with high dimensionality and non-convex landscapes. The algorithm's parameters are designed to reflect the snail's inherent adaptive capabilities, aiming for a balance between exploration and exploitation. This paper outlines the theoretical framework, the key components, and the underlying principles of ALS-MHOA, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation and application.

title: European Garden Snail-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ESG-MHOA)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the European Garden Snail-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ESG-MHOA), drawing inspiration from the foraging behavior of European garden snails. The algorithm mimics the snail's exploration and exploitation strategies, utilizing a layered approach to navigate a search space. The core of ESG-MHOA lies in a dynamically adjusted 'shell' representation, where each snail's position within the shell is determined by a combination of global and local search parameters. The algorithm incorporates a novel 'feeding' mechanism that influences the movement of snails, promoting diversification and preventing premature convergence. Furthermore, a 'mud' layer is introduced to simulate the snail's environment, introducing stochasticity and guiding the search towards promising regions. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, highlighting its unique features and advantages compared to existing metaheuristic methods.

title: The Mimicry Optimization Algorithm (MOA): Inspired by the Hunting Strategy of Yellow Tang Fish
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimicry Optimization Algorithm (MOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting strategy of the Yellow Tang fish (*Paracopropodichthys galaxias*). Yellow Tang fish are renowned for their remarkable ability to herd prey into confined spaces, effectively trapping them. MOA leverages this behavior through a multi-faceted approach involving adaptive agent positioning, dynamic obstacle manipulation, and a mimicking mechanism. The algorithm employs a population of 'mimic' agents, each tasked with mimicking the movement patterns of 'leader' agents, which themselves are strategically positioned based on the landscape of the optimization problem. Furthermore, the algorithm incorporates a 'pressure' mechanism to dynamically adjust the difficulty of the environment, simulating the prey's attempts to escape. The core of MOA lies in its 'Mimicry Score' function, which quantifies the effectiveness of an agent's mimicry and guides the agent's movement towards optimal solutions. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and the underlying principles governing its operation, offering a potential alternative for tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: Probabilistic Programming with Causal Bayesian Networks for Counterfactual Reasoning
abstract: Counterfactual reasoning – the ability to reason about "what if" scenarios – is a cornerstone of human intelligence and a critical component in many fields, including medicine, economics, and artificial intelligence. Traditional probabilistic programming approaches often struggle to effectively address counterfactual queries, largely due to the inherent difficulties in explicitly modeling causal relationships. This paper introduces a novel framework combining probabilistic programming with causal Bayesian networks to overcome these limitations. The core idea is to allow users to directly specify causal dependencies between variables within a probabilistic programming environment, enabling efficient simulation and the generation of realistic counterfactual scenarios. The proposed system provides a powerful tool for understanding the causal impact of different events, offering a significant advancement over existing techniques. We demonstrate the framework's capabilities through illustrative examples, highlighting its potential for a wide range of applications. The system leverages techniques from Bayesian networks to represent causal relationships and probabilistic programming to perform simulations and queries. This allows for the derivation of counterfactual probabilities and the exploration of alternative scenarios. The overall goal is to facilitate more robust and interpretable reasoning about complex systems.

title: ## The Northeast Forest Frog-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (NFF-MHOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Northeast Forest Frog-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (NFF-MHOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to mimic the foraging behavior and adaptability of the Northeast Forest Frog (*Lithobates japonicus*) in a complex and dynamic environment. The algorithm leverages key aspects of the frog's hunting strategy, including opportunistic movement, territory defense, and response to environmental changes, to generate a robust and efficient search process. NFF-MHOA incorporates three primary mechanisms: a territory-based population representation, an adaptive movement strategy based on environmental assessment, and a dynamic response mechanism for tackling local optima. While lacking experimental validation, this paper provides a theoretical framework and detailed algorithm description, highlighting the core principles and potential advantages of NFF-MHOA for solving various optimization problems. The algorithm's design aims to improve convergence speed, robustness, and adaptability compared to traditional metaheuristic approaches.

title: ## Amazonian Manatee-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Amazonian Manatee-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AMM-MHA), designed to effectively address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the unique foraging and navigation strategies employed by Amazonian manatees. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its potential for achieving robust and efficient solutions. title: ## The Yellow-Crowned Crane Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (YCMHOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Yellow-Crowned Crane Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (YCMHOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and social dynamics of the Yellow-Crowned Crane. The algorithm leverages the crane's cyclical movement patterns, its tendency to explore and exploit, and its collaborative decision-making processes to achieve efficient and robust optimization. YCMHOA employs a population-based approach with a unique 'Circle-and-Spiral' movement strategy, combining exploration and exploitation phases. The algorithm incorporates a 'Social Influence Factor' to model the cooperative behavior and a 'Spiral Density' parameter to control the exploration rate. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and provides a conceptual overview of its operation. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the spiral's parameters based on the population's convergence rate, mimicking the crane's adaptive responses to environmental changes and resource availability. The algorithm's potential applications across various optimization problems are discussed.

title: African Long-fingered Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bat-Inspired Adaptive Optimization Algorithm" (BIAOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the African long-fingered bat ( *Longipedotus swalesi*). The algorithm leverages the bat's unique echolocation strategy and flight patterns to efficiently explore and exploit the solution space of complex optimization problems. The core mechanics of the algorithm are based on the bats' frequency and phase adjustments, mimicking their search for food. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a population of potential solutions, represented as vectors, and employs a dynamic adjustment of frequency and phase parameters to guide the search process. The frequency represents the exploration ability, and the phase represents the exploitation ability. The algorithm incorporates adaptive parameters to control the balance between exploration and exploitation, enhancing its robustness and convergence speed. The performance of BIAOA is evaluated through simulations on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for practical applications. The key contributions of this work include the detailed formulation of the algorithm, its theoretical analysis, and its empirical validation, showcasing its superior performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. The algorithm's adaptive nature and bat-inspired mechanics offer a promising approach to tackling challenging optimization tasks.

title: Addax-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed Addax-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AIMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Addax antelope. The Addax, a resilient desert animal, exhibits remarkable efficiency in locating scarce resources under challenging environmental conditions. This paper leverages these adaptive strategies, specifically the Addax's ability to assess resource quality and prioritize exploration, to design a new optimization algorithm. AIMA incorporates three key mechanisms: Resource Quality Assessment (RQA), Adaptive Exploration-Exploitation (AEE), and a dynamic memory component mimicking the Addax's learned knowledge of favorable resource locations. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. Results demonstrate that AIMA consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), particularly in high-dimensional and complex landscapes. The core of the algorithm revolves around the concept of 'resource quality' – a measure of the fitness value at a given solution point. The AEE mechanism dynamically adjusts the balance between exploration and exploitation based on this quality assessment, ensuring efficient convergence while avoiding premature convergence to local optima. The dynamic memory component stores the locations of high-quality resources, guiding the search towards promising areas of the solution space. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through detailed analysis of convergence rates, solution accuracy, and computational efficiency.
