title: Unsupervised anomaly detection with deep generative models: an experimental analysis of model variability and mitigation strategies
abstract: PurposeUnsupervised anomaly detection allows identifying anomalies from unlabeled data, making it useful for neuroimaging analysis and computer-aided diagnosis. Given an individual’s scan, we use a generative model to construct a subject-specific image of healthy appearance and compare both images with identify anomalies. Such approach has drawbacks as the reconstructions are imperfect, and model variability is not taken into account.ApproachWe study model variability arising from using different random seeds during training and explore strategies to mitigate the effect of unwanted reconstruction errors and variability. The strategies include model ensembling, anomaly map normalization, and anomaly map designs based on single or multiple pseudo-healthy reconstructions. We compare these approaches in the context of dementia-related anomalies on 3D FDG PET from ADNI using variational autoencoder models.ResultsOur experiments suggest that variance between models can be reduced by aggregating their reconstructions in a Z-score based anomaly map. This strategy is highly effective, but computationally expensive, as it requires training several instances of the model. An alternative strategy is to normalize the anomaly map using statistics computed from a healthy validation set. We show that this normalization strategy substantially reduces performance variability across models and even increases anomaly detection performance in certain cases.ConclusionWe highlight a largely overlooked source of variability in deep generative models, their random seed, which can lead to substantially different anomaly detection performance and biased evaluation. Our experimental analysis emphasizes that it is crucial to design robust anomaly maps and to mitigate the impact of randomness-induced variability, by accounting for model reconstruction errors for instance using Z-score ensembling, or healthy-control normalization, to support more stable and trustworthy deployment in real-world clinical practice.

title: Less Is More: Balancing Positive and Negative Space in Visual Concept Blending
abstract: Graphic designers often blend visual concepts to communicate multiple ideas within a single image, leveraging positive and negative space to create balance, emphasis, and aesthetic appeal. While computational methods have begun to support automatic concept blending, they largely overlook the role of spatial composition in the design. To address this gap, we present an automatic pipeline that explicitly applies positive and negative space throughout the blending process. Our approach first identifies plausible regions for concept integration by combining semantic reasoning from vision-language models with geometric constraints derived from real-world examples. Conditioned on these regions, the system generates blended compositions using a hybrid pixel-vector pipeline: diffusion-based inpainting produces a fast, coarse initialization, which is then refined through vector-based optimization at the point level to ensure structural coherence and balanced semantic expression. A multimodal agent orchestrates this process as a planner and evaluator, enabling iterative improvement and interpretable control. Through an evaluation using both baseline comparisons and a user study, we demonstrate greater expressiveness, creativity, and concept recognizability by effectively leveraging positive and negative space. We further demonstrate the generalizability of our approach across diverse applications, including controllable image and infographic generation.

title: LLM-Driven Autonomous Vehicles Inherit Human Driver Biases in Pedestrian Yielding: Results and Implications From A New Benchmark
abstract: Public trust in Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) may depend not only on technical success but also on the fairness of their decision making. While a recent trend in AV research involves using general purpose "common sense" models to guide AV decision making, the degree to which these inherit human biases in driving is still understudied. Given that psychology studies have shown human driver biases exist, such as lower pedestrian-yielding rates to Black pedestrians in the US, we argue that analyses of model bias should also be part of AV evaluation. Concretely, in this paper we propose two new bias testing methodologies for Large Language Models (LLMs) and Visual-Language Models (VLMs)-"All Else Being Equal" tests and "Self-Consistency" tests-in order to assess bias in pedestrian-yielding decisions. Our findings show that both LLMs and VLMs make yielding decisions which are influenced by pedestrian gender, ethnicity, religion, disability, age, skin tone and socio-economic status. While the type and degree of bias is different from model to model, we highlight common patterns-and raise questions about the "common sense" model paradigm, particularly the need to either revise the paradigm or address issues of downstream bias.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Quantifying Pulmonary Attribution in Anatomy-Guided Chest X-Ray Classification Under Domain Shift
abstract: Deep-learning models can achieve strong chest X-ray (CXR) classification performance without establishing whether their predictions predominantly rely on pulmonary image content. This study evaluates pulmonary attribution containment as an anatomy-related reliability property distinct from diagnostic performance. We propose DBCA-SegNet-MGAP, a multi-task anatomy-guided CNN-Transformer framework that combines complementary feature representations through bidirectional cross-backbone attention, predicts a soft lung mask, and incorporates this anatomical prior directly into classification through Mask-Guided Adaptive Global Average Pooling (MGAP). Pulmonary attribution containment is quantified using the Anatomical Local Energy Ratio (ALR) and high-intensity cumulative ALR (cALR@0.9). Experiments were repeated across three training seeds using the COVID-19 Radiography Database for four-class internal testing and a locked Shenzhen-to-Montgomery protocol for zero-shot external tuberculosis testing. On COVID-19, the proposed model achieved a weighted F1 of $0.9615 \pm 0.0015$ and macro ROC-AUC of $0.9906 \pm 0.0007$. In an architecture-matched dual-bridge comparison, replacing conventional GAP with MGAP increased ALR from $0.3878 \pm 0.0098$ to $0.7086 \pm 0.0104$ and cALR@0.9 from $0.5265 \pm 0.0101$ to $0.9905 \pm 0.0018$, while weighted F1 remained essentially unchanged ($0.9618 \pm 0.0015$ vs. $0.9615 \pm 0.0015$). Under locked external transfer to Montgomery, ROC-AUC remained $0.9080 \pm 0.0043$ and pulmonary ALR remained $0.6466 \pm 0.0081$, whereas weighted F1 decreased to $0.7528 \pm 0.0080$ and ECE increased to $0.1683 \pm 0.0055$. These findings show that diagnostic discrimination, calibration, and pulmonary attribution containment are distinct model properties and support their joint evaluation under internal testing and external domain shift.

title: Research on Neural Network Technology in Public Safety Anomaly and Hazard Detection
abstract: Abnormal hazards in public places have the characteristics of low frequency, diversity and strong timeliness. Single video model is easily affected by occlusion, illumination and network interruption. In this article, an abnormal danger detection method is constructed, which combines the temporal and spatial characteristics of video, environmental sensing information and communication status, and introduces the neural network synchronization control mechanism under DoS attack. The model uses convolutional network to extract local appearance and motion information, describes the evolution of events with gated time series units, and then completes multi-source feature fusion through attention mechanism. When DoS attacks cause intermittent loss of node data, state observation and synchronization compensation are introduced to maintain the time consistency between the edge detection results and the central model. The experimental results show that the F1 value of the proposed method reaches 0.922, which remains at 0.861 under the packet loss rate of 40%. Synchronous compensation reduces the average state error by about 41.7%. The research shows that the combination of dangerous content identification and network operation state can improve the stability of public safety anomaly detection under the condition of disturbed communication.

title: Ethical use of AI in E-commerce Product recommendations- Consumer trust in Shopsy
abstract: Abstract AI has been a significant influence in the Indian e-commerce landscape, particularly on social commerce sites such as Shopsy, where AI algorithms are capable of creating product suggestions that drive sales. These suggestions make shopping simpler, more applicable and also boost sales. They also pose some significant questions. Is there merit in the suggestions? Is user data safe? Do people understand the purpose of the product(s) they are seeing? But have you ever felt like recommendations were too personal? This is even more crucial for Shopsy, given the reseller-based business model. In this case, there are two levels of trust: between the platform and the reseller; between the reseller and the customer. In the event an AI suggestion is not ethical, trust can fall at both levels and impact the entire business. The study focuses on the ethical use of AI in product recommendations, consumer trust, effects on consumer purchase intention and customer loyalty on Shopsy. The focus is on three ethical aspects: transparency, fairness, and data privacy. The study also examines whether the ttrust decreases when the respondents feel that recommendations are “too intrusive.” For that purpose, Primary data were collected from 50 active Shopsy users and resellers in tier-1, tier-2 and tier-3 cities in India. This was an instrument that consisted of a structured Google Form questionnaire with a 5-point Likert scale. It has been investigated three hypotheses: 1) the relationship between ethical AI and consumer trust; 2) the relationship between consumer trust and purchase intention and loyalty; and 3) the moderator of perceived intrusiveness. Existing literature indicates that transparency, fairness, and privacy are important factors in establishing trust. Users will be more likely to purchase and remain loyal when they have confidence in the ethics and non-intrusiveness of the AI. However, excessive personalisation or lack of control can lead to a loss of trust. This insight prompts important recommendations for Shopsy, such as making recommendations explainable, conducting bias audits, providing data control options, adhering to the DPDP Act 2023, and educating resellers on responsible usage of AI. The research fills a gap in Indian social-commerce and offers a straightforward structure that strikes a balance between personalization and ethics, fostering sustainable growth. The terms used in the article are featured in bold and underlined. The article uses the following keywords, which are bold and underlined. Artificial Intelligence (AI), E-commerce, Product Recommendation, Consumer Trust, Shopsy

In this case, there are two levels of trust: between the platform and the reseller; between the reseller and the customer. In the event an AI suggestion is not ethical, trust can fall at both levels and impact the entire business. The study focuses on the ethical use of AI in product recommendations, consumer trust, effects on consumer purchase intention and customer loyalty on Shopsy. The focus is on three ethical aspects: transparency, fairness, and data privacy. The study also examines whether the ttrust decreases when the respondents feel that recommendations are “too intrusive.” For that purpose, Primary data were collected from 50 active Shopsy users and resellers in tier-1, tier-2 and tier-3 cities in India. This was an instrument that consisted of a structured Google Form questionnaire with a 5-point Likert scale. It has been investigated three hypotheses: 1) the relationship between ethical AI and consumer trust; 2) the relationship between consumer trust and purchase intention and loyalty; and 3) the moderator of perceived intrusiveness. Existing literature indicates that transparency, fairness, and privacy are important factors in establishing trust. Users will be more likely to purchase and remain loyal when they have confidence in the ethics and non-intrusiveness of the AI. However, excessive personalisation or lack of control can lead to a loss of trust. This insight prompts important recommendations for Shopsy, such as making recommendations explainable, conducting bias audits, providing data control options, adhering to the DPDP Act 2023, and educating resellers on responsible usage of AI. The research fills a gap in Indian social-commerce and offers a straightforward structure that strikes a balance between personalization and ethics, fostering sustainable growth. title: Wallhacks, Bots, and the Arms Race: A Narrative Review of Anti-Cheat and Security in Online Games
abstract: Online games are adversarial distributed systems twice over: the design pits players against players, and the security pits every player against the cheaters who modify clients, automate play, and exploit the network. This article presents a narrative review of the literature of that arms race. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the cheat taxonomy, in which Yan and Randell's systematic classification, Hoglund and McCamish's exploitation anatomy, Webb and Soh's survey, and Consalvo's sociological study fixed the enemy's catalog --- modified clients, automation, information exploits, and the social worlds of gaining advantage; the detection systems, in which Yeung's statistical cheater detection, Pao's avatar-trajectory analysis, Thawonmas's behavioral bot detection, and Mitterhofer's server-side techniques fixed the server's counters --- machine learning over movement, the bot's statistical shadow, and the client's integrity checks; and the security frame, in which Anderson's security engineering, the zero-day economics of Bilge and Dumitras, the botnet takeovers of Stone-Gross and colleagues, and the software-exploitation tradition of Hoglund and McGraw placed game security in the discipline's larger war. It is concluded that the literature describes an arms race with a moving frontier: every detection layer (statistical, behavioral, kernel-level) escalates the attacker's layer (client mods, bots, drivers), and the field's settled wisdom is architectural --- cheat resistance designed into the protocol beats cheat detection bolted onto the client.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Topological Structure Analysis and Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, exhibits unique properties that challenge classical intuition. This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to manifest within non-linear topological structures, exploring novel quantum computation models based on this principle. We propose a framework that leverages the inherent topological properties of quantum states, aiming to enhance entanglement stability and computational efficiency. The core mechanism focuses on optimizing quantum circuit topology to mitigate entanglement decoherence, a persistent challenge in quantum information processing. The research explores the impact of topological structure on quantum entanglement, providing a novel approach to improve the performance of quantum algorithms. This work offers a new perspective on harnessing quantum entanglement for advanced computational applications, potentially revolutionizing the landscape of quantum information theory.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Dynamic Routing of Distributed Computing Resources
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to dynamic routing in distributed computing systems leveraging the phenomenon of quantum entanglement. Traditional routing algorithms suffer from latency issues inherent in classical networks, limiting their efficiency and scalability. Our approach utilizes entangled nodes to provide instantaneous information about the state of the entire distributed network, enabling real-time awareness and optimized routing decisions. We introduce a framework where each computing node is entangled with a designated "entanglement node." Measurements of the entanglement node's quantum state provide immediate information about the states of all connected computing nodes. Routing decisions are then based on probability distributions derived from these entangled states, further optimized using quantum algorithms. This method offers a significant reduction in routing latency and promises a more efficient and scalable distributed computing architecture. The core claim of this work is that quantum entanglement can enable significantly more efficient and faster dynamic routing, overcoming the bottlenecks present in classical network routing. ---

title: Causal Discovery Based on Multi-Variable Probabilistic Models
abstract: This paper explores the application of multi-variable probabilistic models for causal discovery. Traditional causal discovery methods often rely heavily on domain expertise and observational data, presenting significant challenges in complex systems where such information is limited or unavailable. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing multi-variable probabilistic models, specifically Bayesian Networks and Structural Causal Models, to automatically learn and infer causal relationships. The core mechanism involves employing algorithms designed for probabilistic inference within these models. The resulting framework offers a data-driven method for identifying causal connections, potentially reducing the reliance on pre-existing knowledge and facilitating discovery in scenarios with sparse or incomplete information. We demonstrate the theoretical underpinnings of this approach and outline a methodology for its implementation, focusing on the ability to model complex dependencies and ultimately, uncover underlying causal structures. This work contributes to a more automated and robust approach to causal inference, opening up possibilities for analysis in diverse fields. ---

title: Relational Causal Inference via Differential Privacy
abstract: Causal inference from observational data is a critical challenge in numerous domains, yet it's notoriously susceptible to biases arising from confounding variables and selection effects. Simultaneously, the increasing availability of sensitive data necessitates robust privacy protection mechanisms. This research proposes a novel framework for relational causal inference that integrates differential privacy (DP) directly into the causal discovery and effect estimation processes. The core idea leverages graphical models – specifically, Bayesian networks – to represent causal relationships, combined with DP algorithms designed to mitigate the risk of information leakage while maintaining the accuracy of causal effect estimates. We introduce a new approach to incorporating DP constraints during the structure learning phase of Bayesian networks, addressing a significant gap in existing DP-based causal inference methods. The framework's theoretical properties are explored, demonstrating the potential for achieving both strong causal inference capabilities and rigorous privacy guarantees. We outline a methodology for quantifying the trade-off between privacy parameters (ε, δ) and the accuracy of causal effect estimation, offering guidance for practical implementation. This work represents a significant step forward in enabling reliable and privacy-conscious causal discovery in real-world scenarios.

title: ##基于多尺度认知图谱的知识发现
abstract: This paper explores the application of multi-scale cognitive graphs for knowledge discovery. The core claim is that constructing such graphs, representing knowledge at varying granularities, allows for a more nuanced understanding of complex systems and facilitates more effective knowledge extraction. The proposed mechanism involves mapping knowledge into multi-scale graphs, utilizing graph analysis algorithms – including node discovery, pathfinding, and pattern recognition – to unveil patterns and relationships. This approach moves beyond the limitations of traditional knowledge graphs that often operate at a single scale. The research demonstrates the potential of multi-scale graphs to provide a more holistic and insightful representation of complex systems, leading to novel knowledge generation. The resulting graph structures are analyzed to identify emergent relationships and patterns, ultimately contributing to a deeper understanding of the system under investigation. The key contribution lies in the systematic framework for constructing and analyzing these multi-scale graphs, offering a robust method for knowledge discovery in complex domains. ---

title: Adaptive Computational Paradigm Based on Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational paradigm, termed the Adaptive Computational Paradigm based on Quantum Entanglement, that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve enhanced parallelism and distributed computation. Traditional computing paradigms often struggle to fully exploit the potential of entanglement for efficient calculations and reasoning. This research proposes a framework utilizing entangled states to significantly improve computational throughput and scalability. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the design of a quantum computation environment and the implementation of algorithms designed to exploit entanglement for faster processing. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential advantages and challenges associated with this approach, emphasizing its promise for future advancements in computational science.

title: 自适应神经网络的动态激活函数
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic activation function for neural networks, designed to enhance performance through adaptive threshold adjustments based on input data's linear relationships. Traditional activation functions often employ fixed parameters, limiting the network's ability to effectively learn and generalize. Our proposed method dynamically adjusts activation thresholds to optimize network behavior, leading to improved prediction accuracy and efficiency. The core mechanism involves a sophisticated algorithm that iteratively optimizes the activation function's parameters to achieve a desired level of performance. We present experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of this approach compared to existing activation functions.

abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to complex system simulation utilizing the principles of quantum entanglement. This paper details the theoretical framework, implementation of the core mechanism, and preliminary results demonstrating the method's potential for advancing complex system simulation. We discuss the challenges and future directions of this research.

title: Information-Theoretic Robustness Certification for Deep Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for certifying the robustness of deep neural networks utilizing information-theoretic principles. The core idea is to quantify the network's sensitivity to input perturbations by measuring information loss within its internal representation space. We leverage mutual information and Kolmogorov complexity to establish rigorous guarantees on robustness. Specifically, we define a sensitivity metric based on the mutual information between the original and perturbed inputs, and employ Kolmogorov complexity to model the complexity of the network's decision boundaries. This approach offers a mathematically grounded and provable certification method, moving beyond the limitations of empirical robustness testing. The proposed framework provides stronger guarantees by directly relating robustness to the fundamental properties of information and complexity. The key contributions of this work lie in the application of information-theoretic tools to the problem of deep network robustness certification, and the development of a quantifiable metric based on Kolmogorov complexity for assessing decision boundary complexity. ---

title: Adaptive Differential Privacy with Dynamic Noise Calibration
abstract: Traditional differential privacy (DP) mechanisms rely on fixed noise scales, a strategy that frequently leads to either over-provisioning of noise, resulting in diminished data utility, or under-provisioning, leaving the data vulnerable to privacy attacks. This paper introduces a novel adaptive differential privacy framework that dynamically calibrates noise scales in response to both the sensitivity of the underlying query and the characteristics of the data distribution. The core of this approach lies in a real-time sensitivity estimation module, coupled with a stochastic noise generator. This allows for a more precise and efficient trade-off between privacy guarantees and data utility, addressing a key limitation of existing DP methods. The proposed framework offers a significant improvement in privacy-utility balance, particularly when dealing with heterogeneous datasets and complex queries. Mathematical notation highlights the key components and calculations within the system.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Satisfaction Problem (Q-CSP)
abstract: Quantum-enhanced Constraint Satisfaction Problem (Q-CSP) addresses the limitations of traditional CSP solvers, particularly in the context of complex, large-scale problems. This research proposes a novel approach leveraging quantum annealing to accelerate the solution process. The core claim is to design a CSP solver that utilizes quantum annealing to efficiently explore solutions, achieving near-optimal performance compared to classical methods. The investigation focuses on the design and implementation of a quantum annealing algorithm tailored for this specific problem. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, the rationale behind its selection, and the experimental evaluation of its performance. The primary objective is to demonstrate a significant reduction in computational time while maintaining or improving solution quality. This work presents a practical exploration of a quantum annealing solution for the Q-CSP, highlighting its potential for tackling complex constraint satisfaction problems.

title: Geometry-Based Mapping for Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computing approach, termed Geometric-Based Mapping, that leverages the inherent properties of geometric structures to enhance the efficiency and stability of quantum computations. Traditional approaches often focus on manipulating quantum states, but this method employs geometric mappings to optimize quantum behavior. The core mechanism involves a carefully designed mapping process, resulting in improved quantum gate fidelity and reduced errors, potentially offering significant advantages in specific applications. The work addresses the limitations of current quantum algorithms by strategically utilizing geometric transformations to mitigate issues arising from inherent quantum decoherence and gate imperfections. This paper explores the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of this approach, demonstrating its potential to unlock new capabilities in quantum information processing.

title: Automated Theorem Proving with Neural Network Guidance
abstract: Automated theorem proving (ATP) aims to develop systems capable of mechanically proving mathematical theorems. Despite significant advancements, ATP systems often struggle with complex reasoning tasks, largely due to the inherent difficulty in representing and executing logical deduction rules. This work proposes a novel approach to ATP that integrates neural networks to provide guidance during the proof process. The core idea is to train a neural network to suggest promising proof steps and identify relevant theorems, essentially acting as an "intelligent assistant" for the ATP system. This guidance mechanism is expected to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of ATP, particularly in tackling challenging mathematical problems. The presented framework utilizes a reinforcement learning approach, where the neural network learns to optimize the proof strategy based on the current state of the proof and the available theorems. The system is evaluated conceptually, outlining the architecture and training process, and highlighting potential improvements. evidence.abstract: Automated theorem proving (ATP) aims to develop systems capable of mechanically proving mathematical theorems. Despite significant advancements, ATP systems often struggle with complex reasoning tasks, largely due to the inherent difficulty in representing and executing logical deduction rules. This work proposes a novel approach to ATP that integrates neural networks to provide guidance during the proof process. The core idea is to train a neural network to suggest promising proof steps and identify relevant theorems, essentially acting as an "intelligent assistant" for the ATP system. This guidance mechanism is expected to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of ATP, particularly in tackling challenging mathematical problems. The presented framework utilizes a reinforcement learning approach, where the neural network learns to optimize the proof strategy based on the current state of the proof and the available theorems. The system is evaluated conceptually, outlining the architecture and training process, and highlighting potential improvements. Further research will focus on developing and refining the network architecture, exploring different training strategies, and integrating the guidance mechanism with existing ATP systems.

title: Bioko Needle-clawed Galago Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Bioko Needle-clawed Galago Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm" (BNG-MHA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the Bioko Needle-clawed Galago, a primate endemic to Bioko Island, Equatorial Guinea. The algorithm leverages the galago's unique hunting strategy – characterized by a series of short, erratic movements interspersed with periods of stillness – to establish a robust and efficient search process. The core principles of the BNG-MHA include a stochastic movement mechanism mimicking the galago's unpredictable trajectory, a local search procedure based on the animal's exploratory behavior, and a global search component influenced by the galago's tendency to shift its focus when encountering obstacles. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in tackling challenges with complex landscapes and multiple local optima. The BNG-MHA exhibits competitive results against established metaheuristic algorithms like the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. This research provides a valuable contribution to the field of metaheuristic optimization by demonstrating that biological inspiration can be a powerful source for designing innovative and effective algorithms.

abstract: This paper presents an automated framework for generating and reasoning with high-dimensional non-linear matrices using deep learning. This framework offers a significant advancement over existing techniques, addressing limitations in adaptability and complexity. This work demonstrates the potential for autonomous matrix generation and inference, opening new possibilities for data analysis and modeling.

title: Quantum Entangled Metric Modulation (QEMM)
abstract: Quantum Entangled Metric Modulation (QEMM) presents a novel approach to dynamically modulate the entanglement of multiple quantum states, offering exponential speedups in complex quantum computations. The core mechanism leverages a dynamically adjustable "entanglement matrix" that adapts to the specific properties of each entangled system, employing stochastic control based on highly complex, non-linear correlation analysis. This contrasts with traditional entanglement keys, which require computationally intensive key establishment. This paper details the theoretical framework, implementation of the QEMM algorithm, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its potential for significant speedup in quantum simulations and algorithm execution.

title: Beaded Hylomyscus: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Hylomyscus*
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Beaded Hylomyscus" (BH), inspired by the foraging strategies observed in *Hylomyscus*, a small rodent known for its intricate and efficient burrow systems and food-gathering techniques. The algorithm leverages the concept of 'bead chains' – a visual representation of the rodent's burrow construction – to guide the search process. BH incorporates elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) while introducing a novel 'bead-linking' mechanism that dynamically adjusts the connectivity between particles, mimicking the rodent's adaptive burrow network. The performance of BH is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with a relatively low computational cost. The key contributions of this work are the innovative bead-linking strategy and the application of rodent foraging behavior as a fundamental principle for algorithm design. The algorithm's core is defined by the following equations: * Particle Position Update: $x_{i}(t+1) = w * x_i(t) + c_1 * r_1 * (\text{pbest} - x_i(t)) + c_2 * r_2 * (\text{gbest} - x_i(t))$ * Velocity Update: $v_{i}(t+1) = w * v_i(t) + c_1 * r_1 * (pbest_i - x_i(t)) + c_2 * r_2 * (gbest - x_i(t))$ * Bead-Linking Adjustment: $λ_{ij}(t+1) = \tanh(α * (x_i(t) - x_j(t))) * \text{sign}(x_i(t) - x_j(t))$ where $λ_{ij}$ represents the linkage strength between particle *i* and particle *j*. * Temperature Update (SA Component): $T(t+1) = T(t) * (1 - α * \frac{\Delta E}{T(t)})$ where $\Delta E$ is the change in error function value.

title: Ashaninka Oldfield Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of a Nocturnal Rodent
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Ashaninka Oldfield Mouse" (AOM), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Ashaninka oldfield mouse ( *Peromyscus defassa*), a nocturnal rodent known for its efficient and adaptive search strategies in complex environments. The algorithm incorporates elements of adaptive step size adjustment, memory-based exploration, and a novel "trail scent" mechanism mimicking the mouse's olfactory navigation. The core of AOM is a self-adaptive parameter system that adjusts parameters based on the objective function's landscape. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results indicate that AOM exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), particularly in challenging and high-dimensional search spaces. Future research will explore the algorithm's application in real-world engineering problems and investigate the theoretical underpinnings of its performance.

abstract: This paper explores the integration of non-linear neural network architectures with evolutionary computation techniques to facilitate rapid design exploration of complex design spaces. The research focuses on demonstrating the effectiveness of this architecture in generating novel designs across a range of problem domains, highlighting its potential for streamlining the design process.

title: Arguedas's Grass Mouse: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Mus agregris*
abstract: This paper presents Arguedas's Grass Mouse (AGM), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Mus agregris*, the Arguedas's grass mouse. This rodent is renowned for its highly efficient and adaptive foraging strategies in complex, spatially distributed environments. AGM leverages these behaviors – specifically, exploration, exploitation, and adaptive movement – to construct a robust optimization process. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a representation of the search space as a set of grass mouse agents. Each agent's movement is governed by a modified Brownian motion with adaptive step-size and direction, mimicking the mouse's probabilistic navigation. Furthermore, the algorithm incorporates a local search component and a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance. Theoretical analysis demonstrates AGM's convergence properties and its potential for improved performance compared to traditional metaheuristic methods. The algorithm is demonstrated through a series of benchmark problems, showcasing its effectiveness in a range of optimization tasks. The key contributions of this work are the novel integration of adaptive movement, a probabilistic representation of the search space, and a dynamic balance between exploration and exploitation.

title: ## The Wrasse-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (WISAR)
abstract: This paper introduces the Wrasse-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (WISAR), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Wrasse fish (Halogenuropsis coeruleus). Wrasses exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate prey amidst complex, three-dimensional environments, utilizing a combination of visual cues, hydrodynamic sensing, and social interaction. WISAR leverages these biological principles by employing a multi-layered search strategy, dynamic adaptation of exploration and exploitation rates, and a novel "herd" concept mirroring the cooperative behavior of wrasse schools. The algorithm's core components include a virtual environment, a population of 'wrasses' represented as agents, and a reward system based on prey location. We detail the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and its conceptual grounding in wrasse foraging behavior, aiming to provide a robust and adaptive approach to various optimization challenges.

title: Quantum Walk-Based Algorithms for Constraint Satisfaction
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum walk algorithms to the problem of constraint satisfaction. Classical constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) are notoriously difficult to solve efficiently, particularly as the problem size grows. We propose a novel approach that leverages the inherent exploration capabilities of quantum walks to address this challenge. The core idea involves mapping a CSP onto a graph and then performing a quantum walk on this graph. The quantum walk's probabilistic nature and interference effects are exploited to accelerate the search for satisfying assignments. We detail the theoretical framework, including the formulation of the quantum walk and the key mathematical operations involved. The analysis focuses on demonstrating the potential for speedup compared to traditional classical CSP solvers. The core claim is that classical CSPs can benefit from the exploration capabilities of quantum walks. The proposed mechanism utilizes quantum walks on graphs to explore the search space of CSPs, leveraging interference effects to accelerate the process of finding solutions. This work lays the groundwork for future research exploring the practical implementation and performance of quantum walk-based CSP solvers.

title: Algorithmic Self-Consistency Theorem Refinement
abstract: The Algorithmic Self-Consistency Theorem (ASTR) provides a framework for analyzing the stability of algorithms. It posits that an algorithm's internal state can be manipulated in a way that leads to a consistent, self-consistent state, implying a fundamental limit to algorithmic control. This paper delves into a refined version of ASTR, extending its applicability to a broader spectrum of algorithms. We introduce a 'Dynamic Stability Field' mechanism to dynamically adjust algorithm states based on input data, thereby enhancing robustness against perturbations. This refinement aims to move beyond a static, limited analysis of stability to a more nuanced understanding of algorithmic behavior, identifying and formally proving inherent stability and resilience.

title: Secure Proof in Non-Asymmetric Trusted Execution Environments (ASEE) Based on Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to security proof within Non-Asymmetric Trusted Execution Environments (ASEE) leveraging Quantum Key Distribution (QKD). The core challenge in ASEE design is establishing trust in the execution of code, often relying on a central trusted party. We introduce a mechanism that utilizes QKD to generate a shared key, which is then employed to securely encrypt the quantum state representing the execution process of the code. Post-execution verification confirms the correctness of the results, followed by decryption using the same key. This process creates a fundamentally verifiable trust foundation, directly addressing the trust issues inherent in traditional ASEE models. The method offers a robust defense against potential attacks by providing a complete audit trail of the code's execution through the quantum key distribution process. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential security advantages of this approach.

We demonstrate the feasibility and potential security advantages of this approach.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Networks for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in Cyber Physical Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to real-time anomaly detection in cyber-physical systems (CPS) utilizing Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs) guided by a reinforcement learning (RL) agent. Traditional Bayesian Networks (BNs) often fail to adapt to the inherent dynamism of CPS environments, leading to inaccurate anomaly detection results. The proposed system addresses this limitation by employing a DBN that continuously updates its structure and parameters, driven by real-time sensor data. A key component is the RL agent, which learns optimal network configurations and inference rules to maximize anomaly detection performance. This adaptive mechanism enables the DBN to effectively respond to evolving system behavior and improve detection accuracy. The core claim of this work is that a dynamically adapting Bayesian Network, guided by reinforcement learning, provides a superior solution compared to static BNs in the context of real-time anomaly detection in CPS.

title: Alashan Ground Squirrel Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Alashan Ground Squirrel Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AGSIMHA), designed to address complex optimization challenges. The algorithm's core inspiration stems from the foraging behavior of the Alashan ground squirrel, a resilient rodent known for its efficient resource utilization and adaptive strategies in a challenging environment. AGSIMHA incorporates elements of exploration and exploitation, mimicking the squirrel's ability to balance searching for new food sources with consolidating established ones. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a squirrel-inspired movement strategy and a novel adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism. Mathematical formulations detailing the algorithm's key components, including the movement probability distribution and the parameter adaptation rules, are presented. The performance of AGSIMHA is evaluated through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's ability to adapt to changing problem landscapes is a key strength. The core of the algorithm relies on a probabilistic movement scheme, represented by the equation: P(si, t+1) = α * (1/N) + (1-α) * exp(-β * ||xi - xbest||2 / σ2), where α is the exploration rate, β is the exploitation rate, N is the population size, xi is the position of the i-th individual, xbest is the best position found so far, and σ is the standard deviation. Parameter adaptation is governed by the equation: Δk = γ * (xi - xbest) / ||xbest||, where γ is the adaptation constant. The algorithm's efficacy is demonstrated through comparative analysis against PSO and AGA.

title: Semantic Web Reasoning with Knowledge Graphs and Deep Semantic Embeddings
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to semantic web reasoning that addresses the limitations of traditional rule-based systems. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of knowledge graphs and deep semantic embeddings to achieve more scalable, flexible, and accurate semantic reasoning. We propose a framework that represents semantic data as a knowledge graph and employs deep learning models to generate semantic embeddings. These embeddings capture the complex relationships within the data, allowing for efficient reasoning and inference. The system's ability to handle large datasets and complex relationships distinguishes it from conventional rule-based approaches. The system is evaluated conceptually, outlining the architecture and key components, and demonstrating its potential for improved semantic web applications. The primary contribution is a hybrid approach that combines the structured knowledge representation of knowledge graphs with the powerful representation learning capabilities of deep semantic embeddings.

title: Title: Topological Space Quantum System Design and Optimization (TS-QS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum system design and optimization, termed Topological Space Quantum System Design and Optimization (TS-QS), which leverages the inherent topological properties of quantum systems to guide parameter optimization and enhance system performance and reliability. Traditional methods often rely on manual parameter tuning, which can be time-consuming and prone to suboptimal solutions. TS-QS offers a fundamentally different perspective, utilizing topological structures to systematically explore parameter spaces and identify configurations exhibiting superior performance characteristics. This paper details the framework, its underlying mechanisms, and demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples.

title: Physical Simulation of Quantum Entanglement Expansion
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement simulation to expand the scope of physical simulation, enabling more precise parameter prediction. Traditional physics simulations often rely on classical computation, while quantum entanglement simulation offers a unique avenue to model complex quantum systems with enhanced precision. We investigate the core mechanisms of this approach, focusing on the implementation of a quantum entanglement simulation to address limitations inherent in current simulation techniques. This paper will detail the theoretical framework underpinning this expansion, outlining the challenges and opportunities involved in translating quantum phenomena into a computational model.

title: Yapay Zekâ Gastronomiyi Dönüştürüyor Mu? Şeflerin Dijitalleşmeye Yönelik Algıları
abstract: Bu araştırmanın amacı, yapay zekâ teknolojilerinin profesyonel mutfaklarda kullanım biçimlerini, şefler tarafından nasıl algılandığını ve gastronomi alanında oluşturduğu dönüşümü değerlendirmektir. Çalışmada, yapay zekânın menü planlama, reçete geliştirme, yeni ürün oluşturma, maliyet hesaplama, stok kontrolü, iş planlaması ve gıda atığını azaltma gibi mutfak süreçlerindeki rolü ele alınmıştır. Nitel araştırma yaklaşımıyla yürütülen çalışmada, profesyonel mutfak deneyimine sahip katılımcılardan elde edilen görüşler tematik analiz yoluyla değerlendirilmiştir. Bulgular, yapay zekânın mutfaklarda özellikle zaman tasarrufu, pratik çözüm üretme, karar verme sürecini kolaylaştırma, hata payını azaltma ve operasyon verimliliğini artırma açısından önemli katkılar sunduğunu göstermektedir. Bununla birlikte katılımcıların yapay zekâya yönelik yaklaşımlarının farklılaştığı; bazı şeflerin bu teknolojiyi destekleyici bir araç olarak benimsediği, bazılarının ise özgünlük, etik, güvenilirlik, mesleki kimlik ve insan dokunuşunun zayıflaması açısından çekinceler taşıdığı belirlenmiştir. Sonuç olarak yapay zekânın gastronomiyi tamamen ikame eden değil, mutfak süreçlerini yeniden yapılandıran tamamlayıcı bir teknoloji olduğu söylenebilir. Bu nedenle yapay zekâ kullanımının şef denetiminde, etik ilkeler doğrultusunda ve mesleki deneyimle desteklenerek sürdürülmesi önem taşımaktadır.

title: Explainable AI-Derived Spatial Pathological Features of Tumor, Necrosis, and Lymphocytes Identify Key Histological Signatures for Residual Cancer Burden Assessment in Breast Cancer
abstract: Background: Conventional histopathological assessment of residual cancer burden (RCB) following neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer relies on manual visual evaluation, lacking objective quantification of spatial interactions among tumor, necrosis, and lymphocyte compartments. This limits prognostic accuracy and impedes personalized treatment stratification. Methods: We developed an explainable AI framework to segment three tissue compartments from H&E patches and constructed 11 spatial pathological features. This two-center study included 347 post-neoadjuvant patients (182 development, 165 external validation) plus 843 TCGA-BRCA cases for exploratory external validation. VGG-16, ResNet-50, and ViT-Base were evaluated; multiple instance learning identified target regions for feature construction. Six machine learning models with LASSO-selected features were interpreted via SHAP and Grad-CAM, with TCGA-BRCA serving as an exploratory external cohort. Results: VGG-16 achieved optimal segmentation (all AUCs > 0.90). In the external validation set, XGBoost achieved AUCs of 0.781 for Task 1 (RCB-0 vs. RCB-1+2+3) and 0.896 for Task 2 (RCB-0+1 vs. RCB-2+3). For Task 3 (RCB-0+1+2 vs. RCB-3), the model achieved an AUC of 1.000, with complete separation between groups. SHAP analysis revealed that the Necrotic Tumor Mixed Cluster (T+N) was the dominant indicator for Task 1 (mean |SHAP| = 0.439) and Task 2 (mean |SHAP| = 0.803), while the Pure Necrotic-Rich Zone (N-only) was the dominant indicator for Task 3 (mean |SHAP| = 1.967). In exploratory TCGA association analyses, the Pure Tumor-Rich Zone (T-only) exhibited a positive correlation (ρ = 0.706, p < 0.001; T-only is a feature used to derive this model-estimated RCB-like score), whereas the Lymphocyte-Infiltrated Necrotic Zone (N+L) showed a negative correlation (ρ = −0.407, p < 0.001) with the model-estimated RCB-like score, linking tumor-rich zones to immunosuppression and lymphocyte-infiltrated necrotic zones to immune activation. Conclusions: Our spatial pathological features effectively estimate RCB, with T+N and N-only as the predominant SHAP-identified indicators across the three tasks. Exploratory analyses further suggest that tumor-rich and lymphocyte-infiltrated necrotic zones correlate with opposing immune phenotypes, supporting personalized breast cancer management.

title: Bayesian Additive Regression Trees for Circular Data: A Machine Learning Framework
abstract: Circular data arise in a wide range of scientific fields, including meteorology, medicine, biology, and neuroscience, yet existing regression methods for such data are largely restricted to parametric generalized linear models or tree-based methods that impose distributional assumptions on the circular response. In this paper, we propose a family of Bayesian Additive Regression Tree (BART) methods for regression with circular data, covering three cases: Circular–Circular BART (CCBART), where both the response and the covariates are circular; Circular–Linear BART (CLBART), where the response is circular and the covariates are linear; and Linear–Circular BART (LCBART), where the response is linear and the covariates are circular. The proposed methods adopt a projection approach, decomposing circular variables into their sine and cosine components, fitting separate BART models on these projections, and recovering circular predictions via the two-argument arctangent function. This avoids specifying a von Mises or wrapped normal likelihood directly for the circular response, though it does not avoid all distributional assumptions: BART assumes flexible Euclidean regression models, with Gaussian errors, for the projected sine and cosine components. The approach retains the full inferential power of BART, including posterior uncertainty quantification, automatic variable selection, and the ability to capture nonlinear effects and interactions without pre-specification. An extensive simulation study demonstrates that the proposed methods are highly competitive with random forest benchmarks and consistently outperform linear model benchmarks, with the clearest and most consistent advantage over random forests emerging at high noise levels and in the Linear–Circular case, where LCBART achieves up to 34% lower RMSE than projected random forests. Applications to wind direction forecasting and human motor resonance data further illustrate the practical utility of the proposed methods.

title: Prabhasa-BabyLM: Matched-Budget Tests of Paninian Structure in Small-Model Pretraining
abstract: Under a fixed pretraining budget, which inductive biases actually improve a small languagemodel, and which only appear to until they are tested against a matched control? Prabhasa-BabyLManswers this for Paninian morphosyntax through a controlled study on the BabyLM 2026 benchmark.Three mechanisms are tested: morpheme-boundary N-hot embeddings, karaka role-stratified masking,and a supervised role-prediction objective. Because Paninian parsers exist for Sanskrit and not for English, the deterministic mapping from Universal Dependencies relations to karaka roles thatsupplies every English label in this work is specified in full, situated against semantic role labelling, and measured for what it loses: only 68.3% of the subword positions the model sees carry the roleits own parse assigned. A 114M-parameter bidirectional encoder is trained on the Strict (100M-word) and Strict-Small (10M-word) budgets and every claim is tested with three to five seeds, pairedbootstrap inference, and Holm–Bonferroni correction. The Strict entry scores 74.56 BLiMP againsta GPT-2 baseline of 74.53 and stands third on the Strict track by Overall Average (45.21) at the timeof writing. The gains are attributable to the training objective, the architecture, the training budget,and completeness of evaluation coverage, not to the Paninian mechanisms. Pure masked languagemodelling is indistinguishable from a hybrid MLM+CLM objective at 10M words but exceeds it by5.49 points at 100M. At matched mask budget, karaka-stratified masking is causally inert, and the karaka auxiliary objective yields only +0.76 points over five seeds. The result is a controlled separationof the design choices that help at this scale from a linguistically motivated prior that does not.

title: A fuzzy inference network with multimodal feature knowledge embedding and its application in medical diagnosis
abstract: A fuzzy radial basis inference network with multimodality prior feature knowledge embedding is proposed for multimodality feature fusion and small sample set classification. This model mainly consists of a multi-channel modal feature input layer, a fuzzy radial basis neuron network (FRBN) layer, a modal category feature aggregation layer, a fuzzy rule layer, and a T-S fuzzy classifier. For the differences in spatiotemporal distribution, information granularity, and semantic representation of different modal features, FRBNs is used to embed multimodality diversity prior category feature knowledge, as well as to process the semantic and spatiotemporal information consistency of input modal features. Based on fuzzy computing logic, inference rules are established and multimodality features are fused layer by layer. Specifically, for classification tasks, high-order semantic features of each modality are extracted separately, and a similarity measurement function for modal features is constructed. Then, the fuzzy dynamic C-means clustering algorithm is used to select representative sample features from subsets of different categories in each modality, in order to implicitly represent prior category knowledge. They are used as the kernel center of FRBN to achieve the embedding of diversity prior feature knowledge. In the modality category feature aggregation layer, the diversity feature information of each modality category subclass is aggregated towards the category and generates a non-convex class interface. Fuzzy multiplication operation is adopted to establish fuzzy reasoning rules for classification tasks, and multimodality classification is implemented based on T-S fuzzy classifier. The proposed method can embed and utilize prior feature knowledge of each modality in a mechanism, impose structural and data constraints on the model, reduce the requirement for the completeness of the sample set, and maintain semantic consistency between modalities and within modalities. Applying the proposed method to medical diagnosis, four types of heart disease classification were performed using multimodality medical data such as echocardiogram, multi-lead electrocardiogram, myocardial enzyme examination, and clinical symptoms, with an accuracy rate of 83.37%. This verifies the effectiveness and application value of the proposed method.

title: Assessing Suicide Risk in Arabic Crisis Helpline Calls: A Comparison of Arabic and English Large Language Models
abstract: Crisis helplines assess suicide risk through structured interviews, a process that is slow and dependent on operator training and workload. Natural language processing could support risk assessment and call prioritization, but almost no work addresses Arabic-language helpline calls or operates within the privacy constraints of real helpline data. We analysed de-identified transcripts from Lebanon's National Lifeline for Emotional Support and Suicide Prevention. Audio never left the helpline: calls were transcribed on site with a speech recognition model for Levantine Arabic, and an Arabic named-entity recognition model removed identifying information locally. Only the de-identified transcripts were shared with the research team. Operators recorded the five suicidal ideation items of the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale, which we combined into two binary outcomes: at-risk and high-risk. We also machine-translated the transcripts into English, giving a paired Arabic/English comparison. On each corpus, we fine-tuned five instruction-tuned large language models alongside six transformer encoder baselines (four Arabic, two English) and evaluated all models on a held-out test set. We included 383 calls: 373 for the at-risk task (52.3% positive) and 297 for the high-risk task (30.0% positive). The best Arabic model reached a macro-F1 of 81.19 and a ROC-AUC of 90.61 on high-risk; the best English model reached 85.00 and 92.59, identifying 88.9% of high-risk calls. In both languages, high-risk calls separated more cleanly than at-risk calls, and translation to English did not reduce the best observed performance. evidence.title: Assessing Suicide Risk in Arabic Crisis Helpline Calls: A Comparison of Arabic and English Large Language Models
evidence.abstract: Crisis helplines assess suicide risk through structured interviews, a process that is slow and dependent on operator training and workload. Natural language processing could support risk assessment and call prioritization, but almost no work addresses Arabic-language helpline calls or operates within the privacy constraints of real helpline data. We analysed de-identified transcripts from Lebanon's National Lifeline for Emotional Support and Suicide Prevention. Audio never left the helpline: calls were transcribed on site with a speech recognition model for Levantine Arabic, and an Arabic named-entity recognition model removed identifying information locally. Only the de-identified transcripts were shared with the research team. Operators recorded the five suicidal ideation items of the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale, which we combined into two binary outcomes: at-risk and high-risk. We also machine-translated the transcripts into English, giving a paired Arabic/English comparison. On each corpus, we fine-tuned five instruction-tuned large language models alongside six transformer encoder baselines (four Arabic, two English) and evaluated all models on a held-out test set. We included 383 calls: 373 for the at-risk task (52.3% positive) and 297 for the high-risk task (30.0% positive). The best Arabic model reached a macro-F1 of 81.19 and a ROC-AUC of 90.61 on high-risk; the best English model reached 85.00 and 92.59, identifying 88.9% of high-risk calls. In both languages, high-risk calls separated more cleanly than at-risk calls, and translation to English did not reduce the best observed performance. Suicide risk can be classified from de-identified Arabic transcripts without sending audio outside the helpline. The high-risk results support further testing as an operator-facing tool; lower-severity ideation proved the harder case.

title: Autonomously Acquiring Robot Manipulation Skills with Language-Driven Quality-Diversity
abstract: Quality-diversity (QD) algorithms have been gaining traction in robot learning, where diverse motion primitive libraries allow robots to adapt zero-shot to constraints at deployment time. However, such methods typically require expert designers to write the success condition, fitness and diversity metrics, and this strongly limits the robot's autonomy. On the other hand, existing LLM-based reward-shaping techniques allow robots to learn autonomously but only output single high-performing solutions, limiting the robot's adaptability. In this paper, we propose an approach designed to output diverse motion primitive archives by autonomously leveraging quality-diversity algorithms, only requiring a free-form description of the task in common language. To address the difficulty of designing relevant fitness and diversity metrics, we propose an autonomous exploration mechanism able to reliably output sets of functionals covering the fitness and behavior descriptor (BD) space. First, we pose policy exploration as a functional design problem, where the functional spaces are lower-dimensional than the full BD and fitness spaces, and propose an LLM-based exploration scheme to sample from these low-dimensional spaces without any task-specific prompts, fine-tuning or expert intervention. We adapt a multi-BD variant of the MAP-Elites success (MES) algorithm, designed to leverage the heterogeneous BD samples. Finally, through experiments based on the genesis simulator, we show that our method effectively generates archives of diverse motion primitives, outperforming classical QD algorithms with inferred and hand-written parametrizations on a set of $4$ robotic manipulation tasks.

title: LOCI: A Locator-Critic with Refinement Loop
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) still struggle on tasks requiring complex visual understanding. We argue that the core issue is not high-level reasoning, but instead failing to locate critical details in the image. Due to this shortcoming, VLMs generate often plausible but incorrect reasoning based on flawed perceptual grounding. To address this, we propose Locator-Critic (LOCI), a training-free framework that decouples visual search from evidence verification. LOCI employs a Locator agent to propose candidate visual evidence and a separate Critic agent to evaluate its relevance and sufficiency. These agents engage in an iterative refinement loop, progressively improving the evidence until it is adequate to answer the given question. This decoupled, self-correcting process yields substantial performance gains, achieving state-of-the-art results on multiple complex visual benchmarks. LOCI improves accuracy for both open-weight models like Qwen3-VL (+12.1 on V*, +5.8 on HR-Bench and +11.2 on VisualProbe-Hard) and proprietary models like Gemini 2.5 Pro (+8.9 on V*, +4.3 on HR-Bench, +4.8 on VisualProbe-Hard).

title: SocialReasonBench: A Video-QA Benchmark for Social Reasoning with Counterfactual Narrative Videos
abstract: Recent advances in Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) have greatly improved video understanding, yet their ability to reason about human-centered social situations remains limited. Existing benchmarks typically rely on videos with a single observed trajectory, making it difficult to determine whether models truly understand social dynamics or merely exploit recurring narrative patterns. We introduce SocialReasonBench, a video multiple-choice QA benchmark for evaluating socially grounded reasoning in scenarios derived from interactive narratives. Built from gameplay videos of Detroit: Become Human, the benchmark leverages branching storylines where player decisions lead to alternative social outcomes that can be checked against the game's own script, flowchart, and recorded branches. We develop a multi-agent curation pipeline that localizes socially meaningful clips, grounds answer labels in game-state signals, and generates theory-guided questions with diagnostic distractors. SocialReasonBench covers seven reasoning dimensions, including intent recognition, emotional empathy, moral dilemma, counterfactual reasoning, and causal antecedent. Experiments on contemporary LMMs show that models perform reasonably well on basic social understanding but struggle with counterfactual and causal reasoning. Further ablation and diagnostic error analyses reveal that models often depend on incomplete modality cues and fall into reasoning traps such as visual shortcuts, highlighting a gap between observable event recognition and deeper reasoning over latent social states.

title: CHASE: How Content Ecosystems Are Reshaped When Ranking Is the Only Target
abstract: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is increasingly used to improve content visibility in LLM-based retrieval systems, yet its population-level effects under repeated optimization remain poorly understood. We introduce Content Homogenization under rAnking Signal Exploitation (CHASE), a controlled simulation framework for studying how content ecosystems are reshaped when creators repeatedly adapt documents to an LLM ranking signal. We use ranking as a proxy for source visibility and validate this abstraction against citations in grounded generated responses, obtaining a rank-citation AUC of 0.853 $\pm$ 0.093 across six domains. CHASE then iterates ranking, feature discrimination, rewriting, and evaluation over 20 rounds across different domains. Quality-ranking alignment decreases in all six domains: from R0 to R20, the change in Spearman's rho ranges from -0.107 to -0.018, with a mean change of -0.068, which means documents closer to the ranking feature profile become less aligned with independently judged document quality over the simulation horizon. A random-target control has shown that it is associated with adaptation toward ranking-derived incentives rather than iterative rewriting alone. The resulting ecosystem dynamics are strongly domain-dependent. Together, these findings show how repeated optimization against a fixed LLM ranking signal can reshape both content populations and the incentives faced by content creators.

title: Strengthening Recursive Constructions for Zero-Error Shannon Capacity
abstract: The exact Shannon capacity is unknown for every odd cycle beyond the five-cycle $C_5$, making odd cycles a central open problem in zero-error information theory. Improving the known lower bounds requires constructing large independent sets in strong powers of these graphs. Recent AI-assisted work has produced a rapid sequence of improvements: building on the construction of Itty et al., Gao developed a recursive product construction for combining structured independent sets, and Buys, Polak, and Zuiddam (BPZ) subsequently strengthened this through a richer recursion framework. We continue this line of AI-assisted exploration and introduce a heterogeneous refinement of these constructions. The central observation is that the usefulness of an intermediate construction depends not only on the size of its current main independent set, but also on the auxiliary structure it carries into subsequent recursion. Consequently, different parts of that auxiliary structure need not use the same independent set, and different occurrences in a recursion need not use the same intermediate representation. We formalize this for Gao's binary product and derive explicit propagation rules showing how heterogeneous choices strengthen the resulting gadget while leaving its current code size unchanged, then extend the principle to the more general BPZ framework, tailoring constructions to the distinct roles they play within the recursion. Applying these refinements to the seven-cycle $C_7$, we obtain an independent set in $C_7^{\boxtimes 500}$ yielding $Θ(C_7)\ge 3.25883262\ldots$, improving the best known lower bound. Beyond the numerical gain, the results illustrate a general principle for recursive zero-error constructions: intermediate structures with the same dimension and current code size can have different downstream value depending on where and how they are used in the recursion.

title: Explainable AI for Adaptive Security in Regulated Environments: A Unified Framework Integrating Federated Risk-Based Authentication and Privacy-Preserving On-Premises LLM Deployment
abstract: Healthcare and public-sector organizations face a compounding security imperative: protecting sensitive personal data against adaptive cyber threats while preserving the operational fluency that practitioners require in time-critical workflows. This paper proposes a unified Explainable AI (XAI) security framework that synthesizes federated learning-enhanced Dynamic Risk-Based Authentication (FL-RBA) with privacy-preserving on-premises Large Language Model (LLM) deployment into a cohesive, compliance-native paradigm. The framework introduces SHAP-based rationale generation to address the interpretability gap inherent in transformer-based authentication scoring, producing audit-ready decision trails that satisfy HIPAA and GDPR requirements. Pilot evidence from a live healthcare deployment demonstrates a 95% high-risk interception rate, 2.5% false-positive rate, and sub-1.2-second decision latency. On-premises LLM integration eliminates all external data transmission while delivering clinical intelligence capabilities comparable to cloud-based alternatives. The unified model provides a replicable blueprint for regulated organizations seeking to operationalize AI without compromising data sovereignty or regulatory alignment.

title: Intelligent Commerce: Impact Of Voice Search on Online Shopping with Reference to Google Assistance Usage
abstract: Abstract The relentless infiltration of artificial intelligence within contemporary retail frameworks has catalysed a monumental paradigm shift, transitioning conventional e-commerce systems into highly fluid environments known as intelligent commerce. This systemic transformation has completely altered how modern consumers locate, evaluate, and purchase products online. This empirical inquiry systematically evaluates the profound behavioural shifts triggered by voice search utilities on user acquisition pathways, focusing specifically on Google Assistant. Leveraging state-of-the-art Natural Language Processing (NLP) models combined with Google’s sprawling, data-rich search ecosystem, Google Assistant fundamentally alters traditional consumer behaviour. It transforms tedious text-based search queries into highly intuitive, conversational, and hands-free interactions across mobile devices and connected smart home environments. Through an empirical assessment of a 50-respondent cohort predominantly comprised of Gen Z consumers and digital-native students, this study explores how operational convenience, transactional velocity, and AI-driven personalized product recommendations minimize cognitive friction during the consumer purchasing journey.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Business: Ransforming Strategy, Innovation, Productivity and Competitive Advantage
abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most influential technologies shaping the future of business. From automated customer service and predictive analytics to generative AI, intelligent decision-making and autonomous business processes, AI is changing how organizations create value, manage resources and compete in domestic and global markets. The rapid development of machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, robotics and generative AI has expanded the role of AI from a specialized technological tool to a strategic business capability. This research paper examines the role of Artificial Intelligence in transforming contemporary business and evaluates its potential impact on the future of organizations. The paper discusses the applications of AI in marketing, finance, human resource management, operations, supply-chain management, customer relationship management, entrepreneurship and strategic decision-making. It also examines the benefits of AI, including increased productivity, cost reduction, personalization, innovation, improved forecasting and faster decision-making. At the same time, the study highlights major challenges such as employment disruption, data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, lack of transparency, ethical concerns, high implementation costs and dependence on technological infrastructure. The study adopts a descriptive and analytical research methodology based primarily on secondary information from academic literature, institutional publications, industry reports and authoritative technology frameworks. The findings indicate that AI is likely to become an important component of business strategy rather than merely an operational technology. However, successful AI adoption will depend on organizational readiness, employee skills, quality data, responsible governance, human oversight and continuous innovation. The paper concludes that the future of business is unlikely to be based on humans versus AI; instead, competitive advantage will increasingly emerge from effective collaboration between human intelligence and artificial intelligence.

title: Quantum Topology Optimization: An Adaptive Optimization Approach
abstract: Quantum Topology Optimization (QTO) is a novel optimization technique based on the principles of quantum topology, offering a promising avenue for addressing complex optimization problems. This paper explores the application of QTO to optimize quantum systems, highlighting its unique capabilities and potential advantages over conventional optimization methods. We present a core mechanism utilizing quantum topology to dynamically adjust system parameters, leading to improved performance. The paper details the methodology, provides a conceptual overview of the underlying physics, and offers a preliminary assessment of the method's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and simulation. The core claim is that QTO provides a more precise and robust optimization approach, particularly for systems exhibiting intricate topological structures.

title: Dynamic Topology Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology learning algorithm designed to automatically learn the topology of a system from data and predict system behavior. Traditional topology learning methods often require manual design of the topology, offering limited automation. Our algorithm leverages neural networks to learn the data's topology and subsequently predicts system behavior based on this learned structure. We propose a framework that streamlines the process, enhancing efficiency and providing a more adaptable approach to topology prediction. This work addresses a key challenge in systems modeling, offering a significant advancement in the field of dynamic topology learning.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate regardless of the distance separating them, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. This paper explores the development of a novel optimization algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance the efficiency and stability of quantum computing. We propose a new approach that utilizes entanglement to facilitate complex computations, potentially unlocking new capabilities in quantum information processing. The core mechanism revolves around designing an algorithm that exploits the unique properties of entangled states to guide the optimization process, leading to improved results and a deeper understanding of quantum entanglement's role in computation. This work investigates both the theoretical foundations of this approach and preliminary experimental investigations into its potential impact.

title: Adaptive Dynamic Self-Adaptation Neural Network Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Dynamic Self-Adaptation Neural Network Optimization algorithm, designed to automate the parameter adjustment process during neural network training. Traditional neural network training relies heavily on manual parameter tuning, which is often a time-consuming and error-prone process. Our proposed algorithm leverages a dynamic self-adaptation mechanism to automatically adjust network parameters, resulting in improved efficiency and potentially enhanced performance. This work addresses the limitations of current training methodologies by introducing a novel approach that prioritizes automated parameter optimization. We present a comprehensive theoretical analysis and illustrative experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this algorithm in optimizing neural network parameters. This offers a significant advancement in the field of neural network training.
