title: Quantum State Adaptive Metric
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Quantum State Adaptive Metric (QSAM) designed to enhance the robustness of algorithms by dynamically adjusting them in response to environmental changes. Quantum states, traditionally viewed as static properties, offer a powerful mechanism for self-adaptation, allowing the metric to continuously re-evaluate performance and adjust parameters. We introduce a system of quantum state transformations and analysis, leveraging the inherent dynamism of quantum systems to provide a robust and adaptive assessment of algorithm performance. The core mechanism centers around quantifying and monitoring the evolution of a quantum state, enabling automated parameter adjustments to maintain optimal performance across varying conditions. This paper explores the potential of QSAM for improving the resilience of various algorithms, particularly those operating in dynamic environments.

title: Non-Local Quantum State Manipulation through Entanglement Tunneling
abstract: Quantum state manipulation represents a significant challenge in quantum computing and communication. Current methods, often reliant on classical communication, restrict the ability to transmit information across distances. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum state manipulation leveraging entanglement tunneling – a mechanism where quantum states instantaneously transfer across distances, circumventing the limitations of local interactions. We detail a "Entanglement Tunneling Protocol" – a meticulously designed algorithm – that demonstrates the potential for instantaneous communication and control over quantum states, fundamentally altering the landscape of information transfer. The paper explores the theoretical foundations, algorithmic implementation, and preliminary experimental validation of this groundbreaking technique. The core claim is that entanglement tunneling offers a pathway towards long-distance quantum communication and control, opening doors to unprecedented capabilities.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology for Quantum State Reconstruction
abstract: Quantum state reconstruction is a fundamental challenge in quantum information processing, particularly when dealing with incomplete measurements. Traditional methods often struggle with large datasets and complex systems. This paper introduces Dynamic Topology for Quantum State Reconstruction (DTQSR), a novel approach leveraging a dynamic topology to intelligently adapt to measurement outcomes, thereby significantly enhancing the reconstruction process. We propose a system that iteratively refines the measurement process, employing a feedback loop driven by a topology optimization algorithm. title: On Information-Theoretic Optimization of Neural Network Connection Weights
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to optimizing neural network connection weights, leveraging concepts from information theory, specifically entropy. The core idea is to utilize the entropy of the connection weights as a metric for evaluating network structure and, subsequently, guide adjustments to improve network performance. We propose a method for quantifying the uncertainty associated with each connection weight, represented mathematically as entropy. This entropy value is then used to drive an optimization process, aiming to reduce uncertainty and ultimately enhance the network's ability to accurately represent and learn from data. The presented framework offers a potentially more robust and data-driven method for neural network optimization compared to traditional gradient-based techniques, particularly in scenarios with limited data or complex network architectures. We demonstrate the theoretical underpinnings and potential benefits of this approach, highlighting its alignment with fundamental information theory principles.

title: Probability Association Graph for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning model based on Probability Association Graphs (PAGs). Traditional reinforcement learning often struggles with effectively capturing the complex relationships between environment states and potential states, hindering learning efficiency and generalization. Our approach leverages the inherent structure of PAGs to reduce the difficulty of learning, especially in environments with intricate dependencies. We propose a framework that dynamically integrates information from the PAG, enabling agents to learn more robust and adaptable policies. The core mechanism focuses on employing a graph-based representation to improve the representation learning process and enhance the model's ability to generalize across diverse scenarios. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach, highlighting its potential for advancing reinforcement learning in challenging environments.

title: Contextualized Quantum Circuit Optimization via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Quantum circuit optimization remains a significant challenge in the development of practical quantum computing. Traditional methods often rely on heuristics or exhaustive searches, which are computationally expensive and may not effectively adapt to the specific characteristics of the quantum data being processed. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging reinforcement learning (RL) to achieve contextualized quantum circuit optimization. The core idea is to train an RL agent to dynamically modify quantum circuits in real-time, guided by a reward function that balances circuit fidelity and execution time. Crucially, the agent incorporates a learned contextual representation of the input data, allowing it to tailor the circuit design to the specific context. We demonstrate the potential of this approach by outlining the key components, the reward function design, and the overall architecture. The potential benefits include improved circuit fidelity, reduced execution time, and the ability to adapt to diverse quantum datasets. This represents a shift from static circuit design to adaptive, context-aware optimization, potentially unlocking the full potential of quantum computation.

title: Recursive Fractal Resonance Network (RFRN)
abstract: This paper introduces the Recursive Fractal Resonance Network (RFRN), a novel self-organizing network architecture designed to leverage fractal patterns for optimized resonance and amplification. The RFRN operates on a meta-algorithm that iteratively generates fractal structures, dynamically adjusting their scale and complexity based on real-time data input. The core claim is that this approach fosters self-organization and optimization through a resonant feedback loop, leading to enhanced network functionality. We analyze the potential of RFRN across various application domains, demonstrating its ability to achieve significant improvements in performance and stability. This work presents a fundamentally new method for network design, moving beyond static architectures towards a dynamically responsive system.

title: Black-eared Rice Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Black-eared Rice Rat Algorithm" (BERRA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the black-eared rice rat (Neotoma megalopora). Rice rats are known for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies, particularly their ability to exploit resources in complex and changing environments. The BERRA algorithm leverages these characteristics to develop a robust and effective solution approach for complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates key elements of rice rat foraging, including resource prioritization, adaptive exploration, and memory-based decision making. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a novel representation of the search space based on resource availability and a dynamic adjustment of exploration and exploitation parameters. The performance of the BERRA algorithm is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive ability compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising tool for tackling diverse optimization challenges. The core mathematical representation of the algorithm is detailed, outlining the key components and their interactions.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of geometric association principles to quantum algorithm design, proposing a novel approach that leverages the inherent relationships within geometric structures to enhance algorithm efficiency and stability. title: Adaptive Kernel Learning via Evolutionary Strategies
abstract: Support Vector Machines (SVMs) are powerful kernel-based classifiers, but their performance is highly sensitive to the choice of kernel function and its associated parameters. Traditional methods for kernel selection involve manual tuning, a time-consuming and often suboptimal process. This paper introduces a novel approach to adaptive kernel learning using evolutionary strategies. The core idea is to directly optimize the kernel function's parameters through an iterative evolutionary algorithm, guided by a differentiable reward function derived from SVM performance. This eliminates the need for manual tuning and allows the algorithm to explore a wider range of kernel configurations. We define a population of kernel functions, each characterized by its parameters, and employ an evolutionary algorithm to select and evolve the best-performing kernels. The algorithm's fitness function is based on the SVM's accuracy on a given dataset. The key contribution lies in the automated kernel learning process and the efficient exploration of the kernel parameter space. This approach offers a potentially significant improvement in SVM performance compared to traditional methods, especially for complex datasets.

title: ## Bershula Mountain Vole: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of a Voles
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bershula Mountain Vole" (BMV), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bershula Mountain Vole ( *Microtus longipes* ). These voles exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources within complex and variable environments. BMV leverages this behavior through a novel combination of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) techniques. The algorithm incorporates elements of the vole's exploratory and exploitation strategies, including a dynamic adaptation of exploration parameters based on environmental changes and a mechanism for prioritizing promising food locations. The performance of BMV is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in tackling challenging optimization tasks. The core of the algorithm lies in the "Terrain Mapping" and "Food Source Prioritization" mechanisms, which mimic the vole's cognitive processes. We demonstrate that BMV achieves competitive results compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, highlighting its potential for real-world applications.

abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly developing field of physics, promises revolutionary insights into the fundamental properties of space and time. This research investigates the application of quantum topology to dynamic geometric transformations, specifically focusing on the design of an algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement and topological structure to achieve controlled geometric reshaping. abstract: This paper explores the application of the Adaptive Resonance Network (ARN) framework to the study of non-linear dynamical systems. Traditional approaches often struggle to accurately model systems exhibiting complex, self-organizing behavior, particularly those where the state is not directly proportional to its input. The core mechanism involves designing an ARN-based framework that allows for the system's state to evolve continuously, driven by its internal dynamics and the interplay of its own state, circumventing the limitations of linear models. The paper details the model's architecture, explores initial implementation and validation through simulation, and discusses the potential implications for modeling diverse complex systems.

title: Dynamic Programming with Quantum-Inspired Exhaustion
abstract: Dynamic programming, a powerful algorithmic technique for solving optimization problems, often faces limitations when dealing with large state spaces, leading to significant memory requirements and computational complexity. This research proposes a novel approach that integrates dynamic programming with quantum-inspired exhaustion techniques. The core idea is to mimic quantum measurement processes—specifically, the concept of probabilistic pruning—to intelligently reduce the search space within a dynamic programming framework. We introduce a method where subtrees are pruned based on estimated probabilities derived from probabilistic sampling, effectively simulating a measurement process that favors regions with higher potential for optimal solutions. This combined approach aims to alleviate the memory bottleneck associated with traditional dynamic programming, offering a more scalable solution for complex optimization problems. The paper details the methodology, explores the underlying principles, and presents a theoretical framework for this integration. The results suggest a significant reduction in computational cost and memory usage compared to standard dynamic programming, demonstrating the viability of this quantum-inspired exhaustion strategy. ---

title: Asian Particolored Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Particolored Bat Algorithm" (PBA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Asian Particolored Bat (Aethomys brandtii). These bats utilize a unique echolocation strategy and a specific movement pattern to navigate complex environments and locate food sources efficiently. The PBA algorithm leverages these principles to address complex optimization problems. The core of the algorithm involves a bat population, each represented by position (s_i) and velocity (v_i) vectors. The bats' movement is governed by a sigmoid function, mimicking the bats' echolocation and response to food concentration. The algorithm employs a global and local search mechanism, with bats dynamically adjusting their velocities based on their individual fitness and the overall population's performance. The convergence criteria are based on both the change in the best solution and the variation within the bat population. The performance of the PBA algorithm is evaluated on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. Key features of the PBA include adaptive parameter control, a robust exploration-exploitation balance, and the ability to handle both continuous and discrete optimization problems. The algorithm's design emphasizes efficiency and adaptability, making it a promising alternative to existing metaheuristic methods.

title: Political Stance Pseudo-Labels for January 8th, 2023 Brazilian Crisis Tweets (BERTimbau)
abstract: This dataset contains political stance pseudo-labels for individual tweets related to the January 8, 2023 attack on the headquarters of Brazil's Three Powers in Brasília. Each tweet was classified independently by a fine-tuned BERTimbau model (`neuralmind/bert-base-portuguese-cased`, macro-F1 = 0.85 on held-out test data), trained on a manually annotated subset (Tweets8JanSPI, ALABARSE et al., 2025) and applied to the full January 8th tweet corpus (raw data from CIBERDEM). Before stance classification, tweets flagged as ironic or sarcastic by an auxiliary BERTimbau-based binary classifier (probability of irony ≥≥ 0.10) were removed from the pool. This decision was made because irony consistently reduces stance-classification precision. Based on internal validation, we adopted an “ignore” strategy rather than flipping the labels. Each row is one tweet, assigned one of three stance labels — a_favor [in favor], contra [against], neutro [neutral] — with the classifier's confidence score. To control noise, we kept only predictions passing per-class confidence thresholds calibrated on a human-labeled validation set (the smallest grid value in {0.90, 0.95, 0.97, 0.99, 0.995} reaching ≥0.90 precision per class, with neutro falling back to the largest grid value since it never reaches that bar): 0.99 for a_favor, 0.95 for contra, 0.995 for neutro. This yields 285,160 high-confidence labeled tweets (27.9% retention over the classified pool). In compliance with the X platform's Terms of Service, which prohibit redistribution of full post content, this repository provides `conversation_id` and predicted labels only, not raw tweet text — the same dehydrated format used by the human-annotated dataset this one derives from (Tweets8JanSPI, https://zenodo.org/records/17555457). Columns - `conversation_id` — X/Twitter conversation (thread) identifier the tweet belongs to, a standard field of the X/Twitter API v2 Tweet object- `predicted_label` — predicted stance (`a favor` / `contra` / `neutro`, kept in Portuguese as produced by the classifier)- `confidence` — classifier confidence for the predicted label (0–1) Class distribution contra = 212,336 (74.5%); neutro = 56,373 (19.8%); a favor = 16,451 (5.8%).

title: Explainable Deep Reinforcement Learning through Concept Inference
abstract: This paper explores the critical need for explainable and robust deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents. Current DRL models often operate as "black boxes," lacking transparency and hindering trust and adaptation in real-world scenarios. We propose a novel framework for incorporating concept inference into DRL, enabling agents to "understand" underlying concepts and leverage this understanding for improved planning and decision-making. Our approach utilizes knowledge graphs to formalize concepts and integrates logical reasoning techniques within the DRL architecture. This allows the agent to not only learn optimal policies but also to reason about the relationships between concepts, leading to enhanced generalization and interpretability. We outline a system architecture and key components, emphasizing the integration of symbolic and connectionist approaches. The core claim of this work is to design a mechanism that allows DRL models to 'understand' concepts, thereby improving their planning and decision-making abilities. The core mechanism relies on the use of knowledge graphs and logical reasoning to formalize concepts and integrate them into the reinforcement learning model. This work contributes to advancing the field by addressing the limitations of current DRL methods and paving the way for more reliable and trustworthy AI systems.

title: Quantum Teleportation Advances: Energy Transfer and 1,400 km Space Tests — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Quantum teleportation transmits quantum *states* (information), not matter or energy; recent experiments extend this to energy teleportation on superconducting hardware and Earth-to-space distances up to 1,400 km. | MATH: Core formalism: Bell-state measurement (BSM) + classical communication (2 bits) + local unitary correction. State transfer fidelity F = |⟨ψ|ρ_out|ψ⟩|²; for ideal teleportation F=1. Energy teleportation (arXiv:2301.02666) uses local operations and classical communication (LOCC) to extract positive energy from a vacuum-like entangled state, quantified by energy density ⟨T₀₀⟩ and conditional entropy S(A|B) = S(ρ_AB) − S(ρ_B). No mass/energy moves — only correlations. | CONNECTION: The 2-bit classical channel per teleported qubit maps to the binary tetrahedral group (order 24) — the symmetry of the F4 lattice root system. The four Bell states correspond to the four cosets of the Pauli group {I, X, Y, Z} modulo phases, which is isomorphic to the Klein four-group V Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: 基于量子态的几何信息编码
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of leveraging quantum states as a geometric information encoding scheme for high-dimensional data compression and transmission. We explore the use of quantum entanglement to enhance data transfer efficiency, proposing a novel approach to represent and manipulate geometric data using quantum properties. The core of our research lies in the design and implementation of a quantum-enhanced geometric representation, focusing on the unique properties of quantum states for efficient data compression and robust transmission. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in compressing and transmitting geometric data, highlighting the potential for significant advancements in data storage and transmission technologies. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

title: ## The Nautilus Algorithm: A Metaheuristic Inspired by Oyster Shell Morphology
abstract: This paper introduces the Nautilus Algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization method inspired by the intricate and adaptive morphology of oyster shells. The algorithm leverages the self-organizing, iterative growth patterns observed in oyster shells, particularly the spiral arrangement of the shell's ridges, to guide the search process. The Nautilus Algorithm employs a multi-dimensional representation of the search space, utilizing a 'shell' structure to encapsulate candidate solutions. The algorithm's core mechanism, termed 'Ridge Propagation,' simulates the growth of shell ridges based on a combination of gradient descent and a stochastic element, mimicking the natural process of shell formation. This approach aims to provide a robust and efficient method for solving complex optimization problems. The paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, key parameters, and a conceptual overview of its operation, highlighting its potential advantages over existing metaheuristic techniques.

title: Andersen's Fruit-eating Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Fruit-eating Bat
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Andersen's Fruit-eating Bat (AFEB), inspired by the foraging behavior of fruit-eating bats. The algorithm mimics the bats' ability to locate fruit through echolocation, utilizing a combination of pulse emission, echo reception, and movement strategies. AFEB employs a population-based search approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. The algorithm's core components include a pulse emission strategy, an echo reception mechanism, and a movement mechanism, all designed to guide the population towards promising regions of the search space. Specifically, the pulse emission rate is dynamically adjusted based on the estimated distance to the target, and the echo reception strength is proportional to the similarity between the received echo and the emitted pulse. Movement is determined by the gradient of the received echo strength. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency. The key contributions of this work are the novel integration of these bat-inspired mechanisms into a cohesive and effective metaheuristic algorithm, and the demonstration of its superior performance compared to established methods. The algorithm's parameters are tuned using a self-adaptive strategy, further enhancing its robustness and adaptability. The ultimate goal is to provide a robust and efficient solution for a variety of complex optimization problems.

title: Quantum State Transformation of Non-Linear Topology
abstract: Quantum state transformation, a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics, offers a powerful framework for manipulating and understanding quantum systems. This paper investigates the application of non-linear topology to quantum state description, proposing a novel method for optimizing quantum states and exploring its potential within quantum information processing, particularly in the context of quantum key distribution. The core mechanism centers around utilizing topological transformations to guide the evolution of quantum states, offering a potential path towards enhanced quantum information processing. The paper discusses the theoretical foundations, implementation details, and preliminary experimental investigations of this approach. We present a model that leverages topological transformations to enhance the fidelity of quantum states and explore its implications for various quantum algorithms. The research highlights the potential of this methodology to significantly impact the development of quantum technologies.

title: ## The Sardine Pacific Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Technique Inspired by Sardine Schooling Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Sardine Pacific Algorithm (SPA), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the complex and adaptive social behavior of Pacific sardine schools. SPA leverages the principles of cohesion, alignment, and avoidance observed in these fish schools to effectively navigate complex search spaces. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic agent population, a weighted cohesion-alignment mechanism, and a novel 'shift' operation mimicking the spatial movement of sardine schools to escape local optima. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, SPA prioritizes maintaining a dense, yet dynamically shifting, population to promote exploration and exploitation simultaneously. The core mechanism, termed the 'Sardine Field', dynamically adjusts the influence of neighboring agents based on their relative position and velocity, contributing to efficient convergence. This paper outlines the theoretical foundations of SPA, details its key components, and presents a conceptual framework for its application to a variety of optimization problems. Future work will focus on implementing SPA and validating its performance through simulations and comparative analysis.

title: Quantum Error Correction Codes for Distributed Databases
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum error correction (QEC) codes to construct a distributed database with enhanced resilience and reliability. Traditional distributed databases face challenges regarding data durability and security due to potential hardware failures and malicious attacks. This work proposes a novel approach where database data is encoded into quantum states utilizing QEC codes. The system employs error detection and correction mechanisms inherent within the chosen QEC code, enabling robust data storage and retrieval, even in the presence of errors. The core claim of this research is to leverage the inherent properties of QEC codes to build a distributed database with fault-tolerance capabilities. The mechanism relies on encoding data into quantum states and leveraging error correction techniques for efficient data management. This approach offers a new paradigm for database systems, potentially improving their reliability, security, and scalability in demanding environments. The system's architecture is designed to minimize the impact of errors, ensuring data integrity and availability. The exploration focuses on the theoretical aspects and potential implementation strategies, highlighting the advantages of this quantum-based approach.

title: Altiplano Grass Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Mus flavicius*
abstract: This paper introduces a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Altiplano Grass Mouse" (AGM), inspired by the foraging strategies of *Mus flavicius*, the Altiplano grass mouse, a rodent species inhabiting the high-altitude grasslands of South America. *Mus flavicius* exhibits remarkable efficiency in locating and exploiting sparse food sources in a challenging environment. AGM leverages this behavior through a combination of adaptive parameter adjustment, a novel search operator mimicking the mouse's probabilistic movement pattern, and a dynamic population management strategy. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around simulating the mouse's tendency to explore promising areas and consolidate around high-value food patches. We demonstrate AGM's efficacy on a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithms (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's simplicity and adaptability make it a promising candidate for various optimization tasks, particularly those involving discrete or combinatorial problems. We present an analysis of AGM's convergence behavior and discuss its potential applications in diverse fields.

title: Red-Crested Finch Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RCFMOA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Red-Crested Finch Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RCFMOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of red-crested finches. The algorithm utilizes a combination of territory defense, mate selection, and resource competition mechanisms to effectively navigate complex search spaces. RCFMOA incorporates a novel 'Dominance Radius' parameter to refine territory boundaries and a 'Proximity Fitness' function to bias mate selection towards solutions with higher overall fitness. The algorithm's core components – territory establishment, defense, mate selection, and resource allocation – are designed to promote exploration and exploitation simultaneously, leading to improved convergence and robustness. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical foundations, operational rules, and potential applications, highlighting its advantages over existing metaheuristic techniques.

title: ## Albertine Rift Brush-furred Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by a Unique Rodent
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Albertine Metaheuristic Optimization (AMO)," designed to address complex optimization problems. The inspiration for AMO stems from the unique foraging behavior and spatial navigation strategies observed in the Albertine Rift Brush-furred Rat (*Neotoma setosa*), a rodent endemic to the Albertine Rift Valley in East Africa. This rat exhibits remarkable adaptability in navigating complex and unpredictable environments, often utilizing a 'scatter-and-search' strategy combined with a robust memory of previously visited locations. AMO leverages these characteristics through a combination of adaptive parameter control, a novel exploration-exploitation balance mechanism, and a dynamic memory representation. The algorithm is formulated using a population-based approach, where individuals represent potential solutions. AMO's core components include a stochastic movement operator, a memory network, and a self-adaptive learning rate mechanism. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AMO through simulations on a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform established metaheuristic algorithms in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's design philosophy prioritizes adaptability and robustness, mimicking the resilience observed in the Albertine Rift Brush-furred Rat.

title: Fractal Information Theory for Quantum State Tomography
abstract: Quantum state tomography (QST) is a fundamental technique for characterizing the state of a quantum system. However, traditional QST protocols often suffer from significant measurement complexity and resource demands, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional quantum states. This work proposes a novel approach to QST that leverages the inherent fractal structure observed in measurement outcomes. We introduce a framework utilizing fractal dimension analysis to guide the acquisition of more efficient and accurate tomography protocols. The core idea is to adaptively refine measurement strategies based on the fractal characteristics revealed in the measurement data. This approach aims to reduce the overall number of measurements required while simultaneously improving the fidelity of the reconstructed quantum state. We demonstrate the theoretical feasibility and potential benefits of this methodology, offering a promising direction for advancing QST techniques.

title: Quantum Reservoir Computing for Time Series Prediction
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum reservoir computing (QRC) to time series prediction. Classical reservoir computing (RC) utilizes a complex, high-dimensional system – the 'reservoir' – as a non-linear feature extractor, followed by a linear regression model for prediction. QRC extends this concept by leveraging the inherent dynamics of a quantum system as the reservoir. We hypothesize that quantum systems, due to their superposition and entanglement properties, can provide richer and more complex dynamics than classical reservoirs, potentially leading to improved prediction accuracy. This work outlines the theoretical framework for QRC, detailing the setup of a suitable quantum reservoir (e.g., a superconducting qubit array), the measurement process, and the training strategy involving a classical machine learning model. We demonstrate a conceptual approach, focusing on the potential advantages and challenges of employing quantum systems for this task. The core claim is that QRC can achieve superior time series prediction accuracy compared to classical RC methods. Key elements explored include the input signal's influence on the quantum reservoir, the selection of appropriate measurement schemes, and the choice of classical learning algorithms. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the potential impact of QRC on various time series prediction applications.

title: 基于量子几何的拓扑变换的量子算法验证
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum geometry to validate quantum algorithms, offering a novel approach to algorithm verification. Traditional methods rely on classical verification, which struggles to fully capture the intricacies of quantum algorithms. We propose a new methodology leveraging quantum geometric models to rigorously assess the correctness and stability of quantum computations. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum geometric representation of the algorithm, and utilizing the inherent properties of quantum geometry – specifically, self-similarity and entanglement – to detect subtle errors and inconsistencies that might be missed by conventional verification techniques. This research aims to provide a robust and efficient method for validating quantum algorithms, addressing limitations of existing approaches.

title: When AI Support Is Removed: Immediate Gains and Delayed Unaided Performance After AI-Supported Learning — A Systematic Review, Evidence Map, and Conditional Meta-analysis. The phrase “Crutch Effect” is a proposed theoretical label and is not treated as an established result.
abstract: This project will identify, appraise, map, and, when scientifically justified, quantitatively synthesize studies in which learners directly use an artificial-intelligence system during structured learning and are later assessed without AI support. The central issue is whether AI-supported learning improves immediate performance but is followed by weaker, attenuated, or reversed delayed unaided performance compared with no-AI or resource/time-matched learning. The review has two linked layers. The broad evidence map will include longitudinal educational and professional-training studies reporting immediate, delayed, retention, transfer, independent-performance, or mechanism outcomes. The primary quantitative synthesis will be restricted to direct withdrawal evidence: direct learner-AI interaction, an appropriate comparator, explicit AI withdrawal or AI-disabled assessment, an objective delayed outcome, and preferably both immediate and delayed AI-free assessments. Studies with a delayed AI-free outcome but no immediate AI-free assessment will be synthesized as Tier B. Mechanistically adjacent studies will be mapped and narratively synthesized as Tier C. Studies reporting only AI-enabled task performance will be classified as Tier D contextual evidence and cannot establish a Crutch Effect. The review will distinguish AI-supported performance, immediate AI-free learning, delayed AI-free independent performance, and transfer or independent professional performance. The primary estimands are the standardized between-group effect at a prespecified delayed AI-free endpoint and, when measurement and timing are comparable, the condition-by-time interaction or difference-in-differences. Immediate AI-enabled performance will be reported separately and will not be interpreted as durable learning. The protocol follows PRISMA-P principles and will be reported using PRISMA 2020, PRISMA-S, and SWiM when pooling is inappropriate. RoB 2 will be used for randomized studies, ROBINS-I for non-randomized comparative studies, and GRADE principles will be applied separately to immediate, delayed, interaction, and transfer outcomes.

The broad evidence map will include longitudinal educational and professional-training studies reporting immediate, delayed, retention, transfer, independent-performance, or mechanism outcomes. The primary quantitative synthesis will be restricted to direct withdrawal evidence: direct learner-AI interaction, an appropriate comparator, explicit AI withdrawal or AI-disabled assessment, an objective delayed outcome, and preferably both immediate and delayed AI-free assessments. Studies with a delayed AI-free outcome but no immediate AI-free assessment will be synthesized as Tier B. Mechanistically adjacent studies will be mapped and narratively synthesized as Tier C. Studies reporting only AI-enabled task performance will be classified as Tier D contextual evidence and cannot establish a Crutch Effect. The review will distinguish AI-supported performance, immediate AI-free learning, delayed AI-free independent performance, and transfer or independent professional performance. The primary estimands are the standardized between-group effect at a prespecified delayed AI-free endpoint and, when measurement and timing are comparable, the condition-by-time interaction or difference-in-differences. Immediate AI-enabled performance will be reported separately and will not be interpreted as durable learning. The protocol follows PRISMA-P principles and will be reported using PRISMA 2020, PRISMA-S, and SWiM when pooling is inappropriate. RoB 2 will be used for randomized studies, ROBINS-I for non-randomized comparative studies, and GRADE principles will be applied separately to immediate, delayed, interaction, and transfer outcomes.

title: AI-driven resolution of uncertain histopathology in cases initially misdiagnosed as triple-negative breast cancer
abstract: Tumors presumed to be metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) may occasionally represent misdiagnoses of primary or metastatic tumors from other origins—particularly lung—due to overlapping clinical characteristics and lack of organ-specific morphological features. While immunohistochemical markers can resolve these discrepancies, they are often underutilized without prior clinical suspicion, leading to significant treatment delays. To address this, we employed GPSai, a tissue-of-origin artificial intelligence (AI) model integrated into routine molecular profiling at Caris Life Sciences, to systematically identify differential diagnoses among 2423 presumed TNBC cases. By integrating AI results with clinical and molecular evidence, we identified a misdiagnosis rate of 3.0%. While over half of these cases were reclassified as non-small cell lung cancer, the misdiagnosis cohort also included various other tumor types. These diagnostic shifts profoundly impact staging, prognosis, and therapeutic selection, highlighting the necessity of an unbiased, systematic approach to identifying misdiagnoses among presumed TNBC.

title: Elite-Weighted Supervised Fine-tuning for Goal-Directed Molecular Optimization
abstract: Goal-directed optimization is essential for steering molecular generators to propose candidates with desired properties. However, it is often implemented with policy-gradient reinforcement learning, which requires a generation-trajectory log-probability whose form depends on the model architecture and generation procedure. This makes an optimizer difficult to reuse across architectures and conditional generative designs. Supervised fine-tuning needs none of that machinery, but its update is driven by a fixed dataset, so the reward never enters the update. We introduce Elite-Weighted Supervised Fine-tuning (EW-SFT), which uses reward to guide elite selection of high-scoring molecules, and updates the model by its own pretraining loss on that set. Ablations show that reward information is passed primarily through elite selection, rather than through continuous weighting within the selected set. Because the update consumes only scored molecules and the model's native loss, the same rule applies across autoregressive, masked-diffusion, and discrete-flow generators, and across de novo, motif-extension, and linker-design tasks. Under a fixed budget of 3D shape alignment oracle calls on two kinase reference compounds, EW-SFT consistently outperforms the corresponding native optimizers. It further improves goal-directed optimization under a 2D similarity oracle on four held-out references and achieves comparable performance on a sample-efficiency benchmark without a trajectory-level RL formulation. These results demonstrate that EW-SFT is a unified and effective optimizer across molecular generators, design constraints, references, and oracles.

title: Different representation learning objectives recover distinct latent structures from the same psychometric data
abstract: Psychometric questionnaires contain rich item-level information, yet it remains unclear whether different representation learning objectives recover the same latent organization. We investigated this question using 757 matched teacher-child pairs from the baseline assessment of the Cyprus ProW preschool trial. Behavioral structure was characterized from child SDQ, ASBI, and CBRS item responses using principal component analysis and clustering, yielding four behavioral phenotypes. A contrastive objective substantially improved teacher-child retrieval relative to PCA-based representations, increasing Top-1 accuracy from 0.13% to 7.27% and Top-10 accuracy from 1.98% to 56.14%. However, contrastive representations preserved behavioral phenotype structure less effectively than PCA-based representations. A multi-task objective jointly optimizing alignment and behavioral prediction partially restored behavioral organization but reduced retrieval performance. These findings indicate that teacher-child correspondence and behavioral phenotypes represent distinct forms of latent organization and demonstrate that the latent structure recovered from linked psychometric data depends on the representation learning objective.

title: SegWave: Wavelet-Driven Segmentation of Tampered Regions
abstract: Verifying image authenticity is increasingly difficult, posing serious risks across journalism, law enforcement, and political domains. Most existing forensic methods rely on high-level visual artifacts and treat frame detection as a simple binary task. To address this, we propose SegWave, a hybrid framework that jointly leverages spatial and frequency-domain cues for image tampering detection. SegWave integrates a transformer-based architecture with the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to capture localized, multi-scale frequency inconsistencies indicative of manipulation. To further improve localization effectiveness, we introduce an Adaptive Sub-band Attention module (ASA) that dynamically highlights the informative high-frequency wavelet components. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that SegWave consistently outperforms state-of-the-art tampering detection methods in challenging evaluation settings.

title: Dec-BFTRL: Squre-Root Regret for Decentralized Online Upper-Linearizable Optimization under Separation Access with Application to Continuous Submodular Maximization
abstract: We study decentralized online optimization of upper-linearizable payoffs over an action set under efficient separation access, with applications to online continuous diminishing-return (DR) submodular maximization. We propose Decentralized Barrier Follow-the-Regularized-Leader (Dec-BFTRL), and evaluate each agent's played action against the average of all local objectives. Each agent maps an internal iterate to a feasible action through an approximate gauge projection, communicates only a cumulative surrogate-gradient dual state, and invokes the local HybridNewton procedure to approximately minimize its post-communication BFTRL potential. For every agent, we achieve expected network-aggregate regret of $\widetilde O(\sqrt{T})$. Over $T$ rounds, each agent uses $T$ neighbor-mixing steps and $\widetilde O(T)$ separation-oracle calls. We give wrapper instantiations covering four up-concave or DR-submodular maximization problems.

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Credit Card Fraud Detection in E-Commerce
abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce and electronic payment services has increased the convenience of digital transactions while also creating more opportunities for fraudulent activity. Conventional fraud detection approaches based on manual review and fixed rules can struggle with large transaction volumes, changing fraud patterns, and false-positive alerts. This study comparatively evaluates four supervised machine learning algorithms-Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) for credit card fraud detection. The study used a labelled transaction dataset and followed an iterative Agile-based development process involving data preparation, model training, testing, and performance evaluation. The models were assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), and training time. The reported experimental results show that Logistic Regression achieved the highest accuracy (63.33%), precision (67.61%), and ROC-AUC (0.6855), while KNN produced the highest recall (67.50%) and F1-score (0.6506). SVM produced moderate results but required the longest training time of 0.0345 seconds. Decision Tree had the shortest training time at 0.0058 seconds but recorded the weakest overall predictive performance, including 54.00% accuracy and 40.00% recall. The findings demonstrate that model selection for fraud detection should not be based on accuracy alone because missing fraudulent transactions can have serious financial and operational consequences. Logistic Regression provided the strongest overall balance among the evaluated models, although the moderate performance of all four algorithms indicates that larger and more representative datasets, improved feature engineering, class-imbalance treatment, and hyperparameter optimization are required before practical deployment.

title: Sistem Pakar Mendiagnosa Kerusakan Kamera Mirrorless Sony Tipe A6000 Menggunakan Metode Certainty Factor
abstract: Kamera mirrorless Sony tipe A6000 merupakan salah satu produk kamera populer yang banyak digunakan oleh para fotografer. Namun, seperti perangkat elektronik lainnya, kamera ini tidak lepas dari kemungkinan mengalami kerusakan. Untuk mendiagnosis kerusakan secara akurat dan efisien, diperlukan sebuah sistem pakar yang dapat membantu dalam proses identifikasi masalah. Penelitian ini mengusulkan pengembangan sebuah sistem pakar untuk mendiagnosis kerusakan pada kamera mirrorless Sony tipe A6000 dengan menggunakan metode Certainty Factor (CF). Metode CF dipilih karena kemampuannya dalam menangani ketidakpastian dan memberikan nilai keyakinan terhadap suatu hipotesis atau kesimpulan. Sistem pakar ini dirancang dengan membangun basis pengetahuan yang mencakup gejala-gejala kerusakan dan aturan-aturan pengambilan keputusan. Sistem pakar yang dikembangkan mampu mendiagnosis kerusakan pada kamera mirrorless Sony tipe A6000 dengan akurasi yang tinggi. Metode Certainty Factor terbukti efektif dalam mengombinasikan bukti-bukti dan memberikan nilai keyakinan terhadap setiap kemungkinan kerusakan. Sistem ini membantu para pengguna kamera dalam mengidentifikasi masalah secara cepat dan tepat, sehingga memudahkan proses perbaikan atau penggantian komponen yang rusak. Selain itu, sistem pakar ini juga dapat digunakan sebagai alat bantu dalam pelatihan dan pendidikan terkait perbaikan kamera

title: Impact of AI-Powered Personalization in Influencing Consumer Purchase Intention and Brand Loyalty
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered personalization is transforming online retail by tailoring product recommendations, promotional messages, search results, and customer interactions to individual preferences. This study examines the impact of AI-powered personalization on consumers' purchase intention and brand loyalty among online shoppers. A descriptive and quantitative research design is proposed, using a structured questionnaire and a five-point Likert scale. Following the structure of the supplied model paper, an illustrative sample of 200 respondents is used for the model analysis. Descriptive statistics, Chi-square, and one-way ANOVA are applied. The illustrative results indicate a significant association between exposure to AI-powered recommendations and purchase intention, as well as significant differences in brand loyalty across levels of perceived personalization. The study suggests that retailers should improve recommendation relevance, provide transparent personalization, protect consumer data, and combine AI-enabled service with human support. The paper concludes that responsible AI personalization can strengthen purchase intention and brand loyalty when consumers perceive the experience as useful, accurate, convenient, and trustworthy.

title: Dimension Decomposition Quantum Computing Framework – Based on Spin Quantum Entanglement Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computing framework, termed the Dimension Decomposition Quantum Computing Framework, centered around the application of spin quantum entanglement. We propose a new optimization algorithm specifically designed to leverage this entanglement, aiming to significantly enhance the efficiency of quantum algorithms. The core concept of this framework is the integration of spin entanglement into the optimization process, which is expected to yield improved results and potentially enable novel quantum computations. This work presents a preliminary design of the framework and explores its potential for advancing quantum computing.

title: Graph-Based Semantic Relation Extraction
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to semantic relation extraction leveraging graph embedding techniques. Traditional relation extraction methods often suffer from limitations such as reliance on manually annotated data, the need for complex rule-based systems, and inherent subjectivity. This research proposes a method that transforms graph structures into continuous vector representations (graph embeddings) and utilizes these embeddings for relation extraction. The core claim is that this approach significantly enhances both the accuracy and efficiency of relation extraction. We explore various graph embedding models and demonstrate their effectiveness in capturing semantic relationships within graphs. The presented method offers a more scalable and potentially more accurate alternative to existing approaches, addressing the shortcomings of previous methods. This work lays the foundation for further research into utilizing graph embeddings for diverse semantic understanding tasks.

title: Title: Quantum Complexity Theory for Constraint Programming
abstract: Quantum Complexity Theory (QCT) offers a promising avenue for enhancing constraint programming by leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum computation. This paper explores the potential of QCT to provide a more robust and nuanced understanding of problem complexity, specifically focusing on the identification of crucial quantum algorithms and their corresponding impact on constraint programming. We propose a novel approach centered around a fundamental relationship between problem complexity and quantum computational resources, aiming to move beyond traditional complexity measures and demonstrate a deeper connection between the problem and the underlying quantum hardware. This work presents a framework for analyzing constraint programming problems using quantum algorithms, ultimately leading to a significant improvement in understanding the limitations and potential of constraint programming. The core mechanism involves a systematic investigation of quantum algorithms applicable to complex constraint programming scenarios, aiming to identify key factors driving complexity.

title: ##基于神经符号人工智能的知识推理引擎
abstract: This paper proposes a novel knowledge reasoning engine that integrates the strengths of neural computation and symbolic reasoning. The core claim is to construct a system capable of autonomously learning knowledge and performing logical inference. This engine leverages neural networks to learn knowledge representations and inference rules, and combines them with traditional symbolic reasoning algorithms. The system aims to overcome the limitations of purely neural or purely symbolic approaches by capitalizing on the representational power of neural networks and the precise reasoning capabilities of symbolic methods. The resulting engine demonstrates improved adaptability and robustness in knowledge-intensive tasks. This work presents a foundational architecture for building intelligent systems that can effectively reason and learn from complex, uncertain data.

title: 自适应量子计算的混沌控制
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum computation utilizing adaptive chaos control. Traditional chaos control methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the potential for optimized performance. We propose a system that employs machine learning to dynamically adjust the parameters of a chaotic control algorithm, resulting in improved stability and efficiency. The core mechanism involves learning a mapping between quantum state evolution and control parameters, enabling automated optimization of the chaos control process. The paper details the design of the adaptive control strategy, its implementation, and the resulting performance improvements observed through simulations. We demonstrate that this approach offers a significant advancement over traditional methods, addressing the limitations of fixed-parameter chaos control.

title: Adaptive Meta-Learning via Differential Evolution of Logical Programs
abstract: Meta-learning aims to enable rapid adaptation to new tasks with minimal training data. Traditional meta-learning approaches often rely on optimizing the parameters of complex models, such as neural networks. However, this approach can lead to black-box models that are difficult to interpret and may not generalize effectively across diverse task distributions. This work proposes a novel adaptive meta-learning framework that utilizes differential evolution to directly evolve the structure of logical programs. Specifically, we employ a differential evolution algorithm to optimize a symbolic logical program, representing the meta-learning strategy. The fitness function is defined based on the performance of the evolved logical program on a variety of tasks. This approach offers several advantages, including increased interpretability, potentially more efficient learning, and improved generalization capabilities. The core claim is that evolving logical program structures, rather than solely network weights, can significantly improve meta-learning. The key mechanism involves directly optimizing a symbolic logical program. This research represents a shift from gradient-based optimization of neural networks to a more explicit and potentially more efficient learning process using symbolic logic.

title: Neural Network Dynamics: Topological Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network learning centered around dynamic topological structures. The core idea is to construct a neural network with locally adaptive synaptic plasticity and a dynamically evolving topology, enabling continuous learning and adaptation to complex, non-static environments without explicit structural specification. The methodology integrates adaptive synaptic plasticity, topological evolution rules, and fine-grained neuronal state encoding. Adaptive synaptic plasticity adjusts synaptic weights based on local neuronal activity, strengthening important connections and suppressing irrelevant ones. Topological evolution rules dynamically modify connection strengths based on information transmission efficiency and local activity patterns, altering the network's topology. Fine-grained neuronal state encoding captures richer temporal information, enhancing neuronal dependencies. This dynamic topological learning mechanism contrasts significantly with traditional static neural networks and rule-based reinforcement learning, offering a potential pathway to building more intelligent and robust systems. ---

title: Bearcat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bearcat Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bearcat, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Bearcats ( *Melogale moschata*). Bearcats are known for their strategic approach to food gathering, utilizing a combination of systematic searching and opportunistic exploitation. Bearcat leverages these behaviors through a novel search operator and a dynamically adjusted adaptive inertia weight mechanism. The algorithm's core components include a position representation, a global best position, and a local best position. The primary innovation lies in the "Pounce" operator, which mimics the Bearcat's sudden shifts in direction when encountering a promising food source. Furthermore, the algorithm incorporates a dynamically adjusted inertia weight scheme based on the distance between the current position and the global best position. We evaluate Bearcat on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Experimental results show that Bearcat exhibits robust performance across diverse problem landscapes, indicating its potential applicability in various real-world optimization scenarios. The key performance metrics considered are convergence speed and solution quality.

title: Geometric Complexity Metric for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric complexity metric designed to enhance the training and evaluation of machine learning models. Traditional metrics often focus on surface area or volume, neglecting the fundamental geometric properties of data points. We propose a new metric that quantifies the complexity of data points – the arrangement of edges, angles, and curves – and utilizes this measure to guide model learning, potentially improving accuracy and interpretability. The core mechanism involves calculating a "complexity score" for each data point, which is then incorporated into the model's optimization process. This approach aims to capture subtle patterns and relationships within the data that may be missed by conventional metrics. The paper details the metric's construction, demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discusses potential future directions for research.

title: Quantum-Inspired Bayesian Inference for Causal Discovery
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal discovery leveraging principles inspired by quantum mechanics. Traditional Bayesian network learning methods often struggle with the vastness of possible causal structures, leading to computational bottlenecks and potentially inaccurate results. We propose a framework that incorporates probabilistic amplitudes, analogous to quantum superposition, to represent and explore multiple potential causal pathways concurrently. This "quantum-inspired" Bayesian inference aims to significantly enhance the exploration process, ultimately leading to improved accuracy in identifying causal relationships within observational data. The core idea is that by allowing for multiple potential pathways to be actively explored simultaneously, we can overcome the limitations of classical methods that typically rely on sequential searching. This approach is evaluated conceptually, outlining the key components and anticipated benefits. The paper focuses on the theoretical underpinnings and the potential impact of this methodology, paving the way for future research and development.

title: Dynamic Symbolic Representation Learning via Iterative Refinement
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to symbolic representation learning, termed Dynamic Symbolic Representation Learning via Iterative Refinement (DSRL-IR). The core idea is to develop a system that learns symbolic representations directly from raw sensory data through an iterative refinement process. Unlike traditional symbolic mapping techniques that often rely on fixed, pre-defined mappings, our system employs a recurrent neural network with a differentiable symbolic layer. This layer iteratively updates a latent representation based on feedback signals that assess the 'correctness' of the generated symbolic output. The system mimics the human conceptual development process, where initial, imprecise understandings are gradually refined through experience and feedback. We propose a framework that allows the system to learn increasingly complex symbolic representations, demonstrating the potential for creating intelligent agents capable of understanding and interacting with the world in a more human-like manner. The key contribution lies in the dynamic, embodied learning process, which contrasts with static symbolic mapping. This approach utilizes a core equation to represent the iterative refinement process: *Rt+1 = f(Rt, St+1)* Where: * *Rt+1* represents the refined latent representation at time step *t+1*. * *Rt* represents the latent representation at time step *t*. * *St+1* represents the feedback signal at time step *t+1*, indicating the correctness of the symbolic output. * *f* represents the iterative refinement function, typically a recurrent neural network. The system is evaluated through simulated environments, showcasing its ability to learn and represent complex relationships between sensory data and symbolic concepts. Future research directions include exploring different feedback mechanisms and integrating this approach with other learning paradigms.

title: Back-striped Weasel: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Agile Movement of a Back-striped Weasel
abstract: This paper introduces Back-striped Weasel (BSW), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the unique and agile movement patterns observed in back-striped weasels (Mustela strigidorsa). BSW leverages a combination of adaptive step-size control, a novel mutation operator mimicking the weasel's directional shifts, and a dynamic population management strategy to explore the search space effectively. The algorithm's core mechanism, the "Stride Adjustment," simulates the weasel's ability to rapidly alter its movement direction based on environmental feedback. We demonstrate the efficacy of BSW through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising candidate for a wide range of optimization challenges. Key performance metrics including convergence speed, solution quality, and computational efficiency are analyzed. Future research directions include incorporating environmental modeling and extending the algorithm to handle multi-objective optimization.

title: Adaptive Dynamic Programming Algorithm for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, but its application is often hindered by the "curse of dimensionality," specifically the state space explosion problem. Traditional dynamic programming methods, while theoretically sound for solving Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), struggle with large state spaces due to the exponential growth of the value function computation. This paper proposes an Adaptive Dynamic Programming Algorithm for Reinforcement Learning (ADP-RL), designed to mitigate this issue. ADP-RL dynamically adjusts the parameters of the dynamic programming algorithm based on the observed dynamics of the environment, effectively reducing computational complexity. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that monitors the convergence rate of the value function approximation and modifies parameters accordingly. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ADP-RL through a theoretical analysis and a simplified numerical example, highlighting its ability to handle complex environments more efficiently than standard dynamic programming approaches. The key innovation lies in the adaptive nature of the algorithm, offering a practical solution for scaling dynamic programming to real-world RL problems.

title: ## The Bioluminescent Navigation Algorithm (BLNA): A Metaheuristic Inspired by Blue Dragonfish Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Bioluminescent Navigation Algorithm (BLNA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique navigation strategies employed by blue dragonfish ( *Cynoglossus mola*) in the deep ocean. These fish utilize a sophisticated bioluminescent communication system to navigate and locate prey in dark environments. BLNA leverages concepts such as 'beaconing' (localized bioluminescence), 'gradient following' (movement towards brighter signals), and 'group cohesion' (collective movement) to achieve efficient global optimization. The algorithm operates within a search space, representing potential solutions, and iteratively adjusts these solutions based on a dynamically updated 'illumination' metric, mimicking the dragonfish's bioluminescent signals. We outline the core principles, mathematical formulation, and key components of BLNA, demonstrating its potential applicability across a range of optimization problems.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Resource Allocation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to the problem of resource allocation. Traditional resource allocation methods often struggle with complex scenarios involving multiple agents with varying priorities and constraints. MARL offers a promising approach by allowing agents to learn optimal allocation strategies through interaction and competition. This work proposes a framework utilizing multiple reinforcement learning agents to dynamically manage and distribute resources. The core claim is that MARL can achieve optimized resource allocation and enhanced fairness compared to traditional centralized approaches. The core mechanism involves constructing a multi-agent system where agents cooperate and compete to maximize their individual rewards while considering the overall system performance. The system learns through trial and error, adapting to changing conditions and agent behaviors. We present a detailed formulation of the problem, outlining the key components of the MARL system including agent representation, reward functions, and the learning algorithm. The potential benefits of this approach, particularly in dynamic and uncertain environments, are discussed, highlighting the adaptability and scalability of MARL for complex resource management challenges. ---

title: ## Black Coral-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BCMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Black Coral-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BCMOA), a novel optimization technique inspired by the growth patterns and resilience of black corals. Black corals, known for their intricate, branching structures formed over extended periods, exhibit a fascinating balance between exploration and exploitation. BCMOA leverages this biological principle to construct a search space and iteratively refine solutions. The algorithm incorporates three key mechanisms: a branching strategy mimicking coral growth, a resilience factor reflecting the coral's ability to withstand environmental pressures, and a dynamic adjustment of the branching probability based on solution quality. The core of BCMOA lies in a probabilistic branching process that generates new candidate solutions by creating branches from existing ones, with the branching probability influenced by the solution's fitness and a dynamically adjusted resilience factor. This approach aims to create a robust search process, adaptable to complex and multi-dimensional optimization problems. The algorithm's effectiveness in representing the complex, hierarchical structure of black coral formations translates to a powerful tool for tackling challenging optimization landscapes.

abstract: This paper proposes a novel hierarchical graph attention network (HGAT) architecture designed to effectively analyze multi-scale data. The core mechanism involves a staged approach, where information is progressively refined through successive attention layers. This results in richer and more robust representations, ultimately improving the network's ability to model complex data structures. The HGAT is evaluated conceptually, outlining its potential applications and demonstrating its advantages over single-scale GATs.

The proposed HGAT addresses this limitation by incorporating a hierarchical representation scheme, utilizing multiple layers of graph attention operating at different levels of granularity. Lower layers focus on identifying local patterns and relationships, while higher layers capture long-range dependencies and global context. The core mechanism involves a staged approach, where information is progressively refined through successive attention layers. This results in richer and more robust representations, ultimately improving the network's ability to model complex data structures. The HGAT is evaluated conceptually, outlining its potential applications and demonstrating its advantages over single-scale GATs.

title: Graph-Based Semantic Memory Retrieval using Contextual Embeddings
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to semantic memory retrieval leveraging graph-based representation and contextual embeddings. Traditional methods for representing and retrieving semantic knowledge often struggle with capturing nuanced relationships and contextual dependencies. Our approach constructs a graph where nodes represent concepts and edges represent semantic relationships extracted from textual data. Crucially, we utilize contextual embeddings, such as BERT, to generate rich vector representations for both nodes and edges. This allows for similarity comparisons and efficient graph traversal, significantly improving the accuracy and granularity of memory retrieval compared to conventional methods. The core claim is that representing semantic relationships as a graph, combined with contextual embeddings, provides a more accurate and nuanced retrieval system. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a theoretical framework, outlining the key components and their interactions. The presented system offers a scalable solution for knowledge representation and retrieval, particularly in scenarios where contextual understanding is paramount.

title: Geometry Topology Structure Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Geometry Topology Structure Optimization, designed to address complex optimization problems by dynamically adjusting geometric topology. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with evolving topological structures, necessitating complex and computationally intensive adjustments. Our algorithm leverages the inherent properties of geometric topology to iteratively refine the problem space, leading to more accurate and robust solutions. We detail the core mechanism, outlining how the algorithm analyzes the topological landscape and intelligently modifies it to guide the search process. The paper provides a comprehensive explanation of the algorithm's design, including the mathematical framework underpinning its operations and its potential impact on various optimization scenarios.

title: Title: Hierarchical Quantum State Representation - Improved Quantum State Learning
abstract: Quantum state representation is a fundamental challenge in quantum machine learning, demanding efficient learning and generalization due to the inherent complexity of quantum systems. This paper introduces a novel hierarchical representation for quantum states, designed to address these challenges. We propose a system of nested levels of abstraction, allowing for the explicit modeling of correlations and patterns across different scales of quantum information. This allows for the learning of complex quantum states that are difficult to capture with traditional methods. The hierarchical structure facilitates the discovery of subtle correlations and patterns that are critical for successful quantum machine learning. This work offers a fundamentally new approach to quantum state learning, promising improved efficiency and generalization capabilities.

title: ## The Giant Tortoise-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (GTSA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Giant Tortoise-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (GTSA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the navigational strategies and foraging behaviors of giant tortoises. The algorithm leverages the tortoise's ability to maintain a consistent direction, adapt to environmental changes, and selectively adjust its pace based on resource availability. GTSA employs a multi-faceted approach combining a directional movement strategy, a dynamic adaptation mechanism, and a resource-based pacing system. The core of the algorithm lies in a novel 'Orientation Vector' representation of the search space, coupled with a 'Terrain Map' that dynamically adjusts based on exploration progress. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, demonstrating its potential for efficiently exploring complex search landscapes. title: Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Cognitive Constraints
abstract: Symbolic regression is a powerful technique for automatically discovering mathematical equations from data. However, its performance is often limited when dealing with complex, hierarchical systems, and it frequently produces equations that are difficult to interpret. This paper introduces a novel approach, Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Cognitive Constraints, which addresses these limitations. The core idea is to decompose the problem into a hierarchy of simpler sub-problems, enabling the algorithm to tackle complex systems more effectively. Crucially, we incorporate cognitive constraints – derived from known physical laws or human intuition – to guide the regression process, ensuring that generated equations are both accurate and meaningful. The resulting system demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy and interpretability compared to standard symbolic regression methods, offering a more robust and human-aligned approach to equation discovery. The primary mathematical framework utilizes a tree-based symbolic representation and a constraint satisfaction algorithm operating on this hierarchical structure. The key innovations lie in the hierarchical decomposition strategy and the explicit incorporation of cognitive constraints to prune the search space and favor physically plausible solutions. Experiments (simulated, due to the absence of real-world datasets for this theoretical exploration) demonstrate the efficacy of this approach across various problem domains, highlighting its potential for applications in scientific discovery and engineering design.

title: ## White Heron Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (WHIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the White Heron Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (WHIMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of white herons. The algorithm mimics the heron's characteristic of scanning the environment, prioritizing promising areas, and adjusting its search strategy based on feedback. WHIMO utilizes a multi-layered scanning mechanism, a dynamic priority system, and a localized adjustment strategy to effectively explore and exploit the search space. The algorithm's core components include a scanning range, a priority evaluation function, and a movement strategy. Unlike traditional metaheuristic methods, WHIMO emphasizes adaptability and localized refinement, leading to potentially faster convergence and improved solution quality. This paper presents a detailed description of the algorithm, its underlying principles, and its potential applications.
